name: The Grove of Woe Incident
title: How a Wedding Invitation Fractured a Party Across Two Planes and Bowser Beat a Man Nearly to Death Over Identity Theft
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadeward Operations / Post-Planar Fracture
location: Raventree Manor Interior / Tymnas's Lodge / The Fracture Grove / The Midnight Portal / The Fracture Atrium / Corvinarus Sanctum
type: Tactical Catastrophe / Forced Party Split / Involuntary Matrimonial Summons / Identity Violence / Dimensional Stranding
status: Ongoing — Party Fractured Across Multiple Planes — Situation Critical — Wedding Still Scheduled
imageCaption: No photographs survive. Bowser destroyed the camera he was carrying when he fell through the portal. The wedding invitation disintegrated at sunrise, as promised in the fine print that nobody read carefully enough.

summary: In the span of approximately four days, the Raventree expedition experienced the following sequence of disasters: Markop locked the tanuki prisoner — the same tanuki from the Birthday Trap incident, the shapeshifter who had impersonated Toadburt and was freed into a bathroom over Remi's furious objections — in a room, Green T handed Remi a Bros Attack instruction sheet and taught her a cooperative fire technique, Remi immediately used this technique to shoot the tanuki through the barricaded door on her SECOND firearms offense, Markop healed the tanuki and confiscated the weapon while delivering a three-point moral argument that Waluigi considers the most surgically precise ethical takedown he has ever documented, a guard delivered an ornate wedding invitation announcing Remi's involuntary betrothal to Lord Malachar Voss of the Sunless Keep, Markop responded by physically carrying Remi out of the building like luggage, the party attempted stealth by SINGING, Markop silenced them by putting his hand over Remi's mouth, they reached the lodge of a groundskeeper named Tymnas who possessed the siglet they needed but had lost his scythe to an entity called the Scorncrow, Markop was kidnapped into the grove by a female entity who stole his axe, Bowser commandeered Salam as a literal surfboard and marched into the wilderness, Remi led the remnants toward the Tree of Woe, Bowser engaged in a tug-of-war with a Mazebound using a one-armed Dan as the rope, Bowser then fell through a midnight portal into an extradimensional sanctum where he encountered the ORIGINAL Dan — a Mages' Guild fire mage connected to Archie Miser — and beat him nearly to death with a warhammer and Bullet Bill cannon, discovered a photograph linking Dan to Archie's operations, found a Bowser Badge fused to Dan's skin that triggered full-body immolation when removed, and is now stranded in a collapsing library with Orange T and Bones while the rest of the party is scattered across the Shadowfell with no healer, no plan, and a vampire wedding approaching. The Oracle is somewhere in the Fracture Atrium. A month has passed in the Shadowfell since the planar fracture. Time is not synchronized. Nothing is synchronized. WAH.
description:
Waluigi has assembled this account from field reports, intercepted communication fragments, Bowser's own retelling — which required approximately sixty percent deflation to reach plausible truth — and the testimony of several Toads who witnessed portions of the events and remain, by all accounts, traumatized. The events described here represent one of the most comprehensive tactical disintegrations Waluigi has ever documented. Not because the enemy was overwhelming. Not because the mission parameters changed beyond recognition. But because the party's own decision-making degenerated into a cascade of impulse, stubbornness, misplaced confidence, and the particular chemistry of people who care about each other but cannot agree on what caring MEANS.

Waluigi would like to state for the record: this is what happens when you put a teenager with a gun and a history of shooting people she shouldn't, a centaur healer with a savior complex and the patience of a saint being slowly ground into dust, a king with abandonment issues and more combat capability than emotional regulation, a former crime lord who thinks assassination is mentorship, and a collection of Toads who believe singing solves problems into a hostile supernatural environment and tell them to 'figure it out.'

They figured it out. They figured out how to make everything worse in ways that will take MONTHS to untangle — assuming anyone survives to do the untangling.

## Context: The Birthday Trap Aftermath and the Tanuki Problem

The events documented here are a DIRECT CONTINUATION of the Birthday Trap incident. Readers unfamiliar with that incident should consult the relevant article, but Waluigi will provide the essential context because this context is the FUEL for everything that followed.

Vostolas the Archivist organized a surprise birthday party for Remi involving caged Toads, a tanuki disguised as Toadburt, a cursed cake designed to place her permanently under Onyx Hand control, and a trapdoor. The party identified the trap before Remi entered, extracted the fake Toadburt, exposed him as a tanuki, debated whether to kill him, accidentally shot Eager in the process, considered slavery as a compromise position, watched democracy collapse entirely, freed the tanuki into a bathroom over Remi's furious objections, and then Remi was angry that she did not get to cast what she believed should have been the deciding vote on whether to execute the prisoner.

The key dynamics from that incident:

Green T wanted execution. Operational security. Loose ends. The logic of a crime lord who has survived by not leaving witnesses. He handed Remi a silenced revolver, told her she needed to be stronger, and framed execution as education.

Remi was willing to execute. She pressed a loaded revolver against the tanuki's head and pulled the trigger before Markop intervened — pulling the gun upward at the same moment Eager bumped into Markop, causing the bullet to graze Eager instead.

Markop wanted mercy. He delivered the devastating moral argument: 'Remi, three people have betrayed you. You didn't shoot them.' He identified that Remi was not shooting traitors — she was shooting people she COULD shoot.

Bowser drew a line. He objected when Green T armed Remi. He punched Remi to stop her from firing. He said: 'That's brutal, even for me.' Then he voted to kill but ALLOWED mercy because Hjumpik would have wanted mercy. The gap between wanting and allowing is where character lives.

The tanuki was freed into a bathroom. Markop untied him and let him go.

Remi was furious. Not about the outcome — about the process. She wanted to VOTE. She wanted her vote to COUNT. The vote she wanted to cast was to kill the prisoner.

This is the emotional context. A party that had just argued about killing a tied-up shapeshifter, accidentally shot one of their own members, and released a prisoner over the objections of their youngest member who wanted blood. Trust was fractured. Remi was angry about process. Green T had just armed a child and framed execution as education. Markop had just delivered a moral argument nobody wanted to hear. Bowser had just demonstrated that he carries Hjumpik with him in moments of decision.

The tanuki was in the bathroom.

And then things got worse.

## The Locked Room and the Lesson

Markop secured the tanuki. He shut the bathroom door, locked it from his side, and made certain the shapeshifter was contained. This was deliberate and careful — the action of someone who has finally learned that leaving loose ends in a haunted manor produces complications requiring stitches.

With the tanuki locked away — the same tanuki who had just been the subject of an execution debate, the same tanuki whose life had been spared over Remi's explicit objection, the same tanuki who was still breathing only because Markop pulled a gun upward and Bowser invoked the memory of Hjumpik — Green T turned his attention to Remi.

Waluigi needs to discuss Green T's approach to mentorship because it explains everything that followed.

Green T is a former crime lord who ran the Tea Leaf Syndicate through tea service and curtains. He survived the fireball that destroyed his organization, watched Earl Grey explode, lost everything he had built, and responded to each humiliation by becoming SHARPER. He is not evil in the cartoonish sense. He is practical in ways that look like evil from certain angles. He shot the Shadow Anchor from the children's table. He destroyed Remi's invisible ring by seeing something nobody else could see. His instinct is always to find the angle that avoids the obvious confrontation — or, when confrontation is unavoidable, to ensure the person doing the confronting is properly trained.

Green T told Remi she needed to focus better. That even if someone pulled her away — as Markop had pulled the gun away during the tanuki incident — she could not miss her shots. He asked the rhetorical question that hung in the air like smoke: what if that had been a bad guy instead of a tied-up shapeshifter?

The question answered itself. If it had been a bad guy, Remi would have missed, the bad guy would not have missed, and the Toads would be writing condolence letters.

Green T handed her a sheet of paper. A Bros Attack — a cooperative combat technique where one party member assists another to amplify effectiveness. The specific technique was a support-fire maneuver: Green T would steady Remi's aim, adjust her positioning, and coordinate timing so her shots landed with greater force and accuracy. The concept is sound. The execution requires practice, timing, and the kind of mutual trust that is difficult to build when one member of the pair has already shot someone she wasn't supposed to shoot.

The instruction sheet was, by all accounts, a simple childish drawing. Stick figures. Arrows indicating direction of fire. A smiling face next to 'GOOD' and a frowning face next to 'BAD.' Green T had calibrated his instructional materials to Remi's comprehension level, which Waluigi considers both pragmatic and slightly devastating.

Remi studied the paper. She understood it. Then she looked at the locked bathroom door — the door behind which the tanuki was sitting, alive, because the party had voted mercy over her objection — and said she thought they should test the technique on 'this guy.'

Waluigi needs to sit with the implications of this. Remi was angry that she did not get to vote on the tanuki's execution. The vote happened without her. Mercy won. The tanuki was freed into the bathroom. And now, given a new weapon — not a gun this time but a TECHNIQUE, a method for making her shots count — Remi's first instinct was to use it on the person who had been spared.

This is not random violence. This is FRUSTRATED AGENCY seeking an outlet. Remi was denied her democratic participation in the decision to kill the tanuki. She was angry about the process, not the outcome. And now she had a process of her own — the Bros Attack — and she wanted to apply it to the unfinished business behind that bathroom door.

Markop, who had been organizing supplies, asked what she meant. Remi held up the Bros Attack sheet and explained she had gotten a paper on how to shoot better. Waluigi notes the enthusiasm — the specific energy of a child showing off a gold star, completely disconnected from the fact that the 'gold star' was a cooperative combat technique and the proposed test subject was a prisoner of war whose life she had just been denied permission to end. Markop asked to see the paper. She handed it to him. The Toads crowded around, staring at the stick-figure diagram with the intensity of military analysts examining battle plans.

For a moment, there was the illusion of order — a team reviewing tactical documentation and preparing a measured response. Then Markop looked at the locked bathroom door. Then he looked at Remi. Then he looked at the door again.

Eager told the Toads to guard the front entrance door — the main door to their current position, not the bathroom. Waluigi notes the distinction because it matters: Eager was thinking about EXTERNAL threats. The undead. The Voss servants. The things in the hallway. He was establishing perimeter security at the correct chokepoint. The Toads responded with 'not on our watch,' which is a phrase Waluigi has heard approximately four hundred times and which has never once prevented the thing they were watching from happening.

Remi aimed at the bathroom door.

## The Second Shooting: The Tanuki Takes Another Hit

Markop objected immediately. They should not be attacking where a tied-up person was, he said, and he was correct. This was the reasonable, ethical, tactically sound position. Firing a weapon at a barricaded door behind which a restrained individual was sitting — the SAME individual whose life had been spared less than a day ago through divine mercy invoked in the name of an absent friend — was, by any standard of conduct, a terrible idea.

Salam, meanwhile, barricaded the entrance to their current position while everyone else argued. This is the kind of quietly competent action that goes unnoticed when louder people are debating whether to shoot prisoners through doors. Salam's instinct to fortify rather than attack was correct. Nobody acknowledged it. Nobody ever acknowledges it. Salam performs essential tactical functions in silence and receives trust questions about whether his money is a trick. Waluigi sees Salam. Waluigi documents Salam. Someone has to.

Remi aimed. Green T, honoring the spirit of the Bros Attack technique, nudged her aim down slightly. The adjustment was small — a matter of degrees. The difference between center mass on a door and lower center mass on a door behind which the tanuki — a shapeshifter who had impersonated their friend, yes, but who was also TIED UP and UNARMED and whose life had been DEMOCRATICALLY SPARED — was sitting.

A shot was fired. The door broke. A scream was heard.

The tanuki. Again. The same tanuki who had survived the execution debate, who had been freed into the bathroom by Markop, who had been locked in by Markop, who was probably sitting in there wondering whether the bathroom was any safer than the birthday trap he had been extracted from. Shot through a door.

Green T's Bros Attack worked. The shot was more accurate than Remi's unaided fire. The coordination improved her effectiveness. The technique functioned exactly as designed — against a prisoner who could not move, who had already been spared once, whose continued existence was supposed to represent the party's capacity for mercy.

Markop rushed to the scene. He healed the tanuki. He untied him. He ordered the party to leave the area immediately. The tanuki survived — barely — and was evacuated from the room in a state that Waluigi can only describe as 'justifiably furious at everyone involved and probably reconsidering every life choice that led to impersonating a Toad in a haunted manor.'

Waluigi wonders what the tanuki is thinking right now, wherever it is. It was hired to impersonate Toadburt. It was exposed. It was wrapped in a rug. A child pressed a gun to its head and pulled the trigger. The bullet grazed someone else instead. It was debated over like livestock. It was freed into a bathroom. It was locked in the bathroom. And then it was shot through the door by the same child using a new technique.

The tanuki's experience of Disaster Inc. is a concentrated version of what every person adjacent to this group eventually endures: you think the crisis is over, and then it gets worse in a direction you could not have predicted.

## The Confiscation and the Argument

Hours passed. The incident settled into the kind of tense silence that follows when everyone in a group knows something deeply wrong just happened and nobody wants to be the first to address it directly.

Then Markop reached for the gun.

The action was deliberate. Markop — four hooves, equine body, horse head with dark intelligent eyes that miss NOTHING — extended his hand toward the weapon Remi was carrying. His intent was clear: confiscation. Remi resisted. There was a struggle. Hands grabbed at the weapon. The party's healer and its most dangerous liability locked in physical contest over a gun.

Markop won. He is a centaur. Four-legged stability is both literal and metaphorical. Remi is a teenager. Physics and moral authority both favored Markop.

Dan offered the only appropriate commentary: 'Dang... that was pretty brutal.'

Markop told Remi she could not use that gun anymore. This was her second time. His voice was firm — the voice of someone drawing a line that should have been drawn earlier but that nobody had the authority or the willingness to draw until a shapeshifter was shot through a bathroom door.

Remi's defense was immediate: the tanuki had pretended to be their friend.

Markop's response was devastating in its precision. Three people had betrayed Remi, he said. She did not shoot them.

Waluigi has documented this argument in the Birthday Trap article, but its repetition here matters because of what Remi said NEXT. She said the three actual traitors were not betraying her — they were 'just having a rough time.' And then she said those people had MADE the tanuki pretend to be their friend, constructing a chain of culpability that absolved the masterminds and condemned the puppet.

The logic is circular and self-serving and deeply human. Remi cannot bring herself to hold the powerful accountable — the people who actually orchestrated the betrayals, who designed the traps, who erected the systems of control — because confronting power requires confronting the possibility that power cannot be reasoned with. It is easier to shoot the puppet than to face the puppeteer. The tanuki is small, contained, and helpless. The Onyx Hand is vast, diffuse, and everywhere. Remi's violence flows downhill, toward the weakest available target, because uphill violence is terrifying and uncertain.

Waluigi recognizes this pattern because Waluigi has seen it in kingdoms. He has seen it in empires. He has seen it in the Regal Empire's entire approach to governance: punish the visible, manageable, containable offender while the architects of suffering remain untouched in their administrative towers. Remi is not doing this consciously. She is doing it because it is the default setting of every frightened person who has been given a weapon and told to use it.

Salam, at the perimeter, heard footsteps approaching the barricaded doors. He reported arrows — his and Eager's. He sensed the approaching figures were undead.

Green T showed Remi how to properly hold the gun — if she was going to carry it again, which Markop had not yet authorized but which the tactical situation might require. He showed her how to aim. He put it away.

Remi thought about shooting the undead at the door. She didn't.

Waluigi considers this the single most significant moment of personal growth Remi has demonstrated in the entire Raventree operation. She had a weapon. She had targets. She had justification. And she chose not to fire. Whether this was because of Green T's training, Markop's confiscation, or simply exhaustion, the result was the same: Remi made a decision that did not involve a bullet.

Waluigi does not know if this represents lasting change or a temporary pause in an escalating pattern. But he documents it because it happened.

## The Wedding Invitation: A Masterwork of Aristocratic Menace

The party moved through what witnesses describe as the 'Moneybags Jungle' — a dense, overgrown area that Salam found conflicting for reasons unspecified in Waluigi's sources. They descended to a lower level. A guard — rushed, breathless, operating under time pressure — intercepted them.

The guard was delighted to see Remi. Just in time for the wedding, the guard said, and handed her a paper.

Waluigi has obtained a copy of this document. He has read it seven times. Each reading has produced a different emotion, ranging from professional admiration for the calligraphy to volcanic fury at its contents.

The invitation was issued BY DECREE OF THE HOUSE OF VOSS from SUNLESS KEEP, RAVENTREE VALE. It announced A Sacred and Eternal Union between Remi — identified as Ward of the Shadowmere Compact — and Lord Malachar Voss, Third Inheritor of the Onyx Throne, Warden of the Sunless Keep.

Waluigi will analyze the key elements because beneath the ornate script and theatrical language lies a legally sophisticated instrument of coercion that would make the Regal Empire's contract lawyers weep with professional envy.

**The wardship claim.** Remi is identified as a 'Ward of the Shadowmere Compact.' The word 'ward' is critical. A ward is not a free person. A ward is someone whose legal autonomy has been delegated to a custodial authority. If the Shadowmere Compact holds wardship over Remi, then Remi's consent to the marriage is, under whatever legal framework the Compact operates within, IRRELEVANT. The custodian consents on behalf of the ward. The ward attends. This is not a proposal. This is a notification of proceedings already concluded.

**The waiting.** The phrase 'has waited the appropriate span of mortal decades for the ward to reach her appointed ascendance' is one of the most disturbing sentences Waluigi has read in a career that includes Shroob invasion manuals, Afton research protocols, and Iron Legion processing doctrine. Lord Voss — an entity old enough to measure time in 'mortal decades' — has been WAITING for Remi to reach a specific age or state. This marriage was arranged before Remi was old enough to understand the concept of marriage. Possibly before she was born. The phrase 'His appetite for this occasion knows no restraint' is a line Waluigi will not analyze further because his therapist has specifically asked him to avoid dwelling on phrasing that activates what she calls his 'protective rage spiral.'

**The weaponized guest list.** Archie Miser is invited as 'Guest of Honor.' Lord Bowser is listed as 'Recognized Dignitary of the Shell Throne.' Green T receives the chilling note: 'Whom We Are Most Delighted to Welcome Back.' Waluigi himself is listed as 'Chronicler of the Recent Unpleasantness.'

The phrase 'Welcome Back' directed at Green T implies prior contact between Green T and the House of Voss. Green T has been here before. Green T has history with these people. The invitation acknowledges this history with the particular warmth of a predator greeting prey that previously escaped. Waluigi has filed this under 'things Green T has not told anyone about that will become critically important at the worst possible moment.'

**The contract disguised as invitation.** The fine print reads: 'By accepting this invitation the bearer acknowledges the full terms of the Shadowmere Compact (Vol. III, Articles 7-19), waives all rights to magical egress during the ceremony, consents to the temporary suppression of pyromantic faculties within the manor grounds, and agrees that all documentation produced thereafter belongs to the House of Voss in perpetuity. The House of Voss accepts no responsibility for conversions, bindings, or temporal displacements that occur as a natural consequence of attendance. Survival is a courtesy, not a guarantee.'

This is a CONTRACT. Accepting it — or even reading it, depending on the magical framework — binds the recipient to terms that include waiving magical escape, suppressing fire abilities, and surrendering intellectual property rights. The casual mention of 'conversions' and 'bindings' as 'natural consequences of attendance' strongly implies that guests at a Voss wedding may be transformed into something other than what they arrived as. Waluigi notes that 'documentation produced thereafter belongs to the House of Voss in perpetuity' means that if Waluigi attends this wedding, his NOTES would belong to the Voss family. His encyclopedia entries. His analysis. His LIFE'S WORK. This clause alone constitutes an act of war against Waluigi personally and Waluigi will not be attending. WAH.

**The acrostic threat.** The 'verse for the occasion' contains first letters spelling a message. Waluigi will not insult the reader's intelligence by pretending this is subtle. The House of Voss does not do subtle. They do ELEGANT, which is different. Subtle means hidden. Elegant means visible but so well-constructed that acknowledging it feels like complimenting your own executioner.

The final line of the invitation: 'If you are reading this after sunrise, the invitation did not reach you. You were already there.'

Remi said: 'This is so sudden.'

Waluigi would like it noted that 'this is so sudden' is the most inadequate response to an involuntary marriage summons from an immortal vampire lord that Waluigi can imagine. The appropriate response involves screaming, strategic withdrawal, and ideally a continent between yourself and the Sunless Keep. Remi's response suggests she processed the invitation as a social event rather than a legal abduction. This is consistent with Remi's established pattern of evaluating situations based on whether they seem interesting rather than whether they seem dangerous. A vampire wedding is INTERESTING. The fact that it is also a binding contract designed to absorb her into an immortal aristocratic bloodline is, apparently, secondary.

## The Evacuation: Markop Takes Command

Markop told Remi they needed to go to the garden. His tone was different now — the centaur healer shifting into emergency mode. Four hooves planted. Dark horse eyes scanning exit routes. The ears that swivel toward threats before his body turns to face them already tracking movement in the corridors beyond.

Markop offered Salam money to buy arrows. The gesture was practical — Salam needed ammunition, Markop had resources. Salam's response revealed the depth of trust damage within the party: he did not know if he could trust Markop, he said. How did he know it was not a trick? Eager agreed.

This is what three betrayals, two shootings, one kidnapping invitation, and a general atmosphere of supernatural hostility does to group cohesion. The party's healer — the person who has spent the entire operation stitching wounds, managing conflicts, carrying teenagers, and trying to maintain ethical behavior in a situation that punishes ethics — offers the party's ranger money for arrows, and the ranger questions whether the money is a trap.

Markop did not argue. He did not explain. He picked up Remi.

Physically. He lifted her. Firefighter carry — over one shoulder, her legs secured, her protests muffled against his back. The centaur who had healed the tanuki twice, confiscated the gun, delivered moral arguments that nobody wanted to hear, and served as the party's operational anchor for the entire Raventree operation simply picked up the girl and started walking.

They left. They did not wait for Salam. They did not wait for Eager. They did not wait for anyone. Markop walked out of the building carrying Remi like luggage, his hooves steady on the stone, his direction clear: away from the wedding, away from the manor interior, toward the garden and the grove beyond it.

Waluigi respects this decision enormously. It was unilateral. It was physically coercive. It was exactly correct. When an immortal vampire lord sends a binding contract disguised as a wedding invitation for someone in your care, you do not hold a committee meeting. You do not consult stakeholders. You do not attempt the democratic process that has already failed twice in the last twenty-four hours. You grab the person and you LEAVE.

## The Singing Incident

Outside the manor, voices could be heard. People were rolling out a red carpet with Remi's face on it. Waluigi needs to repeat that: a RED CARPET with REMI'S FACE on it. The wedding preparations were already underway. The House of Voss was not waiting for RSVP confirmation.

Markop assessed the grounds. They needed to get Remi out of there.

Bowser, drawn toward the carpet with the instinct of a man who sees ceremonial infrastructure and assumes it might be for him, started heading toward it. A Toad grabbed his arm and redirected him. Bowser, for once, allowed himself to be redirected.

Someone suggested stealth. Green T asked the Toads if they could start singing. Dan agreed. They sang.

Waluigi needs to process this sequence. The party identified a stealth requirement. Green T's response to the stealth requirement was to initiate a GROUP MUSICAL PERFORMANCE. Drums. Loud noises. A full-volume concert performed by multiple Toads, a plumber in green, and a former ghost-hunting coordinator, all while attempting to sneak past hostile forces constructing wedding infrastructure for their teammate's involuntary marriage.

Remi sang along, mumbling the words, still draped over Markop's shoulder, contributing to the chorus with the enthusiasm of someone who has forgotten she is being carried away from her own kidnapping.

Markop yelled for them to stop. One by one they stopped. Dan first. Then Green T. Then the Toads. Remi kept singing — still in Markop's hands, still over his shoulder, still humming and mumbling a tune the rest of the group had abandoned. Markop put his hand over her mouth. She eventually stopped.

The voices in the distance fell silent.

Markop did not wait to find out if they had been heard. He continued moving.

## Tymnas: The Groundskeeper and the Missing Scythe

The party reached the lodge of Tymnas — a groundskeeper responsible for maintaining the grove at the center of the Raventree estate. Weathered, practical, possessed of the deep resigned frustration that belongs to people who perform essential work that nobody respects until it stops getting done. Waluigi recognizes this energy. Waluigi has BEEN this energy.

Tymnas greeted them with casual warmth and handed them seeds. Then, when they asked about the siglet — the quest objective they had been pursuing through hours of shooting, singing, fleeing, and matrimonial documentation — Tymnas showed them his ring finger.

The siglet was a ring on the groundskeeper's finger. It had been there the entire time. They could have come straight here.

Waluigi does not know whether to laugh or weep. The party navigated a haunted manor, shot a tanuki through a door, received a vampire wedding invitation, was nearly discovered by hostile forces while performing a musical number, and was carried across the grounds in a firefighter carry — all while the thing they needed was sitting on an old man's hand in a cottage they could have visited first.

Tymnas explained what they needed to do in exchange. An entity — 'the shadowy bastard' — had attacked him, sent him sprawling, and stolen his scythe. The scythe was the tool he used to maintain the grove, to keep the weeds and thorns and darker things in check. Without it, the grove had become dangerous. Its central feature — the Tree of Woe, a tree existing simultaneously across multiple planes, called the Tree of Dreams by the fey — had awakened. Its branches were now 'thick with hanging corpses and the blackest crows you ever saw.'

The entity that stole the scythe was called the Scorncrow. Fast, resilient, shrugging off normal weapons, wielding the stolen scythe with expert proficiency, commanding a 'giant murder of spectral crows' that obeyed its commands. Tymnas had tried shouting at it. Shouting did not work.

Tymnas offered dinner and a bedroom. The door to the guest quarters was blocked. Dan grabbed the doorknob and heard Bowser whispering through the other side — something about blocking the door, having made a mess, needing a bit of time because 'a king knows how to clean his castle.' Waluigi does not know what mess Bowser made in a groundskeeper's guest room and Waluigi does not want to know.

Salam checked outside the window and sensed someone approaching. Dan stepped away from the door. Dan and Tymnas eventually made their way to the bath — a small wooden bucket arrangement that served as the lodge's washing facility. Eager guarded the door. Dan and Tymnas shared the space with the comfortable familiarity of people who have both survived things that make bathing together seem perfectly reasonable by comparison.

Eager spoke with Tymnas about the grove's nature through the door. The Tree of Woe. The Scorncrow. The danger. Tymnas was contemplative, pausing to wonder whether the Scorncrow was a 'he' or an 'it,' then waving the question away with a weathered hand. Whatever it was, it was exceptionally dangerous, used the scythe's power to enhance its own abilities rather than tending Tymnas's hedges, and commanded spectral crows that never shut up.

Waluigi notes the tactical profile: fast, weapon-resistant, armed with a stolen magical artifact, commanding aerial spectral forces in its home territory with air superiority. This is not a weeding problem. This is a military engagement against a supernatural combatant that the party would need to fight with a teenager who just had her gun confiscated, a healer, some Toads, and whatever Bowser was doing in the guest bedroom.

## The Kidnapping: Markop Taken

Time passed. Markop retrieved Eager from the bath, where Eager had been washing Tymnas's body — both of them sitting in the small wooden tub, a domestic tableau that Waluigi finds oddly touching in the context of a survival mission in a haunted nightmare grove.

Remi explored the kitchen of Tymnas's lodge — the warmest and most welcoming space anyone in the party had encountered since arriving in Raventree. Rich yellows and greens that 'practically strained against whatever force sucks the color from this plane.' Shelves of knick-knacks, dishes, foodstuffs. Food that looked 'almost normal.' Waluigi notes the word 'almost.' In Raventree, even comfort is approximate.

The party heard voices outside — Vostolas and associates entering the lodge through the front door. Tymnas answered a doorbell. The party slipped out a window as the Voss delegation entered through the front. They were not seen. The Toads — oblivious in the bath — picked up a vial of black ash from somewhere in the lodge.

Markop led the group upward, toward the center of the grove. Toward the place where the scythe was.

He saw someone in the bushes. He asked what they were doing.

The figure — female, humanoid, possibly fey — grabbed his axe. She said: 'Welcome to the grove. Welcome to the gray.' She grabbed Markop and pulled him into the undergrowth. He disappeared into the grove's interior with the speed and finality of someone being swallowed by vegetation.

The party's healer was gone. Kidnapped into a cursed forest by an entity that had also taken his weapon. The centaur who had spent the entire operation stitching wounds, confiscating firearms, healing tanukis, carrying teenagers, delivering moral arguments, and serving as the only structural support keeping this party from total collapse — yanked into the bushes like a misplaced garden tool.

Waluigi has seen parties lose their healer before. It never goes well. It goes ESPECIALLY poorly when the healer's absence coincides with an approaching combat encounter against a supernaturally enhanced scarecrow with a stolen scythe and the healer was also the only person in the group who consistently made good decisions.

## The Split: Bowser's Commandeering

Bowser looked at the bushes where Markop had disappeared and asked if they were going to save him.

The Toads assessed the situation with cold pragmatism: they could help, but some of them were fragile.

Remi offered a perspective that Waluigi finds emblematic of her entire crisis management philosophy: Markop was pretty strong, so he did not need help at all.

Waluigi will note: Markop was just kidnapped. His axe was stolen. He was dragged into a supernatural forest by an unknown entity. And Remi's assessment was 'he'll be fine.' This is either extraordinary faith in Markop's capabilities or extraordinary unwillingness to interrupt her own plans. Waluigi suspects it is both. Remi has spent the entire operation watching Markop survive things that should have killed him — the death beam, the Mazebound dragging, the Vivian encounter — and has concluded that Markop's survival is a constant rather than an achievement. She does not understand that every time Markop survives, he is spending something that does not replenish infinitely.

Bowser offered Remi a comparison that, while crude, contained historical weight. She reminded him of Peach, he said, if Peach didn't have any guards and was a big baby. At least Peach would put up a fight.

Remi said she couldn't wait to meet Peach one day.

Bowser looked down. Something passed across his face that witnesses describe as sadness — genuine, unguarded, the kind that breaks through even the thickest shell of bravado. 'Right...' he said.

Bowser carries a letter to Princess Peach. Waluigi has documented it elsewhere. 'Dear Peach, I heard you were here. I am NOT kidnapping you. Unless you want to go? No, wait. I am just visiting. Please do not unleash Mario on me. Love, Bowser.' Burn marks on the edges from frustration. Written in elegant calligraphy forced on him by royal tutors he probably terrorized. The letter is Bowser trying to be good and not knowing how. The burn marks are from him trying to destroy drafts and then deciding to keep them because the act of writing to Peach matters more than the quality of what is written.

Peach has been dead since 955 BF. Remi does not know this. Nobody has told her. Bowser absorbs the reference like a punch to the chest and moves on because that is what Bowser does — he takes hits and keeps walking.

The party stood there. Nobody was moving toward Markop's rescue.

Bowser made a decision. He pointed at Salam and commandeered him with the volume and authority of a king who has decided that the chain of command is whatever he says it is. Salam was coming with him. Salam was an accomplice. Waluigi is unclear on what Salam was allegedly an accomplice TO, but Bowser's logic was sufficient for Bowser.

Eager objected — Salam was their healer and was coming with THEM. Bowser grabbed Salam, lifted him off the ground, and held him horizontally like a surfboard. He promised not to let Salam get hurt and walked into the grove carrying a ranger like a piece of equipment.

The party was in pieces.

**Markop:** Kidnapped, somewhere in the grove, without his axe.

**Bowser, Salam, and Dan (one-armed Shadowfell version):** Heading into the grove to find Markop.

**Remi, Eager, and Rodger:** Alone at the edge of the grove, without a healer, without Bowser's strength, without a plan.

Remi looked at Eager and Rodger. The quest was important, she said. They didn't come this way for nothing. So let's do the quest.

They headed toward the Tree of Woe.

Waluigi documents the party split not because it was strategic — it was the OPPOSITE of strategic — but because it represents the fundamental failure mode of this group. They do not split because of disagreement about objectives. They split because of disagreement about PRIORITIES. Bowser prioritized loyalty — Markop had done him a service, and Bowser repays debts. Remi prioritized the mission — the siglet, the scythe, the tree. Neither was wrong in isolation. Together, they ensured that neither group had sufficient resources to accomplish their goal safely.

This is the paradox of Disaster Inc.: individual correctness producing collective catastrophe.

## Bowser's Path: The Grove, the Maze, and the Portal

Bowser put Salam on the ground and told him to look. Salam found footsteps leading to the right side of the grove. They followed.

Then something grabbed Dan. He was pulled into the bushes with tremendous speed and force by a Mazebound — one of the grove's hostile entities, a creature of the labyrinth that seized intruders and consumed them.

Bowser had one shot. He roared. He activated his Giant's Might — the ancient magic of his lineage, the power that separates a Koopa king from an ordinary Koopa. He grew. His muscles swelled. His voice shook the trees. He grabbed Dan.

The Mazebound pulled from the other side.

A tug of war. Dan in the middle. His one arm was in agony. The Mazebound pulled with the strength of something that lived in the spaces between paths and fed on the lost. Bowser pulled with the strength of a king who had decided this particular person was HIS to protect.

Bowser roared LOUDER and punched with his free fist. Dan tried to dodge — one punch hit him, another hit the Mazebound. Dan slashed at the creature. It screamed. Bowser tugged harder. The Mazebound tried to grab Bowser's fists. Bowser kept punching — a fury of punches, the kind he used to smash boulders in his youth, each impact driving the Mazebound back until it released Dan.

Bowser grabbed Dan, said he would take this and go, and RAN.

Waluigi notes: Bowser ran. He did not stay to finish the fight. He did not attempt to kill the Mazebound. He secured the person he came to protect and LEFT. This is, by Bowser's standards, extraordinary tactical discipline. Bowser's instinct is to fight everything until it stops moving. Choosing retreat — choosing the objective over the battle — suggests something about this operation has shifted his priorities in a way Waluigi finds both encouraging and deeply unprecedented.

Bowser continued through the grove, beheading a Mazebound in passing — apparently unable to sustain his pacifist streak for more than ninety seconds — and encountered Bryan the Toad, the original Dan, and the aftermath of another Mazebound engagement.

The original Dan's eyes glowed. He demanded: 'Hand over that Dan now. There can only be one.'

Waluigi needs to address this. The Dan situation is one of the most complicated identity crises in the party's orbit. The original Dan — documented extensively elsewhere in this archive — was once a decent leader of the Liberated Toads who got his hands on a cursed staff, killed thirteen of his own people, nearly consumed their souls, had his arm chopped off by Green T, and was taken to an archmage for treatment involving dark magic and shrinking. The one-armed Shadowfell Dan traveling with the party is a copy, duplicate, or alternative version whose relationship to the original is unclear. The original Dan's demand represents a territorial claim over the identity itself — the assertion that two Dans cannot coexist.

Bowser's response was characteristic: he did not care about their rivalry. He just wanted to know where Markop was. If the original Dan wanted the other Dan, he could ask the Toads nicely.

They used non-magical fire — a simple lighter — to burn through crops and reached the Midnight Portal. Bowser was told Markop had gone through. He was skeptical — no footmarks, no evidence. Bryan and the original Dan claimed they had seen Markop fight a Mazebound and flee through the portal.

Then, with the casual cruelty of someone who does not understand what they are saying, one of them asked if maybe there was another princess through the portal — or had Bowser given up on that since she died?

Silence.

'Don't disrespect the princess,' Bowser said. His voice was quiet — the kind of quiet that large, powerful beings produce when choosing between violence and restraint. He said he had kidnapped her many times. As though that explained everything. As though the history of kidnapping was, in Bowser's mind, a form of devotion rather than a crime.

Someone asked if he would ever move on. Bowser told them to back off — was this a therapy session?

Waluigi documents this exchange because it is the THIRD time in this operation that Bowser's grief over Peach has surfaced. With Remi. With the question about moving on. And with the letter he carries. Each time, the grief breaks through the armor of bravado and roaring and fire, and each time Bowser shoves it back down because the alternative is acknowledging the answer to 'will you ever move on.'

The answer is no. Bowser will not move on. Bowser will carry a letter to a dead princess for the rest of his life because the act of carrying matters more than the impossibility of delivery.

Bowser ordered them toward the portal. They started walking. Bowser, sensing something was about to go wrong, picked up the sleeping Dan and followed. He bumped into them. The portal activated. Bowser tripped. He fell in. With Dan.

## The Fracture Atrium: Bowser Falls Through

Bowser and the sleeping Dan materialized in a circular atrium lined with marble statues of Corvinarus ancestors. Faces leaning inward, looming. Teleportation circles of burnished gold inset within black marble. The sigils that had illuminated upon arrival faded to dull, lifeless gray.

They were in the Corvinarus Sanctum — an extraplanar space, the receiving area of a dimension constructed by someone with sufficient power and ego to build a personal reality. The Oracle had described this place. Archie had been here. This was where the flesh vats were. Where the time dilation warnings originated. Where a month had passed in the Shadowfell while days passed in the Material Plane.

The sigils were dead. The portal behind them was closed. They were trapped.

The original Dan snickered from somewhere in the atrium — he had come through as well. The original Dan was awake. The copy Dan was asleep. All of Bowser's friends were gone.

Bowser put his hand on the sleeping Dan's shoulder and told the original Dan to scram. The original Dan asked if Bowser was a one-man army. Bowser said he WAS his own army. The original Dan proposed a duel over Dan. Bowser accepted.

'This fight will be your last,' the original Dan said.

## The Duel: Bowser vs. the Original Dan

The original Dan opened with Scorching Ray — a fire-based magical attack that backfired in the Fracture Atrium's unstable magical environment, bursting back toward its caster. Dan shrugged off his own flames with the practiced indifference of someone who has fire resistance built into his classification.

Bowser laughed and cracked his knuckles. He assessed his opponent with a tactical eye that Waluigi would not have credited him with before this operation — recognizing Mages' Guild clothing design, estimating second-class fire mage classification, probably trained in the Aumnwood or Ironwood region. Bowser asked if Dan wanted to talk about his history. Dan did not.

Bowser invoked the Fire Rune — ancient Giant magic integrated with natural Koopa pyromancy. The rune is carved into fist or weapon surface. Upon striking, it summons fiery shackles — chains of magma that wrap the victim, restrain them, and burn continuously. The kinetic force of the blow ignites the rune, the rune generates the chains, the chains cook the target inside their own position.

Bowser's warhammer connected twice. Dan was knocked backward with tremendous force and wrapped in chains of molten fire. But the fire had no effect — Dan moved his hands within the burning cuffs as though they were warm bracelets, continuing to smirk with the specific arrogance of someone who has been playing with fire long enough to forget that fire is not the only threat in the room.

Bowser punched him. 'This is for lying to me.' Black eye. Another punch. 'This is for acting like you're better than me.' Dan broke the cuffs. A firestorm descended from above — Dan's environmental fire, raining down upon the atrium. Bowser retreated into his shell. Dan summoned acid elementals that pierced through Bowser's skin — a new attack vector bypassing heat resistance.

Bowser emerged from his shell and produced a portable Bullet Bill cannon.

Waluigi needs to pause here. Bowser was carrying a PORTABLE BULLET BILL CANNON. Through a haunted grove. Through a midnight portal. Into an extraplanar sanctum. He had it with him THE ENTIRE TIME. He chose to use fists and fire runes for the first portion of the fight because — and Waluigi cannot believe he is writing this — Bowser was showing RESTRAINT. He opened with honor. He escalated to technology only when honor proved insufficient.

Two Bullet Bills fired, tracking Dan with the mindless determination of ordnance designed by Koopa engineers who believe the answer to every tactical question is 'more explosions.'

Dan was hit. He told Bowser to go home. Bowser roared that he did not WANT to be here — he just wanted to know where Markop was. He called Dan cocky. He said he did not like people who played dumb.

One final punch. Dan flew backward, hit a wall, slid to the floor. Unconscious.

Bowser stood over the crumpled body of a second-class fire mage who had made the terminal error of assuming that a large reptile with a crown was merely a large reptile with a crown. He patted the Bullet Bill cannon. 'Good job,' he said.

## The Looting: What Bowser Found

Bowser searched the body. The original Dan had a black eye, blue bruising, burn marks, and bruised ribs. Alive but comprehensively beaten.

**A photograph.** Dan with other Toads on an airship. With Archie Miser. Waluigi needs to address this photograph because it connects the original Dan directly to Archie's operation. Archie has been identified throughout the Raventree crisis as a figure of significant importance — wanted by multiple factions, possessing containment knowledge related to the Three-Eyed Bandit, and currently somewhere in the Shadeward after absorbing too much portal energy from the Oracle's ritual. If the original Dan is one of Archie's associates, then his presence here, his demand for the copy Dan, and his willingness to fight Bowser all make strategic sense: he was protecting operational security for a network that Archie built.

**A Mages' Guild notebook.** Containing containment protocols related to the Three-Eyed Bandit. Bowser's reaction was characteristic — maybe if he fought Archie, he could make gold. A friendly fight. Bowser views every discovery through the lens of profit and combat opportunity.

**A wand.** Dan's casting implement. Bowser took it.

**A water pouch** containing Shadeward water — water from the shadow realm itself — with **a gold coin taped to the back.** Bowser considered using the coin to pay off Wario's debts, which is both mathematically optimistic and morally questionable.

**A Bowser Badge.** This stopped Bowser cold. Pinned to Dan's body was a badge bearing Bowser's own insignia, with a number written on it: 447.

Bowser stared at it. He thought about ripping it off. Skin came off with it.

The badge was not pinned to clothing. It was integrated into Dan's body — fused, bonded, or grown into the skin. When Bowser tore it free, Dan's body erupted in flames from the removal point. The badge was not decoration. It was a SYSTEM COMPONENT. Removing it triggered catastrophic biological response.

Waluigi needs to analyze this. What is the Bowser Badge? Why does it bear Bowser's insignia? Why is it numbered — 447 implies at least 446 others. Why is it fused to Dan's biology? What system is it a component OF? And why does its removal trigger immolation?

Waluigi has insufficient data to answer these questions definitively. But Waluigi has theories, and Waluigi's theories tend to age well.

The numbering system implies an organization. An organization that uses Bowser's insignia. An organization with at least 447 members or assets. An organization whose membership requires physical integration of an identifier that cannot be removed without lethal consequence. This sounds like a military unit — specifically, it sounds like a Koopa military unit, or something designed to LOOK like one.

Is Bowser aware of this organization? His surprise at finding the badge suggests no. But Bowser ran a kingdom. He had underlings who made traps — he said so himself during the Birthday Trap assessment. Is it possible that a military apparatus bearing his insignia exists that Bowser does not know about? Is it possible that someone built an organization using Bowser's name and symbology without his knowledge or consent?

Waluigi does not know. But 447 is a large number. And the original Dan — a Mages' Guild fire mage connected to Archie Miser — was wearing it.

Bowser sighed. He wanted information, so he did not want Dan to die just yet. He attempted to reattach the badge. It did not rebond. He cauterized the wound with his own fire, trying to stabilize the body. The original Dan was in critical condition — stable for now, but without proper medical care the damage would be fatal.

Bowser took the spellbook. He checked on the sleeping Dan — still sleeping peacefully, oblivious to everything. He checked the sleeping Dan's pockets. Nothing interesting.

Then Bowser looked up and saw Orange T.

## Orange T, Bones, and the Collapsing Library

Orange T — a Toad associated with the manor's internal operations — was present in the sanctum, treating Bones. They were in a circular chamber filled with elaborate wooden shelves extending upward in diminishing tiers, packed with leather-bound books of assorted colors and shapes. Three grand lecterns stood on a raised platform at the center, holding ornate tomes with metal locking mechanisms and ornate scrollwork that immediately marked them as texts neither mundane nor ordinary.

The chamber was beautiful. It was also collapsing. The floor was shattering — slowly, progressively, like fine china hurled in slow motion. The marble broke into fragments. The purple carpet tore and split. The room was being pulled apart by forces the architecture could not resist.

Bones — the person Archie had left in the Oracle's care with strict instructions not to put him in a flesh vat — was here. Being treated by Orange T. In a disintegrating room. In a dimension where time moves differently and portals close behind you.

The Oracle is somewhere in this sanctum as well. The 46-year-old interdimensional custodian with the flesh vat collection who warned Archie about time dilation and noted that Archie was absorbing TOO MUCH power during the transit ritual. The Oracle who exists in all of this like a hand in dirty water: visible only by the things it disturbs. Waluigi does not trust the Oracle. Waluigi has not trusted the Oracle from the beginning. The Oracle keeps being useful. This does not improve trust.

Bowser is now stranded in a collapsing extradimensional library with an unconscious imposter Dan in critical condition, a sleeping copy Dan who will not wake up, a Toad treating an injured skeleton person, and no clear way back to the party.

## Current Positions: The Catastrophe Map

**Bowser, Orange T, Bones, sleeping Dan, and critically wounded original Dan:** Corvinarus Sanctum — collapsing library — stranded across planar boundary.

**The Oracle:** Somewhere in the Fracture Atrium — same sanctum complex — intentions unclear.

**Remi, Eager, and Rodger:** Approaching the Tree of Woe — without healer, without heavy combat support, heading directly toward the Scorncrow.

**Markop:** Kidnapped — somewhere in the grove — without his axe — location unknown.

**Salam:** Separated during the portal chaos — location uncertain within the grove.

**Green T:** Location unconfirmed — last seen in the lodge area — listed on the wedding invitation as someone the House of Voss is 'Most Delighted to Welcome Back.'

**Tymnas:** At his lodge — siglet ring on his finger — scythe still missing.

**Vostolas:** Entered Tymnas's lodge with associates — objectives unknown.

**The House of Voss:** Rolling out a red carpet with Remi's face — wedding preparations ongoing — survival is a courtesy, not a guarantee.

A month has passed in the Shadowfell since the planar fracture. Time is not synchronized. The Onyx Hand has had thirty days to recover. Vivian Corvinarus has had thirty days to consolidate or be hunted. Green T has been surviving in a hostile death-world for weeks.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Waluigi has documented many operational disasters. The Battle of the Brobot. The Shroob Temporal Incursion. The Fazbear acquisition. Each involved extraordinary circumstances — alien invasions, dimensional warfare, haunted pizza robots. Extraordinary circumstances produce extraordinary failures.

The Grove of Woe Incident is not an extraordinary failure. It is an ORDINARY failure amplified by the particular chemistry of this group. Every decision that led to the current catastrophe was individually defensible.

Markop locking the tanuki — correct. Green T training Remi — debatable but understandable. Markop confiscating the gun — correct. Markop carrying Remi away from the wedding — correct. Bowser pursuing Markop's rescue — correct. Remi continuing the mission — correct.

The problem is not that any single decision was wrong. The problem is that correct decisions made by people with incompatible priorities produce INCORRECT outcomes.

Markop prioritized protection. Bowser prioritized loyalty. Remi prioritized the mission. Green T prioritized training. Salam prioritized trust verification.

Every one of them was right. And the aggregate result of all of them being right was a party scattered across two planes of existence with no healer, no plan, and a vampire wedding approaching.

This is the fundamental paradox of group operations: individual correctness does not guarantee collective success. You can have five people making five good decisions and produce a result worse than if one idiot had made all the decisions alone, because at least the idiot would have been CONSISTENT.

Disaster Inc. is held together less by belief than by repeated survival. Every time the universe should have broken them and did not, the bond thickened. Not because they became healthier. Because they became harder to separate. This incident separated them anyway.

The tanuki was shot twice. Spared twice. Shot through a door by the person who was denied the vote to kill it. Healed twice by the person who denied the vote. And somewhere in a bathroom in Raventree Manor, a shapeshifter who impersonated a Toad for a birthday trap is probably wondering whether any amount of money was worth getting involved with these people.

Remi needs the scythe. Bowser needs Markop. Markop needs his axe. Salam needs to trust someone. Green T needs to not be 'welcomed back' by vampires. The Toads need to stop singing. The tanuki needs a therapist.

None of these needs are compatible with each other. None can be sacrificed without consequence. And the clock — both literal and matrimonial — is ticking.

The wedding invitation said: 'Survival is a courtesy, not a guarantee.'

Waluigi considers this the most honest thing the House of Voss has ever written.

And somewhere in a collapsing library in another dimension, the King of the Koopas is standing over the body of a man he just beat nearly to death, holding a photograph that connects to a conspiracy he doesn't understand, carrying a badge bearing his own insignia that he did not authorize, in a room full of books he can't read, with a portal that won't reopen behind him.

Bowser's response to this situation will probably involve punching something.

Waluigi is, against his better judgment, rooting for him.

Because what else is there?

WAH.

name: The Seven Nights at Fazbear: A Complete Record
title: What Actually Happened, Night by Night, According to Wario's Ledger and Waluigi's Investigative Journalism
location: Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza (Nights 1, 2, 7) / Abandoned Freddy's East (Night 3) / Fazbear's Fright Ruins (Night 4) / Circus Baby's Pizza World (Night 5) / The Pizzaplex Remains (Night 6) / The Secret Bunker (Night 7)
type: Supernatural Investigation / Corporate Salvage / Accidental Heroism / Sequential Disaster
status: Classified; Reconstructed from Wario's Ledger, Michael Afton's Deposition, Surveillance Recordings, and One Very Awkward Interview Over Garlic Bread
summary: A night-by-night reconstruction of Wario's seven-night tenure as the sole employee of his own haunted pizza franchise. Each night escalated the stakes, introduced new complications, and demonstrated in increasingly vivid detail that Wario's immunity to supernatural horror is both his greatest asset and everyone else's worst nightmare. Documented here because the Mages' Guild version of events is sanitized beyond recognition and Wario's own account is approximately forty percent bragging.
description:
Waluigi has assembled this record from multiple sources: Wario's ledger (which Waluigi photographed during a visit to the Super Steakplex while Wario was in the kitchen), Michael Afton's written deposition, surveillance camera footage that the Mages' Guild believed they had confiscated, the collective testimony of seven former Fazbear employees who agreed to speak on condition of anonymity, and one telephone interview with a woman named 'Donna' who identified herself only as 'Wario's mother' and provided context that Waluigi found both illuminating and deeply humanizing.

Waluigi has organized the account chronologically. This is more difficult than it sounds because Wario's ledger entries are written in a personal shorthand that mixes Italian, broken English, financial notation, and what appear to be garlic bread recipes. Translating 'NITE 1: GOT MASK, STINKY GUY SHOWED UP, PASTA MOLTO BENE' into a coherent historical record required considerable interpretive effort.

Waluigi has done his best. WAH.
