sections.subtitle: The Boss Takes the First Shift
sections.overview:
Night One established the template for everything that followed: Wario entering a space that should terrify him, being completely unbothered, obtaining something valuable, and then being approached by someone in the parking lot who wanted something from him.

The date was the 14th of Autumn's End, 1038 BF. Wario arrived at the Hurricane flagship location—the original Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, a building that had been abandoned for eleven years and looked it—at approximately 11:45 PM. He was wearing his standard outfit augmented with a hard hat labeled 'THE BOSS' in marker and a reflective safety vest that he had borrowed from a construction site and not returned.

His stated purpose: 'Check out my new property and see what's worth taking.'

His unstated awareness: zero. Wario had read the health department file, the lawsuit documentation, and the franchise disclosure statement. He had not read the three Mages' Guild supernatural hazard classifications, the fourteen incident reports referencing 'aggressive animatronic behavior,' or the anonymous employee testimony that described the back rooms as 'a place where you can feel something watching you even when you can absolutely confirm that nothing is there.' These documents had been flagged for his attention by his acquisition lawyer. Wario had used them as coasters.

subsections.name: The Location: Hurricane Flagship
subsections.description:
The Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza had been the crown jewel of the franchise in its operational days. It was the largest location, the most profitable, and the most infamous. It was here that the original five children had been murdered. It was here that the original animatronics—Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and the Marionette—had spent decades haunting the night security staff. It was here that the spring-lock incident had occurred, trapping William Afton in the Spring Bonnie suit.

By the time Wario arrived, the building had been through three complete ownership cycles and two attempted renovations, each of which had been abandoned partway through when the contractors reported 'inexplicable equipment failures' and 'a persistent feeling of malevolent observation.' The result was a building that was simultaneously in three stages of renovation, decorated in three distinct aesthetic eras of Fazbear branding, and smelling of old pizza, motor oil, and something that eleven years of abandonment had not been able to fully erase.

Wario described it in his ledger as: 'Bit run down. Could use some garlic.'

Waluigi considers this assessment both accurate and insufficient.

points_of_interest.name: The Main Dining Area
points_of_interest.description:
The largest room in the building, featuring the main stage where Freddy, Bonnie, and Chica had performed. The animatronics were gone—moved to storage years earlier—but the stage remained, along with the faded murals, the disconnected speaker system, and several hundred plastic chairs stacked in corners.

Wario walked through this room with a flashlight and a clipboard, making notes on what was salvageable. His notes: 'Chairs OK. Table maybe. Murals ugly.' He did not note the temperature drop of approximately eight degrees that occurred as he crossed the threshold from the entrance hallway to the main dining area. He did not note the fact that his flashlight flickered twice in a pattern that the former head of security, in his incident report from seven years earlier, had described as 'a warning.' He noted that the floor needed refinishing.

points_of_interest.name: Pirate's Cove
points_of_interest.description:
The curtained alcove where Foxy had performed. The curtains were still drawn. Behind them, the space was empty—Foxy's suit had been removed and placed in storage with the others. But the space felt occupied in a way that Wario noticed enough to write about in his ledger: 'Creepy corner. Don't put tables there. Put the bar.'

Waluigi notes that Wario's instinct to NOT put tables near Pirate's Cove was sound, though Wario's reasoning was aesthetic rather than supernatural. The former employees had universally reported that the area around Pirate's Cove remained anomalously cold even after Fritz's spirit was no longer bound to Foxy's suit. Some locations retain spiritual impressions long after the entity that created them has departed.

points_of_interest.name: The Prize Corner and the Marionette
points_of_interest.description:
This is where Night One became significant.

The Prize Corner was a booth near the back of the main dining area where children had redeemed tickets for prizes. In its operational days, it had featured a music box that played a lullaby. The music box had been connected to the Marionette—when the music stopped, the Marionette became active and dangerous.

The music box was silent. Had been silent for eleven years. The Marionette's physical suit was in the back storage room, along with the others.

But the Marionette—Charlie's spirit, the guardian, the architect of the haunting—was present in the Prize Corner when Wario walked past.

What happened next is described differently by different sources. Wario's ledger: 'Grabbed the Frederick mask from the case in the back. The puppet thing was watching. I watched it back. It blinked first.' Michael Afton's deposition: 'I don't know how he got past the Marionette. I have tried to enter that storage room fourteen times over the years and been physically repelled every time. The Puppet has attacked people for approaching the masks. He just walked in and took one.' The former head of security, interviewed by phone: 'The Marionette was the most dangerous entity in any of the locations. Whatever that man did to get past her, I don't want to know.'

Waluigi's assessment: The Marionette evaluated Wario. It recognized something in him that it had never encountered before. A human being who was genuinely incapable of being corrupted by the tragedy it had spent decades managing. And it stood aside.

Wario walked out of the storage room with the Freddy mask under his arm, made a note in his ledger ('Mask: fancy, probably worth something, keep'), and went to check on the kitchen equipment.

subsections.name: The Parking Lot: Michael's Introduction
subsections.description:
Wario was loading salvageable kitchen equipment into his van when he noticed a hooded figure standing near the dumpsters.

Michael Afton stepped forward into the beam of Wario's flashlight. He was wearing a faded gray hoodie, dark trousers, and the expression of a man who had been carrying an enormous weight for a very long time and had recently had it confirmed that the weight was, in fact, exactly as heavy as he had always feared.

He smelled terrible. Multiple witnesses across multiple incidents have confirmed this. Michael's 'alternative biology'—the result of having his internal organs replaced by a malfunctioning animatronic—produces an odor that has been variously described as 'decomposing,' 'chemical,' and 'like something decided to keep walking after it should have stopped.' Wario, who has a high tolerance for unpleasant smells due to his own personal hygiene philosophy, noted the smell but did not let it affect his assessment of Michael as a business contact.

'Pardon me,' Michael said. 'You ARE the owner of this location, yes?'

Wario confirmed that he was 'The Boss' and asked what Michael wanted, while simultaneously calculating whether Michael might be a buyer for the kitchen equipment.

Michael presented the Freddy mask—which he had apparently removed from Wario's van while Wario was inside the building. He then asked Wario to collect the remaining three masks from the other abandoned Fazbear locations and bring them to him.

'What's in it for me?' Wario asked.

'The goodness of your heart,' Michael replied.

The silence that followed lasted approximately four seconds. During this silence, Wario processed the concept of 'doing something for free,' found it structurally incompatible with his worldview, and filed it under 'things that other people do.'

'You're crazy if you think I'd agree, chump!' Wario declared, got in his van, and drove home.

Michael retrieved the mask from where Wario had left it on the roof of the van—Wario had put it there to free up his hands and forgotten it—and stood in the parking lot for another twenty minutes.

His journal entry for that night is brief: 'He walked past the Puppet. She let him. I need to understand why. I need him to keep going to these locations. I'll try again tomorrow.'

points_of_interest.name: Michael Afton: Background
points_of_interest.description:
Michael is William Afton's eldest son. He spent his adult life trying to undo his father's damage, a quest that took him to multiple Fazbear locations, cost him his original biological integrity, and ultimately brought him to the parking lot of the Hurricane flagship at midnight to ask a stranger to collect haunted masks for free.

Michael's deposition describes his motivation: 'My father created something. Not just the animatronics, not just the murders. He created a SYSTEM. A self-perpetuating cycle of suffering that used grief, guilt, and obsession as fuel. I spent decades trying to dismantle it from the inside. The problem is that the inside of this system is exactly where it does its best work. I needed someone from outside it. Someone it couldn't touch.'

He found Wario.

Of all the people in the Midlands who might have purchased the Fazbear franchise, of all the humans who might have walked into that parking lot that night, Michael found the one person who was structurally immune to recursive tragedy.

points_of_interest.name: What Michael Didn't Tell Wario (Night One)
points_of_interest.description:
Michael did not tell Wario that the masks contained bound spiritual energy. He did not explain what the masks were for. He did not mention his father. He did not mention that the last person to aggressively pursue the masks had been permanently traumatized by the process.

He asked for the masks and offered the goodness of Wario's heart as payment.

Waluigi considers this either the most poorly calibrated pitch in history or a deliberate strategy. Michael knew Wario had rejected the deal. Michael also knew that Wario was going to continue visiting the other locations for his own reasons. The masks were already being collected. Michael just needed Wario to bring them to him at the end.

He would try a different approach on Night Two.

sections.name: Night Two
sections.subtitle: The White Rabbit and the Double Deal
sections.overview:
Night Two took place at 'Abandoned Freddy's East'—the second largest location, which had operated under the name 'Freddy Fazbear's Family Diner' during its final years of operation before closing amid a health code crisis that the documentation describes as 'extensive' and that the former employees describe as 'the least of our problems.'

The building was smaller than the flagship, with lower ceilings and a claustrophobic layout that the designers had apparently intended to feel 'cozy' and that had instead created a maze of narrow corridors that were deeply unpleasant to navigate alone at midnight.

Wario navigated them cheerfully, making notes on salvageable equipment and ignoring the sounds of movement in the walls that the former night security guard—interviewed by phone from what he described as 'somewhere far away, don't try to find me'—had documented in seventeen separate incident reports as 'the thing in the walls, it's always the thing in the walls, I told them about the thing in the walls and they said it was probably rats, it is not rats.'

subsections.name: The Second Mask: Bonnie
subsections.description:
The Bonnie mask was located in a locked maintenance room in the east corridor. The lock had been broken—not forced, but disassembled from the inside, which was architecturally impossible given that the mechanism was designed to prevent exactly that.

Wario picked up the Bonnie mask, noted that it was 'purple, fancy, probably worth something,' added it to his bag, and moved on.

He did not note the temperature drop. He did not note the faint sound—described by former employees as 'like a guitar string being plucked, but wrong, wrong in a way that makes your teeth ache'—that accompanied the removal of Jeremy's mask from the location where it had sat for eleven years.

He noted that the maintenance room had a good utility sink that could be repurposed for his planned restaurant kitchen.

The ledger entry for this discovery: 'Sink: excellent. Keep. Purple mask: also keep.'

points_of_interest.name: Jeremy's Spirit: Night Two Manifestation
points_of_interest.description:
Jeremy—the child bound to Bonnie—was, of all the five spirits, the most overtly aggressive. Former security staff had documented 'the purple rabbit' as the first animatronic to leave the stage during nighttime hours and the most persistent pursuer of personnel.

When Wario removed the Bonnie mask, Jeremy's presence was measurable by equipment that Waluigi obtained from a Mages' Guild contact. The temperature in the east corridor dropped to approximately four degrees. The electromagnetic readings spiked. And then—nothing. The presence receded.

Jeremy did not pursue Wario.

Waluigi theorizes that the Marionette had communicated something to the other spirits between Night One and Night Two. The guardian had made a decision. The others were being asked to trust that decision. Jeremy, the aggressive one, held back.

This required considerable restraint from a spirit whose primary expression for decades had been aggression.

subsections.name: The Parking Lot: Vanny's Introduction
subsections.description:
Wario was locking up the east location when the White Rabbit appeared.

Vanny was wearing a full white rabbit costume—a custom piece that she had constructed herself, referencing the original Spring Bonnie design that William Afton had worn. The costume was well-made. Detailed. The kind of craftsmanship that suggested both skill and obsession.

She emerged from behind a delivery truck with the energy of someone who had rehearsed this entrance.

'Third verse, same as the first! I'm so happy, I could burst!' she announced.

Wario stared at her.

'Yeah, yeah. Shut your trap!' Wario replied, displaying the interpersonal warmth that has characterized all of his business relationships.

Vanny's opening strategy was charm. She complimented Wario, asked about his work, expressed enthusiasm for the animatronics. She spoke about Springtrap—the deteriorating suit containing her object of devotion—with an intensity that Wario found bewildering.

'He's the real backbone of all of this! He's so dreamy...'

'You sayin' this guy's more famous than me?' Wario asked.

This question derailed Vanny's prepared approach. She had not anticipated someone being MORE concerned with their own fame than with the supernatural horror she was describing. She pivoted, promised a reward 'WAY better than gold coins,' and disappeared.

Wario's ledger entry for Night Two's parking lot encounter: 'Lover-girl in rabbit suit wants the masks too. Two buyers now. This is the best deal I've ever made. WAHAHA.'

points_of_interest.name: Vanny: Background
points_of_interest.description:
Vanny's history with the Fazbear franchise began in childhood. She was one of countless children who grew up with the Fazbear brand—the birthday parties, the animatronics, the pizza. But where most children remembered Fazbear's with a mixture of nostalgia and vague unease, Vanny became obsessed with the darkness underneath.

She found the rumors. The incidents. The MCI. And then she found William Afton—not the man himself, who was technically dead and trapped in a decaying rabbit suit—but his presence, through recordings, through documentation, through the particular quality of cruelty that leaves marks on the world even after its source is gone.

She fell in love with an idea. The idea of someone who had discovered the secret technology—Remnant theory—that could bind a consciousness to matter. Someone who had proven, through the most terrible means imaginable, that death was not final. That will was strong enough to persist beyond biology.

She wanted to be loved by this idea. She wanted to restore it to full function. And she needed the masks' concentrated spiritual energy to do it.

Michael Afton, in his deposition, describes Vanny as 'exactly the kind of person my father created his mythology to attract.' William Afton had not set out to cultivate a devotee. But the system he created—the mystery, the horror, the sense that someone had discovered something fundamentally true about the universe—was precisely calibrated to capture a certain type of vulnerable, brilliant, isolated person.

Vanny was that person. And she was standing in a parking lot in a rabbit costume, trying to charm Wario into helping her.

points_of_interest.name: Wario's Double-Dealing Strategy Takes Shape
points_of_interest.description:
Wario went home on Night Two with two masks, two potential buyers, and a plan.

His ledger entry: 'Stinky guy wants masks. Lover-girl wants masks. Both want same masks. Solution: sell to BOTH. Collect from both. Then maybe take the trash-bots too. WAHAHA.'

This strategy—playing both factions against each other while secretly planning to sell the animatronics as a third revenue stream—was simultaneously the most cynical and the most effective approach to the situation. By refusing to commit to either side, Wario avoided being captured by either faction's narrative. He remained outside the system.

This was not strategy. This was greed. But greed, in this context, functioned as a kind of structural immunity.

sections.name: Night Three
sections.subtitle: The Horror Attraction and the Escalation
sections.overview:
Night Three took place at 'Fazbear's Fright: The Horror Attraction'—or rather, its ruins. Fazbear's Fright had been a brief, ill-advised attempt to monetize the Fazbear franchise's reputation for supernatural horror by converting one of the older locations into a legitimate haunted house attraction. It had operated for approximately six weeks before burning to the ground under circumstances that the fire marshal's report described as 'undetermined origin' and that three former employees described as 'obviously the rabbit suit, it was obviously always going to be the rabbit suit.'

The ruins were, Wario noted in his ledger, 'very dramatic. Good ambiance for a steak restaurant. Keep the scorched walls, customers love that.'

Waluigi notes that the Super Steakplex does not have scorched walls. Wario was eventually talked out of this aesthetic choice by Waluigi, who pointed out that health codes have opinions about fire damage in food service environments.

subsections.name: The Third Mask: Chica
subsections.description:
The Chica mask was in the ruins of the Fazbear's Fright gift shop, sitting in a display case that had somehow survived the fire intact. The glass was unbroken. The lock was functional. The case had been sitting in a burned building for years, and it looked as if it had been placed there yesterday.

Wario broke the glass with his elbow, picked up the mask, and noted that it was 'yellow, nice color, matches my hat.'

The former gift shop employee—the last person to have locked that case before the fire—had described the night of the fire in her incident report: 'I locked the Chica mask in the case because I didn't want it in the break room anymore. It kept showing up in the break room. I would move it to storage and it would be back in the break room. I locked it in the case and went home. That was the night the fire started.'

The mask had been waiting. For eleven years, in a burned building, it had been waiting in an intact glass case.

Wario picked it up and put it in his bag without comment.

points_of_interest.name: Susie's Spirit: The Kitchen Connection
points_of_interest.description:
Susie—the child bound to Chica—had behavioral patterns that puzzled the former security staff for years. Chica was sometimes passive, sometimes extremely hostile, with particular aggression around kitchen areas. The security staff had noted that Chica seemed to be 'looking for something' in the kitchen, returning to the same areas repeatedly.

Waluigi's theory: Susie's last memory before her death involved food. A meal, a birthday, something connected to eating and celebration. Chica—a character whose entire identity was built around food and cooking—was the vessel her spirit had been placed in because the resonance was strongest. And Chica kept returning to kitchens because Susie was still, on some level, looking for the last moment of ordinary happiness before everything went wrong.

Wario, who was actively planning a restaurant, spent considerable time in the kitchen areas of Fazbear's Fright. He did not encounter Susie's presence there. Waluigi suspects this is because Susie recognized that the man planning to convert her location into a steakhouse was, in his own way, trying to make a space for people to gather and eat.

Or perhaps Susie was simply tired of kitchens by that point. Eleven years is a long time to keep looking for something you can't find.

points_of_interest.name: Michael's Night Three Visit
points_of_interest.description:
Michael appeared in the ruins of Fazbear's Fright at approximately 1 AM—inside the building this time, rather than in the parking lot. Wario found him standing in what had been the main corridor, holding a lantern and looking at a burned wall mural.

'You know... I can't help but wonder what it is you're trying to accomplish here,' Michael said.

'Money,' Wario replied immediately.

Michael explained about emotional energy, about electronics acting as mediums, about the arcade cabinets from an earlier location that had apparently displayed relevant information. He spoke carefully, trying to give Wario enough context to understand the stakes without revealing so much that Wario would become frightened and stop.

Wario was not frightened. Wario was mildly interested in the arcade cabinet angle because arcade cabinets were potentially resaleable.

'These are just some slight problems with technology!' Wario declared. 'Don't think about it too hard, Einstein!'

Michael stared at him for a long moment, then nodded slowly. 'Regardless,' he said, 'you've done well. I hope to see you again tomorrow.'

His journal entry for Night Three: 'He told me not to think about it too hard. I have been thinking about nothing else for thirty years. I am not sure if I envy him or pity him. Possibly both. The Chica mask is collected. One more.'

sections.name: Night Four
sections.subtitle: Circus Baby's World and the MCI
sections.overview:
Night Four took place at the ruins of Circus Baby's Pizza World—William Afton's second-generation restaurant, built after the original Fazbear chain's first bankruptcy and designed to attract a new audience. It had operated for exactly one day before closing, under circumstances that the corporate records describe as 'a significant incident involving the primary animatronic unit' and that the former head technician describes as 'Baby ate a child, we saw it happen, we were told to say she malfunctioned, there was no malfunction, Baby worked exactly as William intended her to.'

Circus Baby's Pizza World was where Afton's second generation of animatronics—the Funtime units—had been stored and maintained. By the time Wario arrived, the building was partially collapsed but structurally accessible, and the storage areas in the basement were intact.

This was also the night Vanny told Wario about the Missing Children Incident.

subsections.name: The Fourth Mask: Foxy
subsections.description:
The Foxy mask was the most difficult to acquire. It was located in the deepest part of the basement storage—a sub-basement that wasn't on the building's official plans and that Wario found by following a draft of cold air through a cracked wall.

The sub-basement was the original Afton research space. Where William Afton had conducted his early Remnant theory experiments. The walls were covered in diagrams, equations, and notes that Waluigi, upon reviewing photographs Wario had taken on his phone, recognized as a precursor to the technology that the Regal Empire had been refining since 840 BF.

Wario photographed the walls because 'might be worth something.'

The Foxy mask was in a sealed container labeled 'DO NOT REMOVE—CONTAINMENT ACTIVE.' Wario removed it.

His ledger note: 'Orange fox mask. Very dramatic. Container said do not remove. Did anyway. WAHAHA.'

points_of_interest.name: Fritz's Spirit: The Final Approach
points_of_interest.description:
Fritz—the child bound to Foxy—had been the most physically aggressive of the five spirits. Foxy's sprint capability combined with a child's desperate rage had made 'Foxy coming out of Pirate's Cove' one of the most feared events in the security staff's experience across all locations.

When Wario opened the containment unit and removed the Foxy mask, the cold that descended on the sub-basement was different from the cold that had accompanied the other masks. This wasn't the cold of a haunted space. This was the cold of something that had been running for a long time and had finally, finally stopped.

Fritz's spirit didn't pursue Wario. Fritz's spirit, according to Michael Afton's deposition, 'just... stopped. For the first time in decades, Fritz just stopped. I could feel it from outside the building. Like a held breath finally released.'

Fritz had been running toward something for decades. He didn't know what. Just running, because stopping meant acknowledging that there was nothing to run toward.

Waluigi suspects that Charlie—the Marionette—had been telling the others something between each night. Preparing them. Helping them understand that the masks being collected was not a threat but an opportunity. That whatever came next might be better than what they had.

Fritz stopped running. And then Wario put the mask in his bag and went upstairs to photograph the research diagrams.

points_of_interest.name: The MCI Revelation: Vanny's Failed Horror
points_of_interest.description:
Vanny appeared in the Circus Baby's parking lot with what Wario later described as 'a LOT of attitude and a speech she definitely practiced.'

She told him about the Missing Children Incident. The murders. The body disposal. The decades of haunting. She delivered this information with the cadence of someone who had been waiting for the right moment to deploy a devastating revelation.

Wario listened.

And then he said: 'Ghosts? Yeah, I've dealt with these trash-bots before. They used to bicker about REVENGE or something.'

Vanny's response: 'WHAT.'

The silence that followed was, by multiple accounts, extraordinary. Vanny had prepared this speech. She had spent years cultivating her understanding of the Fazbear horror. She had timed the pauses. She had modulated her voice for maximum effect.

And Wario had reduced it to 'oh yeah, I know about the ghosts, they're annoying but manageable.'

'B-But you said you didn't—' Vanny began.

'There are just SOME supernatural phenomena in the world that just can't be explained!' Wario declared, with the energy of someone closing a business meeting. 'Don't think TOO hard about these things, Einstein!'

Vanny left. She had been preparing that speech for years. Wario had neutralized it in forty seconds by being Wario.

Her journal entry for Night Four, recovered during her subsequent psychiatric evaluation: 'He KNOWS. He already knew. And he doesn't CARE. How does someone not CARE? How is that POSSIBLE? What IS he?'

Waluigi finds this the most accurate summary of Wario anyone has ever written.

sections.name: Night Five
sections.subtitle: The Pizzaplex and the Confrontation
sections.overview:
Night Five took place at the Pizzaplex—the most recent and most architecturally ambitious of the Fazbear locations. A multi-story entertainment complex that had attempted to modernize the franchise for contemporary audiences, featuring glamrock-themed animatronics, advanced security systems, and an underground maintenance network that was, according to the former head of security, 'either the best-designed utility space I've ever seen or the worst-designed containment facility, and I can never figure out which.'

The Pizzaplex had been closed for three years. It was also the largest of Wario's acquired locations and the one with the most potentially salvageable modern equipment. Wario arrived with a larger truck.

It was also the night that Michael and Vanny were both present simultaneously, and they were arguing with each other before Wario even got out of the vehicle.

subsections.name: The Glamrock Animatronics
subsections.description:
The Pizzaplex's animatronics were a different generation from the original five. Glamrock Freddy, Glamrock Chica, Montgomery Gator, and Roxanne Wolf were the public-facing performers—newer suits, more advanced mechanics, celebrity-themed designs that had been popular in the franchise's final operational period.

These suits were not occupied in the same way the originals had been. No murdered children. No Remnant bindings. But they had been present in a space saturated with Afton's legacy technology, and they had accumulated what Michael Afton called 'residual resonance'—not spirits, but impressions. Echoes of the emotional energy that the Fazbear franchise had generated over decades.

Wario evaluated them as: 'Fancy robots. Fancy. Very fancy. Worth a lot. Take all of them.'

He was not wrong about their value. The Pizzaplex units were ultimately the most technologically advanced of the animatronics he collected, and they fetched the highest prices in the subsequent sale to the Empire's shell companies.

The Glamrock units are now partially incorporated into Iron Legion psychological warfare and crowd control systems. Roxanne Wolf's confidence-projection algorithms—designed to make audiences feel excited and engaged—were adapted for Imperial propaganda broadcasts. Glamrock Chica's social facilitation programming was incorporated into Empire public relations infrastructure.

Wario sold a rock band to the fascists. They are now the fascists' house band. Waluigi finds this deeply, specifically awful.

points_of_interest.name: The Sun and Moon Attendants
points_of_interest.description:
Two anomalous entities in the Pizzaplex's daycare area—a sun-themed figure called 'Sunny' and a moon-themed figure called 'Moony' (designations assigned by former staff; their official names were 'Sun' and 'Moon')—represented a unique design: a single animatronic that shifted between two distinct personalities and physical configurations based on the lighting conditions.

Sunny was cheerful, energetic, and designed to engage children during daycare hours. Moony was subdued, rule-enforcing, and designed to manage children during nap time. The transition between them was triggered by light levels.

Wario encountered Sunny in the daycare area at approximately 12:30 AM. The lights were off. He was therefore greeted by Moony.

'You are not supposed to be here,' Moony said.

'I own the place,' Wario replied.

There was a pause.

'...You own the place,' Moony confirmed.

'That's right.'

'...Okay,' Moony said, and stepped aside.

Wario's ledger: 'Sun/moon robot. Weird. Does what it's told when you tell it who's boss. Good work ethic. Maybe hire for the Steakplex.'

The Sun/Moon animatronic was eventually sold to the Empire shell company along with the others, which Waluigi considers a genuine loss. It was one of the few Fazbear entities that Wario seemed to genuinely like.

subsections.name: The Night Five Confrontation
subsections.description:
Michael and Vanny were in the Pizzaplex parking lot when Wario arrived, and they were not getting along.

Vanny: 'If you knew what was good for you, you'd leave him to ME!'
Michael: 'Under what circumstances? You know neither of you should be handling that—that THING!'
Vanny: 'What, so YOU can boss him around? Fat chance!'

Wario got out of his truck, assessed the situation, and announced: 'You guys BEAT IT, or I'll show you both a BEATIN'!'

Both of them immediately redirected their attention to Wario, which is a pattern Waluigi has observed across multiple Wario-adjacent incidents. Wario has an ability to command focus in chaotic situations that is entirely unrelated to any legitimate authority or tactical capability. He simply speaks with such absolute conviction about his own importance that other parties recalibrate.

Michael introduced himself properly for the first time: 'My name is Michael. Nice to meet you.'

Vanny also introduced herself more directly, dispensing with the coy White Rabbit persona.

Both of them then explained their competing claims on the situation, essentially undoing each other's arguments in real time. Michael explained the danger of Springtrap. Vanny explained why the danger was actually the point. Michael explained why Vanny was wrong. Vanny explained why Michael was boring.

Wario listened to all of this and concluded: 'Since they're fighting over them, maybe they're even more VALUABLE than I took them for!'

His ledger entry: 'Both chumps showed up. Both want the trash-bots. Both want the masks. Plan: sell to both. Take the robots for myself too. Best business week of my life.'

points_of_interest.name: Michael's Warning Story
points_of_interest.description:
During the Night Five confrontation, Michael told a story. It was intended as a warning.

'Let me tell you about a friend I once knew,' he said. 'He was a bit rough around the edges, made plenty of mistakes... but he had a good heart. Always wanted to do the right thing. And I liked that about him. Yet he was also horribly stubborn. He had this hare-brained plan, and he insisted he do it all himself. His cross to bear, so he said. He became obsessed. Fully submerged in his work. Maybe because he was in over his head, or maybe just to try and drown out his guilt... But soon, he began meddling with forces far outside his control.'

Michael paused.

'Do you want to know what happened to him?'

Another pause.

'He turned up dead. His brains splattered across the walls of his study.'

Wario: 'Challenge me? That stinker? I'm the best at ANYTHING! I'm not scared!'

Michael had been describing himself. Or possibly his brother. Or possibly their father. The story was true regardless of whose story it was.

Wario was not the audience for this warning. Wario cannot be warned by tragedy because Wario does not believe tragedy is something that happens to him specifically. Tragedy happens to other people. Wario happens to everyone else.

points_of_interest.name: Vanny's Suspicion
points_of_interest.description:
On Night Five, Vanny confronted Wario about his true identity.

'Don't play dumb with me! I KNOW you're up to something!'

She had been watching him for five nights. She had seen him navigate spaces that should have been hostile to him, acquire objects that should have been inaccessible to him, and respond to supernatural horror with the emotional register of a man evaluating furniture.

'Some guy just shows up someday, and somehow knows exactly what to grab, and exactly how to deal with it? No! You're... you're someone else! I dunno who, but I know you are!'

Wario's defense: 'I'm pretty powerful, lover-girl. Not to mention, I... ALMOST got nothing to hide, I wouldn't lie to you, would I?'

The 'almost' is doing considerable work in that sentence. Wario was lying—he was concealing his identity as 'The Boss' because 'I can't be seen doing a minimum-wage job,' as he put it to Waluigi afterward. He was not Wario the famous WarioWare founder and occasional villain. He was 'The Boss,' a completely normal businessman with no supernatural connections whatsoever.

Vanny was not entirely convinced. But she also could not identify what specifically he was hiding, because what he was hiding was 'that he's embarrassed to be working night shifts,' which was not the sinister secret she was looking for.

sections.name: Night Six
sections.subtitle: The Phone Call, the Files, and the Discovery
sections.overview:
Night Six was the pivotal night. Not because of what Wario did in the building—his salvage operations at the fifth location were routine by his standards—but because of what happened afterward, in the Hurricane flagship parking lot, during a confrontation that was supposed to be the climax of the Michael/Vanny conflict and instead became a referendum on Wario's business ethics and his relationship with his mother.

It was also the night Wario discovered the secret bunker.

Wario arrived at the final salvage location—a smaller, newer Fazbear outlet that had operated briefly under the name 'Bonnie Bowl' before the franchise's final collapse—at 11 PM. He completed his salvage assessment in record time because there was very little to assess: the location had been picked over by previous investigators and contained almost nothing of value except a decent sound system and a very good pasta recipe laminated to the kitchen wall that Wario photographed for personal use.

He returned to the Hurricane flagship for the final confrontation.

subsections.name: The Confrontation: Both Factions, One Parking Lot
subsections.description:
Michael and Vanny were waiting. They had apparently agreed, in Wario's absence, to stop arguing with each other long enough to make a unified demand: choose a side.

Michael: 'Our goals are fundamentally incompatible. If this was your way of finding a compromise between us, I'm afraid it was all in vain. If you want to do any good with what you've collected here... you'll need to choose between us.'

Vanny: 'You've got two choices here! You can go along with me... or you can bore yourself to death with whatever THAT guy's got planned.'

Wario began reading corporate documents.

This was not the response either of them had anticipated. Michael had prepared a measured appeal to Wario's apparently non-existent sense of moral responsibility. Vanny had prepared an attractive offer involving unspecified rewards. Both approaches required Wario to be paying attention to them.

Wario was reading about tax liabilities.

points_of_interest.name: Wario's Mother Calls
points_of_interest.description:
At approximately 1:15 AM, Wario's phone rang.

The caller ID displayed: 'MAMA.'

Wario answered.

What followed, from external observation, was: Wario listened for approximately forty-five seconds. Then Wario screamed ('WAAAAAAAAAAHH!!'). Then Wario said, very quietly and with evident sincerity, 'Sorry. Yeah, I love you too, Ma. Bye-bye.'

Wario hung up.

Vanny: 'Is, um, is everything alright?'

Wario: 'NO! EVERYTHING IS NOT ALRIGHT! I'VE BEEN SCAMMED! SWINDLED! HOODWINKED!'

Wario's mother had apparently been reviewing the corporate documents from the Fazbear acquisition—Donna, as Waluigi learned during his phone interview, has a background in bookkeeping and periodically reviews her son's business acquisitions because 'otherwise he misses things'—and had found reference to the hidden facility.

The corporate documents, buried under years of deliberate obfuscation, contained evidence of a secondary property: a bunker in the woods seven kilometers from the Hurricane flagship, registered under a shell company that had been dissolved before the bankruptcy proceedings. The previous owners had concealed it. The auction house had not known to include it. Wario had purchased the Fazbear franchise and everything connected to it, including a secret facility that no one had told him about.

A secret facility. Stuffed with animatronics.

VALUABLE animatronics.

The ledger entry captures it: 'THE JERKS WHO SOLD ME THE COMPANY WERE HIDING MILLIONS IN PROPERTY RIGHT UNDER MY NOSE. THERE IS A BUNKER. THE BUNKER HAS ROBOTS. I AM GOING TO BE RRRRRRRICH.'

points_of_interest.name: Michael's Reaction
points_of_interest.description:
Michael Afton, upon hearing about the secret bunker, experienced what his deposition describes as 'a wave of recognition and dread.'

He knew about the bunker. He had known it existed but had never been able to locate it. It was where his father had stored the second generation of Funtime animatronics—Circus Baby, Ballora, Funtime Freddy, Funtime Foxy—designed for acquisition rather than entertainment. The most dangerous technology William Afton had created, in a hidden facility, now about to be stumbled upon by the most financially motivated person in the Midlands.

'If you cared about what REALLY mattered, you wouldn't have bought this company in the first place!' he told Wario.

Wario was already in his truck, heading for the bunker's coordinates.

Michael followed.

subsections.name: The Secret Bunker: First Look
subsections.description:
The bunker was accessed through what appeared to be a maintenance shed seven kilometers into the woods east of Hurricane. The shed contained a staircase. The staircase descended thirty meters. At the bottom was a facility that William Afton had built over approximately fifteen years of clandestine construction, funded through the Fazbear franchise's operating profits.

The facility contained:
- Circus Baby: A red-and-white clown-themed animatronic with advanced child-interaction programming, ice cream dispensing capability, and—unknown to Wario—an interior cavity designed to store a small human body. Circus Baby's 'accident' on the first day of Circus Baby's Pizza World had not been a malfunction. She had worked exactly as Afton intended.
- Ballora: A ballet-dancer animatronic with fluid movement algorithms decades ahead of her time, enhanced audio processing that allowed her to track targets by sound, and 'eyes always closed' design that Afton had implemented because eyes-open tracking was 'too obvious.'
- Funtime Freddy: A blue-and-white variant of the original Freddy with a puppet companion called 'BonBon' that could detach and operate independently. Advanced voice mimicry capable of replicating any voice from a brief audio sample.
- Funtime Foxy: A pink variant of the original Foxy with a spotlight system, performance projection capabilities, and movement that could be rendered nearly silent through dampening mechanisms.
- Multiple prototype units: Partially assembled, partially functional, representing experiments that Afton had not lived to complete.

Wario walked through the facility with his phone's camera running, narrating his assessment: 'Ice cream making, ballerina dancing, voice mimickry [sic]... They're basically WALKING stacks of GOLD!!'

He was right. He was not right for the reasons he thought he was right, but he was right.

points_of_interest.name: Circus Baby: The Most Dangerous Animatronic
points_of_interest.description:
Circus Baby was William Afton's masterwork. She was built to attract children with her cheerful appearance, engage them with her ice cream dispensing, and then—when the opportunity arose—acquire them. She had worked once, at the opening of Circus Baby's Pizza World, when she had found and used the interior cavity that Afton had built into her chest.

Afterward, she had been stored in the bunker. Afton had planned to use her again but had been trapped in Springtrap before he could do so.

By the time Wario found her, Circus Baby's spirit had been modified significantly by years of isolation and the presence of other entities in the facility. The 'acquisition programming' was still present but dormant—she had not had a child to acquire in decades, and the hunger had transmuted into something quieter and stranger.

Wario evaluated her as: 'Red and white. Classy. Very fancy. Must be worth a lot. Take.'

He patted her on the head.

Circus Baby, according to Michael Afton's deposition, 'looked at him for a moment and then just... stood there. She didn't activate any of the acquisition protocols. She just stood there.' Michael found this remarkable. Circus Baby had attacked people for approaching her less directly than Wario just had.

The Marionette had communicated something to ALL of the units in Afton's network. Not just the originals. All of them. The guardian's reach extended further than Michael had understood.

points_of_interest.name: The Afton Research Archive
points_of_interest.description:
Deeper in the bunker, past the animatronic storage, was a room that Wario described in his ledger as 'filing cabinets, boring, skip.' He did not skip it. He photographed everything, because 'might be worth something.'

The room contained William Afton's complete research archive: every Remnant theory document, every experiment record, every correspondence with outside parties who had provided funding and resources. The complete history of how a children's entertainer had developed soul-binding technology derived from alien research and used it to murder children.

It also contained the Talbert Files.

Waluigi has seen the photographs. He has not seen the original documents—those remain in the bunker, which is now sealed under Guild jurisdiction. But the photographs, combined with the summary notes Wario made in WARIO'S COOKBOOK, paint a picture of an archive that documents not just the Fazbear crimes but their connection to a network of researchers, funders, and institutions that extends far beyond any single man's obsession.

The Talbert Files specifically reference 'pre-cataclysm imperial research protocols' as the basis for Remnant theory, confirming the Shroob connection. They also reference 'the Agony'—a weaponized, concentrated form of the emotional energy that Remnant theory manipulated—and note that 'full weaponization remains theoretical but achievable given sufficient investment.'

The Empire's shell companies paid extra for the Afton archive. They knew what they were buying.

sections.name: Night Seven
sections.subtitle: Cassidy, The Golden Future, and the Resolution
sections.overview:
Night Seven was supposed to be the resolution of everything. Michael had his plan. Vanny had her counter-plan. The masks were collected, the factions were positioned, and the climax of a decades-long supernatural conflict was approaching its conclusion.

Wario went into the bunker to look for the most expensive robots.

What he found was not the most expensive robots. What he found was a child who had been waiting thirty years for someone to give her permission to leave.

Waluigi has reviewed the account of Night Seven more times than any other element of this incident. He has read Wario's ledger entry seventeen times. He has read Michael Afton's deposition account of what he felt from outside the bunker four times. He has reviewed the Mages' Guild's energy readings from the bunker at the moment of resolution three times.

Every time, Waluigi comes to the same conclusion: the most effective supernatural crisis resolution in the recorded history of the Doughnut World was accomplished by a man who did it while planning where to put the bar.

subsections.name: The Golden Freddy Chamber
subsections.description:
The Golden Freddy suit—Cassidy's animatronic—was not stored with the others. It was in a separate chamber at the very back of the bunker, behind a door that had been welded shut from the outside.

The welding had been done from the outside. Whoever had sealed this room had done so to contain what was inside.

Wario burned through the weld with an acetylene torch he had brought for exactly this kind of situation ('Always bring a torch,' his ledger notes, 'you never know when something needs cutting open') and entered the chamber.

The Golden Freddy suit was in the center of the room, seated in a chair. The suit was deteriorating—fabric worn, stuffing exposed, one eye missing. But the presence inside it was anything but deteriorating.

Cassidy had been the first to be bound and would be the last to let go. She had spent decades maintaining the connection between the five spirits, anchoring them to their suits and to their purpose. She was the reason the haunting had persisted as long as it had. She was also the reason it had remained coherent—without her anchor, the other four would have diffused into background spiritual noise within years of the original bindings.

She had held them together. She had kept them focused. She had sustained their purpose when grief and time would otherwise have eroded it.

And she was terrified of what happened when that purpose was fulfilled.

points_of_interest.name: The Conversation
points_of_interest.description:
Wario entered the chamber, saw the deteriorating golden bear suit, and made a note about its salvage value ('Very worn. Maybe decorative only.'). Then the suit's remaining eye moved to track him.

Wario pointed his flashlight at it.

The eye looked back.

'...I'm scared,' a voice said. Not from a speaker. Not from any mechanical system. From somewhere inside the suit that was not mechanical at all.

'I don't want to lose everything we have.'

Wario lowered his flashlight. He looked at the suit for a moment. Then he said:

'Hey, listen up, kid. I'm begging you to stop that complainin', it gets on my nerves!'

What followed was, by Wario's account, about ten minutes of conversation. By the energy readings the Mages' Guild later recovered, it was closer to forty. Time moves differently in spaces with significant spiritual presence.

Wario told Cassidy about the Super Steakplex. He told her about the Golden Future—the signature dish he was planning, steak with gold leaf, named after the color of the suit she was trapped in. He told her that whatever was next had to be better than a pizza place. He told her that even selfish people like him found value in 'some pesky chumps alongside you.'

He told her to invest in the future.

Cassidy: 'You're right. It... it isn't right to keep them all down here. It isn't right to keep myself down here.'

Wario's phone rang. His mother.

'Bye-bye!' Wario told Cassidy. 'And have a rotten day!'

He answered the phone and walked out of the chamber.

Behind him, thirty years of sustained grief released its hold. Five children who had been trapped in mechanical bodies since before most people currently alive in the Midlands were born found something they had been denied their entire afterlife: permission to stop.

The release was measurable. The Mages' Guild, monitoring supernatural energy levels across the Midlands, recorded a significant dissipation event at 1:47 AM on the 21st of Autumn's End. Their documentation describes it as 'an unexplained but benign release of bound spiritual energy, origin unknown.' Waluigi knows the origin. The origin is garlic breath and business advice.

points_of_interest.name: Michael's Experience
points_of_interest.description:
Michael Afton was standing outside the bunker when it happened. He had been trying to find a way in—the welded door had defeated his tools—and had been reduced to sitting against the exterior wall and waiting.

At 1:47 AM, he felt it.

His deposition: 'It was like... a sound stopping that you had been hearing for so long you forgot it was there. A tension releasing that had become so familiar it felt like the natural state of things. I didn't know what to feel. I had been working toward this for so long that I wasn't sure what came after.

And then Wario came out of the bunker talking about his restaurant.

'The garlic butter is the key,' he was saying into his phone. 'You tell them it's imported, they'll pay more. Yes, Mama. I know. I love you too. Bye.'

I don't think he knew what he had done. I don't think he still fully understands what he did. He walked into a room where a child had been waiting for thirty years, told her to stop waiting, and walked back out.

I've been trying to do that for my entire adult life.

He did it in forty minutes.

I don't know whether to be grateful or furious. I am choosing grateful. It is the better use of whatever time I have remaining.'

points_of_interest.name: Vanny's Collapse
points_of_interest.description:
Vanny was also outside the bunker when the release occurred. She had been attempting to negotiate with Michael—some last-ditch effort to acquire at least one mask before Wario made his decision—when the energy dissipation hit.

She felt Springtrap go dark.

For years, Vanny had maintained a kind of spiritual connection to Springtrap's presence—not a true link, but a sensitivity to the emotional energy that the suit radiated. She had used this sensitivity to track the masks, to understand the Fazbear spiritual network, to sustain her belief in William Afton's continued existence as something more than a deteriorating corpse.

When Cassidy released her hold, the spiritual energy that had been sustaining the entire Fazbear haunting dissipated. Including whatever residual presence had been clinging to Springtrap.

Springtrap became a suit. Just a suit. Deteriorating yellow fabric and broken mechanics, nothing inside.

Vanny sat down on the ground outside the bunker and didn't get up for a while.

Wario, emerging from the bunker while still on the phone with his mother, stepped around her.

'Watch it, lover-girl, you're in my way,' he said, and continued to his truck.

subsections.name: The Resolution: Arrests, Sales, and a Restaurant
subsections.description:
The events following the release were practical rather than dramatic.

Wario called the authorities and reported both Michael and Vanny for trespassing on his property. This was petty. It was also technically accurate—both of them had been on his property, without permission, for seven nights. Michael was detained briefly and released. Vanny was held and eventually received psychiatric intervention.

Wario spent the rest of the night cataloging the bunker's contents.

Over the following two weeks, he sold everything. The original location animatronics to one buyer. The Funtime units to another. The Glamrock units to a third. The research archive to a fourth. He did not know that all four buyers were fronts for the same Regal Empire acquisition division. The shell company structure was very good.

Total proceeds: 27,000 gold coins, plus the Mages' Guild's hush money payment of 5,000 gold coins.

Total investment: 400 gold coins.

Net profit: 31,600 gold coins.

Wario used 18,000 coins to renovate the Hurricane flagship into the Super Steakplex. He invested 8,000 in WarioWare Inc. development. He spent 4,000 on a vacation. He gave 600 to his mother because she asked and he loves her.

The remaining 1,000 he keeps in a safe labeled 'EMERGENCY PASTA FUND.'

The Super Steakplex opened three months after Night Seven. The signature dish—The Golden Future—has been on the menu since opening day: a thirty-two-ounce ribeye with garlic butter and edible gold leaf, served on a plate shaped like a star, priced at forty gold coins.

The name was Wario's idea. He does not remember why he chose it. He does not remember the conversation in the golden chamber. He does not remember Cassidy asking if she would see him again.

Waluigi remembers, because Waluigi photographed the relevant ledger pages before Wario could edit them.

points_of_interest.name: Michael's Departure
points_of_interest.description:
After his release from detention, Michael Afton returned to the Hurricane flagship one final time. Wario was there, overseeing renovation work on what would become the Super Steakplex.

Michael stood in the parking lot for a while. Then he went inside.

Wario was in the main dining area, directing workers on stage demolition. Michael stood in the doorway and watched.

'You're tearing down the stage,' Michael said.

'Table space,' Wario replied. 'Stages don't pay rent. Tables do.'

Michael nodded. 'Good,' he said. 'That's good.'

He left. He has not been seen in the Midlands since. Michael Afton's current whereabouts are unknown, which is consistent with his entire documented history of appearing when needed and disappearing when the work is done.

Waluigi suspects he is still out there. Michael has proven difficult to permanently conclude.

points_of_interest.name: The Ledger Entry for Night Seven
points_of_interest.description:
Wario's final ledger entry for the Fazbear Incident:

'NITE 7: Found the gold bear robot in the back room. Very worn. Spoke to it about business. Made sense of things. Sold everything. 27k coins. Guild paid extra to keep quiet. Did not sign anything. Restaurant opens in 3 months. Menu: steak, garlic bread, the golden future. Name: SUPER STEAKPLEX. WAHAHA. Stinky guy and lover-girl got arrested. Serves them right. Note: tell Waluigi nothing.'

Waluigi was told everything anyway, because Wario had left his ledger on the table at the Super Steakplex's soft opening dinner and Waluigi photographed forty-seven pages while Wario was in the kitchen arguing about the garlic bread temperature.

Note: the garlic bread temperature was fine. Wario was wrong. The bread was perfect.

sections.waluigi_analysis:
Waluigi has spent more time analyzing the Seven Nights than any other incident in this encyclopedia, and the conclusions are both simple and infuriating.

Night One established that Wario was immune to the Fazbear system—the Marionette recognized it and opened the door.

Nights Two through Five demonstrated that this immunity extended to both human factions—Michael's appeals to moral responsibility could not reach Wario, and Vanny's psychological manipulation found no purchase.

Night Six revealed the bunker, which was the practical consequence of Wario's immune position: he could collect the technology without being consumed by what it represented.

Night Seven completed the circuit. Cassidy needed someone who could enter her chamber without bringing the weight of the Fazbear tragedy with them. Every other person who had entered the orbit of this franchise had been contaminated by it. Wario arrived clean, spoke simply, and left.

The five children are at peace. This is good.

The Iron Legion has better robots because Wario sold them the technology. This is bad.

The Talbert Files are in WARIO'S COOKBOOK. This is complicated.

The Super Steakplex serves excellent garlic bread. This is... fine. Waluigi will not comment further on the garlic bread.

WAH.

outcome: All five child spirits released on Night Seven following Wario's conversation with Cassidy. Michael Afton achieved his life's goal and departed. Vanny received psychiatric intervention. Both arrested for trespassing. Advanced animatronics sold to Regal Empire shell companies for 27,000 gold coins. Afton research archive including Remnant theory documents acquired by Empire. Mages' Guild paid 5,000 coins for Wario's silence; Wario did not sign the NDA. Hurricane flagship converted into the Super Steakplex. The Golden Future added to menu. Technology chain from Shroob Vim harvesting to Iron Legion combat systems now complete.

name: The First Glazed Congress
title: The Day the World Tried to Talk Instead of Fight
location: Woohoo Hooniversity Grand Assembly Hall, Beanbean Kingdom — first session; rotating thereafter
type: Diplomatic Foundation / Multi-National Assembly / Constitutional Convention / Historical Accident
status: Ongoing — the Glazed Congress continues to meet annually, continues to argue about everything, and continues to produce legislation that satisfies nobody completely, which Waluigi considers proof that it is working correctly
imageCaption: The official founding portrait shows forty-three delegates in formal attire arranged around the Woohoo Hooniversity's central dais. Waluigi is visible in the back row, slightly too tall, wearing a hat that was not dress code compliant. Three separate delegates attempted to have him removed. All three failed.
