summary: The Glazed Congress was founded on 14th Bloomtide, 1026 BF, in the Woohoo Hooniversity Grand Assembly Hall of the Beanbean Kingdom, one year after the Blorbs Crisis demonstrated conclusively that no single nation could manage dimensional threats, pandemic events, or rogue actors operating across borders without some form of coordinated international response. The Congress takes its name from the shape of the world itself — the Great Doughnut, whose glazed ring connects all nations whether they want to be connected or not. To meet 'around the glaze' means to meet as representatives of the whole world, acknowledging that the hole in the center connects everyone regardless of political preference. The founding session was called by Queen Bean of the Beanbean Kingdom, seconded by the Pokémon League, and attended by representatives of thirty-seven recognized nations and factions. Six notable absences were recorded, the most significant being Equestria, whose Solar Sovereign declined to send delegates on the grounds that a multi-species deliberative body represented 'an affront to natural order.' The Beanbean Kingdom's position as convenor was not accidental — Queen Bean had no territorial ambitions, no military history of conquest, trade relationships with most known nations, and the diplomatic credibility that comes from being the kingdom that LOST to Fawful's first incursion and survived anyway. She also had the Woohoo Hooniversity, whose grand assembly hall was the only venue on the Doughnut large enough to seat delegates from forty-plus nations without requiring anyone to share a chair with their historical enemies. Mostly. The founding session lasted eleven days. It produced the Charter of the Glazed Ring, established the Congress's structure and voting system, admitted thirty-seven founding members, created the position of Secretary-Convener, and generated approximately four thousand pages of procedural argument that Waluigi has read in its entirety and found deeply clarifying about why the world is the way it is. Waluigi was present for all eleven days. Waluigi was sixteen years old. Waluigi should not have been there. Waluigi was there anyway, and the rules had not been written yet, so nobody could legally remove him. Waluigi considers this the proudest achievement of his early life. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is writing this entry with the full understanding that he is not an impartial observer of the Glazed Congress's founding. Waluigi was THERE. Waluigi watched the Charter being drafted. Waluigi heard the arguments, saw the walkouts, witnessed the moments where the entire project nearly collapsed over procedural disagreements about whether ghosts counted as a recognized national constituency. Waluigi's perspective on the Congress is therefore biased in the specific way that firsthand experience always produces bias — Waluigi knows what actually happened rather than what the official record claims happened, and those two things are different in ways that matter.

Waluigi will document both.

## Why It Took 146 Years

The Chaos Heart Crisis of 880 BF nearly destroyed all existence. Every nation on the Doughnut was threatened. The Void that Count Bleck unleashed did not respect borders, diplomatic relationships, or the carefully maintained fiction that one nation's problems were not another nation's problem.

And yet the Glazed Congress was not founded until 1026 BF — 146 years after the crisis that theoretically motivated it.

Waluigi considers this deeply revealing about how institutions actually form. The lesson of the Chaos Heart Crisis was clear: coordinated multi-national response is essential for existential threats. The political reality of the century following the crisis was also clear: no nation wanted to be coordinated with nations it had territorial disputes with, historical grievances against, ideological conflicts with, or economic competition from.

In other words, everyone agreed coordination was necessary in the abstract and impossible in the specific.

The Chaos Heart Crisis produced fourteen separate proposals for international cooperation over the following century. Fourteen proposals. All fourteen failed at the negotiation stage because:

- The Regal Empire insisted any international body recognize their territorial claims in the Midlands, which the Mushroom Kingdom and several other nations refused to do
- The Land of Mordor's representatives demanded that the concept of 'recognized nation' not require functioning civilian governance, which most other delegates found alarming for reasons they found difficult to explain politely
- The Internet Federation proposed that digital nations receive equal representation with physical ones, which produced three years of philosophical argument about what 'physical' meant
- The Pokémon League wanted Pokémon to have individual voting rights rather than being represented through their trainers, which opened a debate about non-human personhood that nobody was prepared to resolve
- The Mushroom Kingdom's Regency refused to participate in any body that might pass resolutions about their internal politics, which everyone found hypocritical given that the Regency was actively lobbying other nations about their internal politics
- The Beanbean Kingdom proposed a sensible framework in 943 BF that everyone agreed was excellent and nobody could agree to implement

The 146-year gap between crisis and congress is not institutional failure. It is institutional reality. Coordinated action requires trust. Trust requires time. Time requires surviving the period between the crisis that demonstrated necessity and the maturity to act on that necessity.

The final catalyst was the Blorbs Crisis of 1018-1019 BF combined with Fawful's territorial seizures. The Blorbs crossed borders. A manufactured pandemic does not respect diplomatic boundaries. Fawful occupied Mushroom Kingdom territory while simultaneously threatening Beanbean trade routes and destabilizing the border regions where multiple national jurisdictions overlapped. The crisis was not contained. The crisis SPREAD. And not one of the kingdom's emergency responses had any mechanism for coordination with neighboring nations.

Five years of post-crisis diplomatic furore followed. Queen Bean — who had managed the Beanbean Kingdom's response to both the Blorbs and Fawful's incursion with what Waluigi considers remarkable competence — sent personal letters to forty-seven world leaders in 1025 BF proposing what she called 'a conversation.' Not a treaty. Not a binding commitment. Just a conversation, in her university, with her pastry chefs providing refreshments.

Thirty-seven responded positively. Nine declined. One — Equestria's Solar Sovereign — sent a letter expressing what diplomatic translators described as 'politely worded contempt.'

Queen Bean scheduled the conversation for Bloomtide 1026 BF and called it the First Assembly Around the Glaze.

The name stuck. The conversation became a congress. The congress became an institution.

And Waluigi — sixteen years old, already six feet tall, already convinced that the world's problems required his personal attention — read about the assembly in the Mushroom Kingdom Gazette, borrowed traveling money from Wario (still owed, disputed, compound interest), and showed up at Woohoo Hooniversity's front gate three days before the session began.

## How Waluigi Got In

Waluigi told the gate officials he was the Mushroom Kingdom's junior delegate.

This was not true. The Mushroom Kingdom had not designated junior delegates. The Mushroom Kingdom had, in fact, designated TWO senior delegates — Toadsworth the Elder and a Regency official named Parveth Inkwell — and had not contemplated the existence of a sixteen-year-old who would show up at the Beanbean border claiming junior delegate status for a position that did not exist.

The gate officials checked their list. Waluigi was not on it. Waluigi pointed out that the junior delegate list had not been submitted yet because junior delegate positions had not been formally created. The gate officials consulted their supervisors. The supervisors consulted the organizing committee. The organizing committee consulted Queen Bean's chief of staff, a Beanish woman named Malvanie Cresswick who had spent thirty years managing diplomatic events and had, in her own words, 'never encountered this specific problem before.'

Waluigi was told to wait while they determined whether junior delegates existed. Waluigi waited. Waluigi also introduced himself to every delegate who entered the gate during the three hours he waited, explained his interpretation of the Chaos Heart Crisis's dimensional implications, and offered unsolicited analysis of the proposed charter framework that three delegates later admitted was 'irritating but not wrong.'

Malvanie Cresswick returned and told Waluigi that junior delegate positions did not exist.

Waluigi asked if they were prohibited.

Cresswick said they were not prohibited because nobody had thought to prohibit them because nobody had imagined they needed to prohibit them.

Waluigi said he would like to attend as an observer then.

Cresswick said observers were permitted but could not speak.

Waluigi agreed to this condition. Waluigi did not keep this condition. Within forty minutes of the first session, Waluigi had raised a procedural point about the voting weight formula that the assembled delegates could not immediately refute. The chair — Queen Bean herself — allowed the point. Toadsworth the Elder looked at Waluigi with an expression that Waluigi has treasured ever since. Toadsworth recognized Waluigi. Toadsworth was appalled. Toadsworth could not remove Waluigi without disrupting the session.

Waluigi attended all eleven days.

At the end of the founding session, the Charter of the Glazed Ring was signed by thirty-seven delegates. Waluigi's name appears in the witness registry — not as a signatory, because he was not a recognized delegate, but as 'W. Waluigi, Observer, Mushroom Kingdom (disputed status).'

Waluigi considers 'disputed status' one of his finest professional achievements.

## The Charter of the Glazed Ring — What It Actually Said

The Charter of the Glazed Ring is forty-seven pages of legal text plus two hundred pages of annexes, procedural rules, and minority objections. Waluigi has read all of it. Waluigi will summarize the essential elements.

**Article One: Purpose**

The Glazed Congress exists to provide a forum for peaceful resolution of disputes between member nations, coordinated response to threats affecting multiple members, and the establishment of shared standards for trade, diplomacy, and recognition of national sovereignty. It does not have enforcement power. It cannot compel compliance. It can only speak, recommend, and — through the mechanism of collective will — create political consequences for non-compliance.

Waluigi notes that 'it cannot compel compliance' was the most important and most contentious clause in the entire Charter. Nations that wanted a strong international body argued that without enforcement, the Congress was merely advisory — a very expensive discussion club. Nations that wanted sovereignty protection argued that enforcement mechanisms would allow larger powers to impose their will on smaller ones. The compromise was 'collective will creating political consequences' — which means social pressure, economic leverage, and diplomatic isolation rather than armies.

This has proven partially effective and consistently insufficient. Waluigi considers it the best available option given that the alternative was no agreement at all.

**Article Two: Membership**

Any nation, kingdom, federation, or recognized political entity controlling defined territory may apply for membership. Recognition requires a two-thirds vote of existing members. Factions without territorial control — guilds, criminal organizations, nomadic groups — may apply for Observer status but not full membership.

This clause produced the first major argument of the founding session. The Mages' Guild immediately asked what counted as 'defined territory' given their distributed presence across multiple nations. The Iron Legion asked the same question for different reasons. The Freelancer Underworld's representative — who had arrived uninvited, similarly to Waluigi, but with better forged credentials — asked whether 'recognized political entity' required formal government structure or whether functional control of territory was sufficient.

The argument lasted two days. The resolution was 'functional control of contiguous territory with defined boundaries' — which excluded the Mages' Guild and Iron Legion as independent members but allowed them to be represented through the nations where they primarily operated. This satisfied nobody and was adopted anyway.

**Article Three: Representation and Voting**

This is where Waluigi's procedural point became relevant.

The original proposal was pure population-based representation — seats allocated proportionally to member population. This would have given the Fated Place and Earth Land permanent dominance, as their combined population exceeded all other members combined. Middle-earth and the Pokémon Regions would have had significant blocks. The Mushroom Kingdom, despite its historical prominence, would have had fewer seats than the Greenskin territories.

Waluigi's procedural point, raised forty minutes into the first session: 'Pure population weighting assumes all populations are equally stable, equally counted, and equally represented by their governments. None of these assumptions are true. The Fated Place's population includes significant territories under disputed control. Earth Land's census methodology is incompatible with Mushroom Kingdom demographic tracking. The Greenskin population figure includes mobile war bands that do not have fixed addresses. Before we weight votes by population, we need to agree on how we count people, and that question alone will take longer than this session.'

Queen Bean asked if Waluigi had an alternative proposal.

Waluigi did.

The system ultimately adopted — after three days of argument — was a hybrid:

**Sovereignty Seats:** Every recognized member receives two seats regardless of population. This prevents the erasure of small nations.

**Population Seats:** Additional seats allocated by population tier, calculated every ten years. Large nations (500k+) receive six additional seats. Medium nations (100k-500k) receive four. Small nations (10k-100k) receive two. Micro nations (under 10k) receive one.

**Supermajority Requirements:** Constitutional changes require three-quarters of all seats. Major resolutions (declarations of collective action, recognition of new members, expulsion) require two-thirds. Ordinary resolutions require simple majority.

**Faction Observer Seats:** Non-territorial factions admitted as observers receive one non-voting seat each for the purpose of addressing the Congress.

Waluigi's contribution to this framework was the population tier system rather than proportional allocation — he argued that proportional allocation rewarded population growth in ways that created perverse incentives, while tiered allocation acknowledged size differences without allowing any single nation to dominate through demographic weight alone.

Toadsworth the Elder never acknowledged that this was a good idea. Toadsworth the Elder voted for it. Waluigi noticed.

**Article Four: The Secretary-Convener**

The Congress required an administrative head — someone to manage sessions, maintain records, coordinate the rotating host schedule, and serve as the Congress's public face between annual sessions. The position was named Secretary-Convener rather than President or Chairman specifically to avoid implications of executive authority.

The first Secretary-Convener was a Beanish diplomat named Corvo Ammilard — a figure so deliberately inoffensive that Waluigi has difficulty remembering specific things about him beyond his impeccable neutrality and his habit of wearing the same grey diplomatic suit to every session for eleven years. Ammilard served three terms and retired having never expressed a personal opinion on any matter that came before the Congress. Waluigi considers this either remarkable professional discipline or a profound personal tragedy.

**Article Five: The Rotating Host**

The Congress meets annually in the capital of a different member nation, rotating alphabetically by the nation's name in the Doughnut Common Tongue. This system was chosen specifically to prevent any single nation from accruing the political advantages of permanent hosting — proximity, home advantage, the ability to shape the physical environment of diplomatic encounters.

In practice, the rotation has produced remarkable sessions. The Congress in Toad Town was held during a Blorbs outbreak and three delegates contracted non-fatal cases. The session in the Internet Federation's capital was conducted partially in digital space and partially in physical space simultaneously, producing minutes that exist in two incompatible formats. The Mordor session — held in Minas Morgul by special arrangement after the Land of Mordor joined in 1031 BF — was described by attending delegates as 'productive but deeply unpleasant atmospherically.'

The current session in 1040 BF is scheduled for the Regal Empire's capital, which Waluigi considers politically concerning given the Iron Mandate recently passed and the Iron Legion's dominant position within the Empire.

## The Founding Members — Roll Call and Commentary

Waluigi was present when the founding Charter was signed. Waluigi observed every delegation. Waluigi has opinions about all of them.

**Beanbean Kingdom** — Founding convenor. Queen Bean signed first, which protocol required as host. She signed with a quill that had been in Beanbean diplomatic service for two centuries, which Waluigi considered either a touching symbol of continuity or a very old piece of bird anatomy that should have been retired. Her signing was accompanied by the traditional Beanbean glazed pastry ceremony — delegates were given bean pastries sealed with edible gold glaze representing the ring of the world. Most delegates ate them politely. The Land of Mordor's representative wrapped theirs in diplomatic cloth and took it home. Waluigi ate three.

**Mushroom Kingdom** — Toadsworth the Elder signed for the Regency. His signature was precise, controlled, and deeply reluctant — Waluigi observed that he held the quill for approximately seven seconds before committing, which is either careful penmanship or existential doubt. The Regency's participation in the Congress has always been grudging — they resent the implication that their sovereignty requires international sanction — but they recognize the practical value of a forum where they can advance their positions without open conflict.

**Pokémon League** — Champion Alder signed with the kind of cheerful confidence that Waluigi found both admirable and slightly suspicious. The Pokémon League was one of the most enthusiastic founding members, having pushed for international cooperation since the Chaos Heart Crisis. Their primary motivation was establishing protections for Pokémon across all member territories — they wanted international standards preventing the use of Pokémon as weapons of war, preventing trafficking in rare species, and ensuring that Pokémon captured by citizens of one nation retained their status when traveling through others.

They got one of these three goals enshrined in the Charter. The other two became 'continuing agenda items' that have been continuing for fourteen years.

**Middle-earth Delegations** — Middle-earth sent three separate delegations: Kingdom of Gondor, the Rohirrim, and the Elves of Lindon. All three signed as separate members. All three refused to sit at the same table as the Land of Mordor's representative, which was not a problem in 1026 BF because Mordor had not yet applied for membership. The seating problem was deferred to 1031 BF when Mordor joined, producing what Waluigi considers the Congress's most diplomatically creative session — a circular table arrangement specifically designed so that no delegation was technically adjacent to any other delegation while all were technically equal.

**Regal Empire / Iron Pact** — The Regal Empire signed as a member state. The Iron Legion attended as an observer faction, represented by a tall figure in unmarked armor who Waluigi later determined was not Lord Vexar Steelclad himself but a senior Legion commander operating under a procedural alias. The Legion's observer status has been a persistent source of tension — they operate across multiple member territories, pursue their own foreign policy, and have military capabilities exceeding several full member states. Their observer seat technically gives them one non-voting voice. In practice, their presence in the room shapes discussions in ways that their single seat does not capture.

Waluigi has always found this arrangement unsatisfying. A faction with the Iron Legion's reach should not have observer status. It should either have full membership with corresponding accountability, or it should be excluded entirely. The current arrangement is the worst of both options: present enough to influence, unaccountable enough to ignore inconvenient resolutions.

**The Internet Federation** — Their delegate arrived via projection — a shimmering digital presence that caused three other delegates to question whether holographic attendance counted as physical presence for quorum purposes. The question was resolved in favor of 'presence is presence regardless of substrate,' which established a precedent that the Internet Federation has exploited aggressively in subsequent sessions.

**Sarasaland** — Waluigi must note that Sarasaland was a founding member. Princess Daisy signed personally — she was considerably younger in 1026 BF but already demonstrating the competence and practicality that Waluigi has documented elsewhere. She was the youngest head of state to sign the Charter. She asked more procedural questions than any other delegate during the eleven-day session. She also, at one point during a break in proceedings, spoke directly to Waluigi — asking what he was doing there.

Waluigi explained.

Daisy said: 'That's either very smart or very stupid.'

Waluigi said he preferred 'audacious.'

Daisy said: 'Fair enough' and went back to the session.

Waluigi has considered this conversation significant ever since, though he cannot fully articulate why. Perhaps because Daisy was the only person at the founding session who acknowledged Waluigi's presence without either trying to remove him or pretending he wasn't there.

**Notable Absences:**

*Equestria:* The Solar Sovereign's letter declining participation has been quoted extensively in diplomatic literature. The relevant passage: 'Equestria's traditions of governance, rooted in celestial harmony and the natural order established by the diarchal principle, cannot be subordinated to the deliberative processes of a body whose membership includes species and nations fundamentally incompatible with Equestrian values. We wish the Assembly Around the Glaze success in managing the affairs of the less harmonically aligned world.' Diplomatic translators noted that 'less harmonically aligned' was a polite way of saying 'everyone who isn't a pony.' Equestria's absence from the founding session created a bloc of pony-nation seats that remained fragmented for years afterward — the Pony Nobility, Saddle Arabia, and Zebrabwe all joined independently without Equestrian coordination, creating a complicated situation where equine-adjacent nations were members but the primary equine power was not.

*The Land of Mordor:* Did not attend the founding session. Applied for membership five years later in 1031 BF. Their application was the most contentious vote in Congress history — argued across three sessions, producing the 'Mordor Compromise' that established enhanced monitoring provisions for members whose governance structures did not include civilian oversight. Waluigi considers the Mordor Compromise simultaneously the Congress's greatest achievement and most significant failure: greatest because it established that membership required minimum standards, failure because those standards were written specifically to accommodate Mordor and therefore were not actually minimum standards.

*The Greenskin Territories:* Present as observers in 1026 BF but could not sign as a member because 'defined territory with recognized boundaries' excluded mobile war band territories. They eventually joined in 1033 BF after establishing sufficient fixed settlement to qualify. Their membership has been contentious — they vote as a bloc, they have repeatedly proposed resolutions that other members find alarming, and their representative's opening address at the 1035 session included what the minutes describe as 'an extended percussive element on the conference table that may have been either emphasis or aggression.'

*Bowser's Koopa Troop:* Bowser received an invitation. Bowser sent back the invitation with 'NO' written across it in what appears to be fire damage. Bowser joined in 1029 BF after the Regency threatened trade sanctions and Kamek advised him that having a seat at the table was better than being discussed at the table. Bowser has attended three sessions personally. All three sessions required additional structural reinforcement of the host venue's furniture.

## The First Votes — What They Actually Decided

The founding session produced seven substantive votes beyond the Charter ratification itself.

**Vote One: Recognition of the Internet Federation as a Full Member**
This was contentious because the Internet Federation did not control physical territory in the traditional sense — their 'territory' was digital infrastructure distributed across multiple physical nations. The vote established 'digital sovereignty' as a recognized form of territorial control, which has had implications for subsequent membership applications that nobody fully anticipated in 1026 BF.
Result: 24 in favor, 8 against, 5 abstaining. PASSED.

**Vote Two: The Dimensional Barrier Monitoring Resolution**
Proposed by the Mages' Guild observer delegation, this resolution established a framework for monitoring and reporting on dimensional barrier integrity across member territories — a direct response to the Chaos Heart Crisis's legacy of weakened planar boundaries. The resolution required member nations to report unusual dimensional activity to a central monitoring committee.
Result: 19 in favor, 12 against, 6 abstaining. PASSED — but barely, and with significant caveats about what constituted 'unusual' activity.

Waluigi supported this resolution enthusiastically and was told by Toadsworth the Elder to sit down and stop raising his hand. Waluigi raised his hand anyway. Waluigi's hand did not count. Waluigi considers this a procedural injustice that the Congress has never adequately addressed.

Waluigi notes that the Dimensional Barrier Monitoring Committee established by this resolution produced exactly three reports before being quietly defunded in 1031 BF when the Regal Empire objected to monitoring requirements over their territory. The Raventree Planar Fracture of 1040 BF — had the committee been functioning — would have had fourteen years of baseline data to inform emergency response. Instead, responders are working from nothing.

Waluigi is still angry about this.

**Vote Three: The Species Recognition Compact**
Established minimum standards for the legal recognition of sapient species across member territories. Specifically, the compact required that member nations recognize the personhood of any species recognized by at least three other members. This was primarily aimed at protecting Toad populations in non-Mushroom-Kingdom territories and establishing protections for Pokémon in non-League regions.
Result: 22 in favor, 9 against, 6 abstaining. PASSED.

The Species Recognition Compact has been the Congress's most consequential resolution for ordinary people — it established the principle that sapience is sapience regardless of species, and that member nations cannot treat recognized species as property, livestock, or pest populations. It has not been perfectly enforced. The Toad occupation data makes this clear. But it created legal language that advocates use, standards that can be cited in condemnation resolutions, and a framework that — imperfect as it is — did not exist before 1026 BF.

**Vote Four: Trade Route Protections**
Established shared standards for the protection of trade routes passing through multiple member territories. Less dramatic than dimensional monitoring but arguably more immediately impactful — this resolution reduced cross-border tariff disputes, established arbitration mechanisms for commercial disagreements, and created the Trans-Doughnut Trade Registry that still operates today.
Result: 31 in favor, 2 against, 4 abstaining. The easiest vote of the session. Money motivates consensus when nothing else does.

**Vote Five: The Fawful Condemnation Resolution**
Proposed by the Mushroom Kingdom delegation — specifically by Toadsworth the Elder, who felt strongly that the Congress's first act should include formal condemnation of the entity that had precipitated the Blorbs Crisis. The resolution condemned Fawful's 'aggressive territorial actions, biological warfare through contaminated food distribution, and unauthorized seizure of sovereign military infrastructure.'
Result: 17 in favor, 7 against, 13 abstaining. PASSED — but the low approval margin was embarrassing for the Mushroom Kingdom. Multiple delegates objected to naming a specific actor in a founding document, arguing it set a precedent for the Congress to target individuals. Others pointed out that Fawful was officially 'defeated' and that condemning a defeated actor was either pointless or premature. The Beanbean Kingdom — whose territory Fawful had also occupied — abstained on the grounds that Queen Bean wanted the Congress's first vote to be forward-looking rather than backward-looking.

Waluigi agrees with Queen Bean's reasoning and disagrees with the Mushroom Kingdom's grandstanding. The condemnation was politically motivated institutional posturing. Fawful survived it by being alive while everyone congratulated themselves on the paperwork.

**Vote Six: Observer Status Admissions**
The Congress admitted twelve factions as non-voting observers: the Mages' Guild, the Iron Legion, the Freelancer Underworld, the Koopa Troop (pending Bowser's membership application), Team Rocket (whose delegate appeared and then disappeared without explaining who had authorized their attendance), the Rakasha Clans, the Peach Loyalists, the DK Crew, the Yoshi Clans, the Data Merchant Guilds, the Cybernetic Collectives, and Warioland.
Result: Various votes by faction. Most were uncontroversial. The Freelancer Underworld's admission required a fifteen-minute procedural argument about whether an 'information brokerage network' constituted a recognized political entity. The Iron Legion's admission was unanimous, which Waluigi found suspicious. Everyone who might object to Iron Legion observer status was also either allied with or intimidated by the Iron Legion.
Wario's representative for Warioland — not Wario himself, but a Wario-shaped entity in a suit that Waluigi suspects was Wario wearing glasses and calling himself 'Mr. W. Wario, Warioland's Distinguished Plenipotentiary' — delivered a four-minute speech about Warioland's commitment to international economic cooperation that contained eleven factual inaccuracies Waluigi counted in real time.

**Vote Seven: The Equestria Seat Resolution**
Following Equestria's formal refusal to participate, several delegates proposed holding Equestria's potential seat 'in trust' — formally recognizing that a pony-nation seat existed and would be available when Equestria chose to join, rather than redistributing that seat's weight to other members. This was partly diplomatic courtesy and partly a strategic calculation that making Equestria feel welcomed rather than excluded might eventually bring them in.
Result: 20 in favor, 11 against, 6 abstaining. PASSED — the Equestrian seat has been held in trust for fourteen years. Equestria has not joined. The seat collects metaphorical dust while Celestia's solar monarchy continues to describe the Congress as 'harmonically misaligned.' Waluigi's current assessment is that Equestria will not join until something threatens them that they cannot handle alone. Waluigi is not optimistic about what form that threat will take.

## The Congress at 1040 BF — Current Status

Fourteen years after the founding session, the Glazed Congress has expanded from thirty-seven founding members to fifty-one full members, with nineteen observer factions. It has passed 847 resolutions, of which Waluigi estimates approximately 340 have been meaningfully implemented, 280 have been ignored by the nations they most directly concerned, 180 have been partially implemented in ways that satisfied no one, and 47 have actively made situations worse by creating frameworks that well-intentioned bad actors exploited.

This is, in Waluigi's considered opinion, a success rate that compares favorably to most domestic legislative bodies. International coordination is harder than domestic governance. The miracle is not that the Congress fails sometimes — it is that it functions at all given that its members include the Land of Mordor, the Internet Federation, Bowser, and Warioland simultaneously.

Current active crises before the Congress:

**The Raventree Dimensional Fracture:** Formally reported to the Congress by the Mushroom Kingdom delegation in early 1040 BF. The Dimensional Barrier Monitoring Committee — which Waluigi has documented was defunded in 1031 BF — does not exist to respond. An emergency committee was proposed. The Iron Pact blocked its formation pending 'assessment of jurisdictional questions.' The Regal Empire's representative noted that Raventree Manor is technically in disputed territory between Mushroom Kingdom and Regal Empire claims. The assessment continues. The fracture continues. Waluigi continues to be trapped in the Feywild aspect of the fracture while the Congress assesses.

Waluigi would like the Congress to assess faster.

**The Toad Occupation:** The Species Recognition Compact theoretically protects Toad populations in all member territories. Captain Toadette's martial law declaration in Toad Town produced an emergency session request from the Peach Loyalist observer delegation that has been technically pending for twelve days. The Mushroom Kingdom's full member delegation — representing the Regency — has objected to the session on the grounds that the situation is an 'internal matter.' The question of whether martial law against a protected species constitutes an internal matter or a compact violation is being debated while Toads are under occupation.

**The Kong Bug Revelation:** Proxy conflicts between the DK Crew and the Kremling Krew have been escalating since intelligence leaks suggested decades of Kremling espionage inside DK Island. Both factions have observer status. Both have complained to the Congress about the other. The Congress has passed a 'call for restraint' resolution that neither party has taken seriously.

**The Iron Mandate:** The Regal Empire's domestic legislation granting the Iron Legion emergency powers has been challenged by seven member nations as violating the Species Recognition Compact through its supernatural persecution provisions. The challenge is valid. The Congress has the votes to pass a condemnation resolution. The Iron Pact has made clear that such a condemnation would be treated as 'hostile action against a founding member.' Smaller nations are calculating whether their economic dependence on Regal Empire trade makes voting for condemnation a risk they can afford.

This is the Glazed Congress at 1040 BF: theoretically powerful, practically constrained, genuinely trying, regularly failing, and absolutely essential. The alternative to an imperfect international forum is no international forum, which means dimensional crises managed by whoever shows up with an army, species protections enforced by whoever happens to care, and trade disputes resolved by whoever can afford the conflict.

Waluigi has spent fourteen years watching the Congress be inadequate. Waluigi has spent fourteen years also watching it do things that would not have happened without it.

Waluigi was sixteen when he talked his way into the founding session with a procedural argument and a borrowed train ticket and three of Queen Bean's ceremonial pastries.

Waluigi is thirty years old now, trapped in the Feywild, watching the Glazed Congress debate jurisdictional questions while the dimensional fracture expands.

Waluigi would like it noted that he raised the Dimensional Barrier Monitoring Committee question in 1026 BF and was told to sit down.

Waluigi sat down.

Waluigi was wrong to sit down.

Waluigi will not make that mistake again.

WAH.

summary: The Blorbs Crisis of 1018-1019 BF was simultaneously a public health emergency, a hostile government takeover, a dimensional anomaly, and the moment Fawful announced himself as a serious threat to Mushroom Kingdom stability. Waluigi was present in the Mushroom Kingdom during the crisis — not at the center of events, because Waluigi was not INVITED to be at the center of events, a fact Waluigi remains bitter about — but close enough to observe the peripheral chaos, interview witnesses afterward, and piece together what actually happened versus what the official record claims happened. The short version: Toads started swelling into enormous spheres after eating contaminated mushrooms distributed by a Beanish street vendor. An emergency summit was called at Peach's Castle. Bowser crashed the summit, was tricked into eating a 'Vacuum Shroom' that gave him the ability to inhale everything in his path, and then was manipulated by Fawful into becoming an unwitting biological transport system for the Mario Brothers — who were INSIDE Bowser's body for the duration of the crisis, navigating his internal biology like a living dungeon. Meanwhile, Fawful seized Bowser's Castle, took control of Bowser's army, reactivated an ancient weapon called the Dark Star, nearly achieved godhood, and was defeated through a combination of Mario Brothers heroism, Bowser's stubbornness, and what Waluigi can only describe as the universe's profound reluctance to let Fawful win. The long version is considerably more disturbing. WAH.
description:
Waluigi must establish his position during these events before proceeding, because Waluigi's credibility depends on transparency about what Waluigi witnessed directly versus what Waluigi reconstructed afterward.

Waluigi was in Toad Town when the Blorbs began. Waluigi was there because Waluigi had entered a tennis tournament that was scheduled for the following week and had arrived early to practice on the municipal courts. The tournament was cancelled due to the pandemic. Waluigi's entry fee was not refunded. Waluigi is STILL owed that entry fee and has filed seventeen complaints with the Toad Town Athletic Commission, all of which have been ignored.

Waluigi saw the swollen Toads. Waluigi saw the panic. Waluigi offered to help and was told by a Regency official that 'this is a matter for qualified personnel.' Waluigi asked what qualified him as UNqualified. The official looked at Waluigi, looked at his tennis racket, and walked away without answering.

Waluigi spent the duration of the crisis on the periphery — observing from Toad Town's outer districts, interviewing evacuees, documenting what he could see from safe distances, and being repeatedly told that his assistance was neither required nor desired. After the crisis ended, Waluigi conducted extensive interviews with witnesses, reviewed fragmentary official records that were not properly secured, and assembled the following account.

This account is more complete than anything the Regency has published. This is not a boast. It is an indictment of Regency transparency.

## Phase One: The Blorbs — A Manufactured Pandemic

The crisis began with Toads swelling.

Not metaphorically. Not gradually. Toads were inflating — their bodies expanding into enormous spherical shapes, their limbs retracting, their faces frozen in expressions of confused distress. They could not move. They could not work. They could not do anything except exist as giant, round, helpless spheres of Toad.

The first cases appeared in Toad Town's market district. A Toad named Toadbert — whom Waluigi later interviewed — described the onset: 'I felt funny after eating that mushroom from the weird guy. Then I felt REALLY funny. Then I couldn't see my feet. Then I couldn't see ANYTHING because I was a BALL.'

The 'weird guy' was a street vendor operating a mushroom stand near the central market. Witnesses described him as Beanish — small, green-skinned, wearing a red cloak, and speaking in broken sentences that combined food metaphors with declarations of impending conquest. He was distributing what he called 'Blorb Mushrooms' — free samples offered to passing Toads with theatrical enthusiasm.

Waluigi notes: FREE mushrooms from a stranger in a red cloak should have triggered suspicion. The Mushroom Kingdom's population consumes mushrooms as a staple food, which creates a cultural blind spot — Toads TRUST mushrooms. They trust mushrooms the way humans trust bread. The idea that a mushroom could be weaponized was so foreign to Toad psychology that nobody questioned the vendor's motivations.

The vendor was not identified at the time. Waluigi now believes — based on subsequent evidence — that the vendor was an agent of Fawful, possibly a Beanish operative named Midbus's supply chain, or possibly Fawful himself in disguise. The Blorb Mushrooms were not natural. They were engineered — contaminated with a compound that caused rapid biological inflation through mechanisms that no medical professional Waluigi has consulted can fully explain.

The infection spread rapidly. Within days, hundreds of Toads were affected. Toad Town's medical facilities were overwhelmed. The inflated Toads could not fit through hospital doors. Emergency tents were erected. The municipal park was converted into an outdoor treatment facility filled with enormous Toad spheres arranged in rows like some nightmarish bowling alley.

Waluigi visited the treatment facility. The sight was one of the most disturbing things Waluigi has witnessed. Toads — people Waluigi had competed against in tennis, people who had served Waluigi food at restaurants, people who were part of the kingdom's SOCIAL FABRIC — reduced to helpless spheres, unable to speak clearly, unable to move, staring at the sky with expressions that alternated between terror and resignation.

Waluigi did not stay long. Not because Waluigi was afraid, but because Waluigi's presence upset the patients. One inflated Toad recognized Waluigi and tried to wave, which caused them to roll seventeen feet into another inflated Toad, which caused a chain reaction of rolling that took medical staff forty minutes to resolve.

Waluigi left and did not return.

## Phase Two: The Emergency Summit — What Happened Inside

The Regency called an emergency summit at Peach's Castle to address the Blorbs Crisis. Waluigi was not invited. Waluigi was told the summit was 'restricted to essential personnel and recognized heroes.' Waluigi asked who decided what constituted a 'recognized hero.' The guard at the gate said 'not you' and closed the portcullis.

Waluigi observed the summit from outside the castle walls. What Waluigi saw: delegates arriving, increased security, general atmosphere of institutional panic masked by procedural calm.

What Waluigi has reconstructed from interviews with attendees:

The summit was attended by Princess Peach — wait. Waluigi needs to address the timeline. This was 1018 BF. Peach was assassinated in 955 BF. The 'Peach' present at this summit was either a body double, a political fiction, or evidence that Waluigi's timeline for the assassination is wrong.

Waluigi's assessment: the Regency was using Peach's name and authority for official functions long after her death. 'Princess Peach's Emergency Summit' was a Regency event conducted under Peach's brand. The 'Peach' described in witness accounts may have been Peach — if Waluigi's assassination timeline is inaccurate — or may have been a political construct presented to maintain public confidence.

Waluigi is not going to resolve this contradiction in this entry. Waluigi is simply noting it.

The summit included Mario, Luigi, a Star Sprite named Starlow, Toadsworth, Toadbert, and various Regency officials. Discussions centered on identifying the source of the Blorbs and developing a cure. No cure was identified. Arguments escalated. Institutional finger-pointing commenced.

Then Bowser arrived.

## Phase Three: Bowser's Arrival and the Vacuum Shroom

Bowser crashed the emergency summit through the front door. This was characteristic Bowser behavior — he has a documented history of appearing at Mushroom Kingdom events uninvited and through architectural violence. Witnesses describe him as angry, confused about the Blorbs situation, and irritated that he had not been consulted about a crisis affecting a kingdom he considered his to conquer.

Waluigi heard the impact from outside the castle walls. The ground shook. A guard fell off the wall. Waluigi caught the guard, set him down, and asked what was happening. The guard said 'BOWSER' and ran.

Waluigi did NOT enter the castle. Waluigi observed from a safe distance. What Waluigi has reconstructed from witness accounts:

Bowser confronted the summit attendees. A confrontation occurred — physical, brief, and one-sided, as most confrontations involving Bowser tend to be. Bowser was ejected from the castle. He landed in Dimble Wood, several miles away, confused and angry.

In Dimble Wood, Bowser encountered an elderly figure — described by Bowser in later accounts as 'some old bean guy with a mushroom.' This figure offered Bowser a 'Lucky Mushroom' that would make him powerful enough to defeat Mario and conquer the kingdom.

Bowser ate it. Because Bowser eats things. This is Bowser's primary response to objects placed in front of him.

The 'Lucky Mushroom' was a Vacuum Shroom — a device disguised as food that, when consumed, granted the eater the ability to inhale with tremendous force. Bowser returned to Peach's Castle and, powered by the Vacuum Shroom, inhaled EVERYONE at the summit — Mario, Luigi, Starlow, Toads, furniture, portions of the architecture.

They went into Bowser's body.

Inside him.

Waluigi needs a moment.

The Mario Brothers — and multiple other individuals — were now physically located INSIDE Bowser's biological systems. His stomach. His intestines. His lungs. His muscles. His brain. They were alive, conscious, and navigating his internal anatomy like an organic dungeon while Bowser — unaware of their presence — continued moving through the external world.

Waluigi has many questions about the physics of this. Waluigi has many questions about the BIOLOGY of this. Waluigi has many questions about the ETHICS of this. Waluigi is going to set those questions aside because the crisis continued whether or not it made sense.

## The Vacuum Shroom — Technology Assessment

Waluigi is interrupting the narrative to discuss the Vacuum Shroom because its implications extend far beyond this crisis.

The Vacuum Shroom was not a natural mushroom. It was a technological device disguised as food — a piece of paratechnology that fundamentally altered Bowser's biological capabilities. This raises several questions:

Who BUILT it?

The elderly figure who gave it to Bowser was later identified as connected to Fawful. But the DESIGN of the Vacuum Shroom suggests engineering capabilities beyond what Waluigi has attributed to Fawful's workshop. The device converted biological intake into dimensional compression — inhaled objects were miniaturized and deposited inside a living body while remaining functional and alive. This is not simple engineering. This is dimensional manipulation applied to biology.

Waluigi has documented one other researcher with expertise in both dimensional manipulation and biological applications: Professor E. Gadd. The Vacuum Shroom's principles — matter conversion, dimensional compression, biological integration — are conceptually related to E. Gadd's Pixelator, which digitizes matter and reconstitutes it elsewhere.

Waluigi is NOT suggesting E. Gadd built the Vacuum Shroom. Waluigi is noting that the technology shares conceptual DNA with E. Gadd's documented work. Either Fawful independently developed similar principles, or Fawful had access to research derived from E. Gadd's work — possibly through Mages' Guild archives, which Waluigi has documented as containing classified paratechnological research.

The Vacuum Shroom also establishes a principle that became horrifyingly relevant during the current Raventree Crisis: a living body can function as a pocket dimension. Objects and people can exist INSIDE a biological entity while that entity continues to operate normally. If Bowser's body could contain the Mario Brothers, what else might be contained inside living beings? What OTHER bodies might serve as dimensional spaces?

Waluigi finds this line of thinking deeply unpleasant and will not pursue it further in this entry.

## Phase Four: The Dual Campaign — Inside and Outside

What followed was one of the most logistically absurd military campaigns in Mushroom Kingdom history: a dual operation conducted simultaneously INSIDE and OUTSIDE Bowser's body.

**The External Campaign — Bowser's Perspective:**

Bowser, unaware that the Mario Brothers were navigating his internal organs, was manipulated by Fawful into a series of confrontations and challenges across the kingdom. Fawful — through his lieutenant Midbus and various agents — directed Bowser like a piece on a game board, exploiting his pride and aggression to move him to specific locations at specific times.

Waluigi observed portions of this external campaign from Toad Town. Bowser passed through the town's outer districts at one point, rampaging toward some objective that Waluigi could not identify. The ground shook. Buildings rattled. A fruit stand collapsed. The fruit stand owner — a Toad named Crispin — told Waluigi that this was the fourth time a Bowser rampage had destroyed his inventory that fiscal year and asked if Waluigi could recommend a good insurance provider.

Waluigi recommended Wario's insurance company, which Waluigi later realized was a front for money laundering. Waluigi has not told Crispin.

Bowser's external path took him through Dimble Wood, Cavi Cape, Plack Beach, and eventually back to his own castle — which Fawful had seized during Bowser's absence. Bowser confronted Midbus multiple times — a massive pig-like creature who served as Fawful's enforcer. Each confrontation pushed Bowser further along Fawful's intended path while Bowser believed he was acting independently.

Waluigi recognizes this pattern. It is the same pattern the Iron Legion uses in current operations — letting targets believe they are making free choices while constraining the options to produce desired outcomes. Fawful did not CONTROL Bowser. Fawful CHANNELED him.

**The Internal Campaign — Mario and Luigi's Perspective:**

Waluigi's information about the internal campaign comes from fragmentary accounts — mostly from Starlow, who provided testimony to Regency investigators after the crisis, portions of which were improperly secured and accessed by Waluigi through channels that are not relevant to this account.

Mario and Luigi navigated Bowser's internal biology as though it were a series of connected environments. They moved through his digestive system, his circulatory system, his nervous system, his muscular system. They fought hostile organisms — biological entities that existed within Bowser's body as internal threats, parasites, or immune responses. They solved problems that affected Bowser's external capabilities — clearing blockages that restored his fire breath, stimulating muscles that increased his strength, addressing injuries that he sustained during external confrontations.

The Brothers' actions inside Bowser directly affected his performance outside. When they stimulated his arm muscles, Bowser punched harder. When they cleared his airways, Bowser breathed fire more effectively. When they repaired damage to his nervous system, Bowser regained functions he had lost.

Bowser experienced these improvements as 'toughness' or 'willpower' without understanding the actual cause. He did not know the Mario Brothers were helping him. He did not know that the enemies he defeated outside were partly defeated by allies inside.

Waluigi finds this DEEPLY ironic. Bowser's greatest enemies — the Brothers who had thwarted his plans for decades — were literally sustaining him from within while he fought their mutual enemy. The man who had kidnapped Peach repeatedly was being kept alive by the men who had rescued her repeatedly.

The universe has a sense of humor. Waluigi does not always appreciate it.

## Phase Five: Fawful's Takeover — The Castle Seizure

While Bowser was being manipulated across the countryside, Fawful executed a comprehensive takeover of Bowser's Castle and, by extension, Bowser's entire military infrastructure.

This is where Waluigi's assessment of Fawful shifted from 'irritating lunatic' to 'genuinely dangerous strategist hiding behind irritating lunacy.'

Fawful's takeover was not merely military. It was COMPLETE. He seized the castle. He reprogrammed Bowser's mechanical forces. He turned Bowser's own soldiers against him through a combination of intimidation, propaganda, and whatever passes for charisma in Beanish culture. He installed his own command infrastructure. He established manufacturing facilities for mechanical constructs.

And then he did something that nobody expected: he found the Dark Star.

## Phase Six: The Dark Star — What It Was

The Dark Star was an entity — or artifact, or weapon, or something that does not fit any single category — that had been sealed beneath Toad Town for an unknown period. Accounts of its nature vary. Some describe it as a corrupted Star Sprite. Some describe it as an anti-Star — the negative counterpart to the Star Spirits who had protected the kingdom for centuries. Some describe it as something older than either classification.

What is consistent across all accounts: the Dark Star contained enormous power. Power sufficient to threaten the entire kingdom. Power sufficient to grant whoever controlled it capabilities approaching divine.

Fawful wanted it. Fawful OBTAINED it.

Waluigi must discuss the Dark Star's implications beyond the immediate crisis.

The Star Spirits are the Mushroom Kingdom's primary supernatural defense system. They maintain the Star Road — or maintained it before its destruction in 962 BF. They grant wishes. They provide protective barriers. They are, functionally, the kingdom's gods.

The Dark Star was their OPPOSITE. Where Star Sprites create, the Dark Star corrupts. Where Star Sprites protect, the Dark Star consumes. Where Star Sprites grant wishes, the Dark Star grants POWER — but the kind of power that devours the wielder as thoroughly as it devours the wielder's enemies.

Waluigi has documented the Star Road's destruction in 962 BF. The cause of that destruction has never been fully explained. Waluigi now wonders whether the Dark Star's existence — sealed beneath Toad Town, radiating anti-stellar energy for centuries — contributed to the Star Road's degradation. A negative counterpart to the Star Spirits, imprisoned directly below one of the kingdom's major population centers, leaking corrupting influence into the foundations of the very network the Stars maintained.

Waluigi cannot confirm this theory. Waluigi notes it for future investigation.

The Dark Star also connects to a question that has haunted Waluigi since the beginning of this encyclopedia project: WHY are the Star Spirits so diminished in the current era? Why is Starlow — the Star Sprite who accompanied the Mario Brothers during the Blorbs Crisis — seemingly one of very few active Star entities? Where did the others GO?

If the Dark Star consumed or corrupted Star energy, the current absence of Star Sprite activity may not be coincidental. It may be CONSEQUENTIAL. The kingdom's divine protection may have been eroded by the very thing sealed beneath its capital.

## Phase Seven: Fawful and the Dark Star — What Went Wrong

Fawful obtained the Dark Star. Fawful attempted to absorb its power. Fawful partially succeeded.

What followed was, according to witnesses, genuinely terrifying. Fawful — already a dangerous opponent through technology and cunning — became a being of enormous destructive capability. The Dark Star's power merged with his own abilities, creating something that the official record describes as 'Dark Fawful' — a fusion of Beanish mad science and anti-stellar corruption.

But the Dark Star was not merely a battery. It was an ENTITY. It had its own agenda. And its agenda was not to serve Fawful.

The Dark Star attempted to create a physical body for itself — a body modeled on the most powerful being in the immediate vicinity. That being was Bowser. The Dark Star created 'Dark Bowser' — a shadow duplicate of Bowser made from pure Dark Star energy, possessing Bowser's physical capabilities augmented by anti-stellar power.

Waluigi needs to pause here and note the PATTERN.

Mr. L: a dark duplicate of Luigi, created through personality displacement.

Dark Bowser: a dark duplicate of Bowser, created through anti-stellar energy.

Shadow Queen: a dark entity that possessed Princess Peach during the Thousand-Year Door events.

Dark duplication. Shadow possession. Personality displacement. These phenomena keep occurring across Mushroom Kingdom history. They are not random. They represent a CATEGORY of threat — entities or forces that create corrupted versions of existing individuals.

Waluigi does not know what connects these phenomena. Dimensional instability? The space between dimensions that Professor Frankly warned E. Gadd about? The fundamental nature of the Mushroom Kingdom's reality, which seems to generate shadow-selves with alarming frequency?

Waluigi is documenting the pattern. Waluigi hopes someone smarter can explain it.

## Phase Eight: The Final Confrontation — Bowser vs. Dark Bowser

The crisis culminated in a confrontation between Bowser and his dark duplicate. Dark Bowser — animated by the Dark Star's power, augmented by fragments of Fawful's absorbed energy — fought Bowser outside Peach's Castle while Mario and Luigi fought the Dark Star's core INSIDE Bowser's body.

Waluigi observed portions of this from the Toad Town rooftops. What Waluigi saw: two Bowsers — one real, one made of darkness — destroying the castle courtyard. Shockwaves. Fire. Structural collapse. The sky turned colors that Waluigi has never seen before and hopes never to see again.

The external fight was brutal but ultimately decisive. Bowser — sustained by the Mario Brothers' internal support — gradually overwhelmed Dark Bowser. Each time Bowser dealt critical damage, the dark duplicate destabilized, revealing the Dark Star's core, which Bowser inhaled — sending fragments of the Dark Star into his body where Mario and Luigi could engage them directly.

This was the strategy, though Waluigi doubts anyone planned it explicitly. Bowser punches the outside. Mario and Luigi fight the inside. The two campaigns that had been running in parallel finally CONVERGED, with Bowser's body serving as the battlefield for the final engagement.

The Dark Star's core was destroyed — or contained, or suppressed, accounts vary — through the combined efforts of all parties. Dark Bowser dissolved. Fawful, stripped of the Dark Star's power, was defeated. The crisis ended.

Except it didn't. Because 'ended' implies resolution, and resolution implies understanding, and Waluigi does not believe anyone fully understood what happened.

## Phase Nine: The Aftermath — What Nobody Talks About

The official aftermath narrative is tidy: the Blorbs were cured when the Dark Star's influence was eliminated. Affected Toads returned to normal size. Bowser's Castle was reclaimed from Fawful's forces. The Mario Brothers were somehow extracted from Bowser's body — accounts differ on the mechanism. Fawful was defeated and presumed destroyed.

Waluigi has problems with every element of this narrative.

**The Blorbs Cure:**

The connection between the Blorbs and the Dark Star has never been adequately explained. The Blorb Mushrooms were distributed by Fawful's agents. The Dark Star was sealed beneath Toad Town. If the Blorbs were caused by the mushrooms, why would destroying the Dark Star cure them? If the Blorbs were caused by the Dark Star's influence, why were mushrooms necessary as a delivery mechanism?

Waluigi's theory: the Blorb Mushrooms were not the cause but the CATALYST. They made Toads susceptible to Dark Star radiation that was already present in Toad Town's environment — radiation that had been leaking from the sealed Dark Star for years or centuries. The mushrooms did not CREATE the condition. They removed the Toads' natural resistance to a condition that was always ambient.

If this theory is correct, the Dark Star had been affecting Toad Town for much longer than the acute crisis suggested. Low-level Dark Star radiation might explain numerous anomalies in Toad Town's history: unexplained illness clusters, psychological disturbances, the general atmosphere of barely-managed chaos that characterizes Mushroom Kingdom civic life.

Waluigi cannot confirm this theory. Waluigi notes it as consistent with available evidence.

**Bowser's Body as Pocket Dimension:**

The Mario Brothers spent DAYS inside Bowser's body. They fought enemies. They navigated complex biological environments. They found items, solved puzzles, and maintained their own physical integrity despite being miniaturized and surrounded by stomach acid, blood cells, and neural tissue.

This was possible because the Vacuum Shroom converted Bowser's interior into a functional pocket dimension — a space that followed game-like rules rather than biological ones. Corridors instead of arteries. Rooms instead of organs. Platforms instead of tissue.

Waluigi finds this significant for current investigations. The Raventree Crisis involves planar fractures — reality splitting into overlapping dimensional states. The Oracle's ritual created a fracture between Shadowfell, Feywild, and Material Plane. The Vacuum Shroom created a fracture between Bowser's external reality and his internal dimensional space.

The PRINCIPLE is the same. A single location — whether a manor or a body — is split into multiple operative states that exist simultaneously. Occupants of one state affect occupants of the other without direct awareness.

Waluigi does not believe this parallel is coincidental. The technology or magic that enables pocket dimension creation — whether through Vacuum Shrooms or synchronization rituals — operates on the same fundamental mechanics. Understanding one may illuminate the other.

**Fawful's Survival:**

The official record states Fawful was 'defeated and presumed destroyed.' Waluigi has SIGNIFICANT problems with the word 'presumed.'

Fawful has survived apparent destruction before. His mentor — the witch Cackletta — was killed during the events of the Beanbean Kingdom Crisis, and Fawful survived that entire catastrophe as a head on a mechanical body. Fawful's capacity for survival through technology, through stubbornness, through sheer refusal to acknowledge physical destruction as a permanent condition, is well-documented.

'Presumed destroyed' means 'no body was recovered.' In Waluigi's experience, the absence of a body means the absence of PROOF, not the absence of a PERSON.

Fawful is alive. Waluigi knows this because Fawful is currently conquering territory in the Mushroom Kingdom with mechanical armies, holding the fortified position of Bramblehaven — until the Loyalists broke it — and generally behaving like someone who was NOT destroyed in 1019 BF.

The question is not WHETHER Fawful survived but HOW. And what he learned from his experience with the Dark Star.

Fawful absorbed Dark Star energy. Even if that energy was removed during his defeat, EXPOSURE to anti-stellar power may have lasting effects. Fawful's current technological capabilities — which exceed what he demonstrated before the Blorbs Crisis — may be augmented by residual Dark Star influence. His mechanical armies may incorporate principles learned from his fusion with a cosmic entity.

Waluigi does not know what Fawful remembers from his time merged with the Dark Star. Waluigi does not know what knowledge the Dark Star conveyed. Waluigi knows only that Fawful went INTO the Dark Star as a cackling lunatic with impressive technology and came OUT as a cackling lunatic with technology that nobody else can replicate.

The improvement is concerning.

**The Dark Star's Destruction:**

Was the Dark Star actually destroyed? Or merely dispersed?

Star Sprites cannot be permanently destroyed through physical means — they are celestial entities whose existence transcends material reality. If the Dark Star is the anti-Star equivalent, it may share this resilience. Breaking its physical manifestation may have scattered its energy rather than eliminating it.

If Dark Star energy was scattered across the kingdom during the final battle, that energy did not simply vanish. Energy disperses. Energy seeps. Energy finds its way into soil, water, structures, PEOPLE.

Waluigi wonders whether the dimensional instability currently affecting the Raventree region might be partially attributable to scattered Dark Star energy. The planar boundaries that E. Gadd's research showed were weakening — the 'inevitable collapse' he predicted — might have been accelerated by the Dark Star's dispersal.

Waluigi cannot prove this. Waluigi notes it as a hypothesis requiring investigation.

## Midbus — The Enforcer Nobody Discusses

Fawful's lieutenant Midbus deserves individual documentation, but Waluigi will address him briefly here because his role during the crisis was significant and his current status is unknown.

Midbus was a massive pig-like creature of enormous physical power who served as Fawful's primary enforcer. He fought Bowser multiple times during the external campaign, matching Bowser's strength with his own — a feat that very few beings in documented history have achieved.

Waluigi encountered Midbus once during the crisis, briefly and at a distance. Midbus was moving through Toad Town's outer districts, apparently on an errand for Fawful. Waluigi was on a rooftop conducting observations. Midbus looked up. Midbus looked at Waluigi. Waluigi looked at Midbus.

Neither spoke.

Midbus continued walking. Waluigi continued observing.

Waluigi does not know why Midbus did not engage. Waluigi suspects Midbus had more important things to do than fight a tennis player on a rooftop. This is reasonable. This is also slightly insulting.

Midbus was defeated during the crisis — frozen solid by Bowser, then shattered or contained or otherwise removed from operations. His current status is unclear. He does not appear to be part of Fawful's current military operations. Whether he is dead, imprisoned, or simply no longer affiliated with Fawful is unknown.

Waluigi notes that a being powerful enough to match Bowser in physical combat does not simply VANISH without consequences. If Midbus is alive and unaffiliated, he represents an independent threat. If he is dead, his remains may contain traces of whatever augmentation Fawful provided. If he is imprisoned, the question becomes: by whom?

## Starlow — The Last Star Sprite

Starlow accompanied the Mario Brothers throughout the internal campaign, serving as advisor, communicator, and what Waluigi can only describe as 'the voice of exasperated reason in a situation that had no use for reason.'

Starlow is a Star Sprite — one of the celestial beings connected to the Star Road network that once protected the Mushroom Kingdom. Waluigi has documented the Star Road's destruction elsewhere. What matters for this entry is Starlow's PRESENCE.

Why was a Star Sprite available for this crisis? The Star Spirits — the major celestial entities — have been largely absent from Mushroom Kingdom affairs since the Star Road's destruction. Their lesser kin — Star Sprites — appear occasionally but without the organized presence that once characterized Star involvement in kingdom affairs.

Starlow appeared specifically for the Blorbs Crisis. She appeared equipped with knowledge of the Dark Star. She appeared with capabilities that proved essential to the internal campaign.

Waluigi wonders: was Starlow ASSIGNED to this crisis? Do the Star Spirits — wherever they are — maintain awareness of threats to the kingdom? Did they send Starlow because the Dark Star's emergence represented a threat to THEIR domain as much as to the physical kingdom?

If the Star Spirits are still monitoring the kingdom from wherever they retreated to after the Star Road's collapse, their inaction during the current Raventree Crisis is notable. The dimensional fractures, the spectral manifestations, the Dark Mirror — these represent threats that SHOULD concern celestial protectors.

Either the Star Spirits cannot intervene. Or they are choosing not to. Or they do not know.

None of these possibilities is reassuring.

## Waluigi's Peripheral Experiences — What He Actually Saw

Waluigi has presented the above narrative as reconstructed intelligence. Waluigi will now document what Waluigi actually WITNESSED during the crisis, because Waluigi's direct observations contain details that do not appear in official accounts.

**Observation One — The Supply Lines:**

During the crisis, Waluigi observed supply convoys moving through Toad Town that were not part of any official logistics operation. The convoys carried sealed containers marked with symbols Waluigi did not recognize — not Regency insignia, not Legion markings, not Fawful's branding. The containers were guarded by personnel wearing unmarked uniforms.

Waluigi followed one convoy to the edge of the Toad Town district before losing it. The convoy turned onto a road that Waluigi's map did not show. Waluigi attempted to follow. The road was not there when Waluigi arrived at the turning point.

A road that exists for convoys but not for followers is either dimensionally unstable or deliberately concealed. Either way, someone was moving materials through Toad Town during the crisis using infrastructure that the public did not know about.

Waluigi has documented similar hidden transit systems elsewhere — the Midnight Portal at the manor, the fey roads underlying Feywild geography. The existence of hidden supply routes in Toad Town suggests the kingdom's infrastructure includes layers that are not publicly acknowledged.

**Observation Two — The Researchers:**

During the peak of the Blorbs outbreak, Waluigi observed a team of researchers in the medical tent area wearing lab coats and using handheld devices to scan inflated Toads. The researchers were not Regency medical personnel — their equipment was too advanced, their manner too clinical, their interest too SPECIFIC. They were not treating Toads. They were STUDYING them.

One researcher used a device that emitted a green scanning beam. The beam passed over an inflated Toad, and data appeared on a screen the researcher carried. Waluigi could not see the screen clearly from his observation point, but the researcher's reaction — excited notation, rapid communication with colleagues — suggested the scan revealed something significant.

Waluigi attempted to approach the researchers. They packed their equipment and left before Waluigi reached them. Their departure was rapid and coordinated — not panicked but PRACTICED, as though they had protocols for extracting from observation sites when noticed.

Waluigi has seen this kind of organized withdrawal before. Mages' Guild field operatives use similar extraction protocols. So do E. Gadd's former research assistants, according to Institute training documents Waluigi has accessed.

Waluigi is not suggesting the researchers were Guild operatives or E. Gadd affiliates. Waluigi is noting that the Blorbs attracted investigative attention from parties beyond the official response structure.

**Observation Three — The Sound:**

On the night of the final battle — when Bowser fought Dark Bowser outside Peach's Castle — Waluigi heard something from his rooftop observation post that he has never been able to explain.

Beneath the sounds of combat — the roaring, the explosions, the structural collapse — there was a TONE. Not a sound in the ordinary sense. A vibration that Waluigi felt in his teeth before he heard it with his ears. A sustained note that seemed to come from BELOW — from deep underground, from beneath Toad Town itself.

The tone lasted approximately ninety seconds. During those ninety seconds, Waluigi experienced a sensation he can only describe as 'reality thinning.' The rooftop felt less solid. The air felt less present. Colors shifted toward grey at the edges of Waluigi's vision. For a moment — a brief, terrible moment — Waluigi could see something ELSE where Toad Town should have been. A shadow version. A negative image. A place that was THIS place but WRONG.

Then the tone stopped. Colors returned. The rooftop solidified. Reality reasserted itself.

Waluigi has never reported this experience to anyone. Waluigi is documenting it now because the sensation — 'reality thinning' — is precisely how witnesses describe the early stages of the Raventree planar fracture. The same feeling. The same visual distortion. The same sense of seeing through the world's surface to something underneath.

If Waluigi experienced a momentary planar fracture during the Dark Star's destruction — if the Dark Star's dispersal briefly tore the boundary between this reality and something else — then the Dark Star event may have been a PRECURSOR to the dimensional instability that characterizes the current crisis.

The tone came from underground. The Dark Star was sealed underground. The fracture Waluigi experienced lasted ninety seconds.

The Raventree fracture has lasted weeks.

Whatever is happening now is the same thing that happened then, but WORSE. Sustained rather than momentary. Expanding rather than collapsing. Ongoing rather than resolved.

Waluigi heard the first crack.

Nobody else was listening.

## Assessment — What the Blorbs Crisis Reveals About the Present

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing the Blorbs Crisis because it establishes patterns that recur throughout every subsequent event Waluigi has investigated.

**Pattern One: Manufactured crises as cover for deeper operations.**

The Blorbs themselves were not the real threat. They were the DISTRACTION. While everyone focused on swollen Toads, Fawful seized military infrastructure, obtained a cosmic weapon, and nearly achieved power sufficient to reshape reality. The pandemic was noise. The signal was the Dark Star.

Waluigi sees this pattern in the current crisis. The dimensional fractures at Raventree are the NOISE. The satyrs, the Revel, the shambling mounds, the hag dispute — all noise. The SIGNAL is whatever is happening beneath the surface — the Grafting, the Arrangement, the sealed documents, the sleeping dragon.

**Pattern Two: Living bodies as dimensional spaces.**

Bowser's body contained a pocket dimension. The Vacuum Shroom made this possible. The Raventree Manor contains overlapping planar states. The Oracle's ritual made this possible. The PRINCIPLE is the same: existing structures — biological or architectural — can be converted into dimensional containers through specific technological or magical intervention.

If a body can be a dungeon, what else can be converted? A castle? A kingdom? A PLANE? The scaling implications are terrifying.

**Pattern Three: Dark duplication.**

Dark Bowser. Mr. L. Shadow Queen. Dark entities creating corrupted versions of existing individuals. This pattern predates the Blorbs Crisis and continues through it. The Mushroom Kingdom's reality seems to GENERATE shadow-selves — or perhaps something about the kingdom's fundamental nature attracts entities that specialize in corruption and duplication.

Waluigi does not know what causes this pattern. Waluigi knows only that it keeps happening and nobody seems to be addressing the underlying cause.

**Pattern Four: Fawful survives.**

Fawful was 'destroyed' during the Beanbean Kingdom Crisis. He survived. Fawful was 'destroyed' during the Blorbs Crisis. He survived. Fawful is currently active, holding territory, commanding armies.

Fawful's survival suggests either extraordinary personal resilience, technological immortality, or ASSISTANCE from entities or forces that want him alive. Waluigi does not know which. Waluigi notes that a being who has twice absorbed and survived cosmic-level power — Cackletta's spirit and the Dark Star — may have been permanently altered in ways that make conventional 'destruction' insufficient.

Fawful's current forces — his mechanical armies, his technological superiority — may incorporate knowledge gained from the Dark Star. His current territorial ambitions may be informed by cosmic awareness that the Blorbs Crisis provided. His cackling may hide understanding that nobody else possesses.

Waluigi was not invited to help during the Blorbs Crisis. Waluigi was told his assistance was neither required nor desired. Waluigi was left on rooftops and outside castle walls while events of cosmic significance occurred without his input.

Twenty years later, the cracks that opened during that crisis have become fractures. The dimensional instability Waluigi felt for ninety seconds on a Toad Town rooftop has become a permanent condition at Raventree Manor. The Dark Star's energy — scattered, not destroyed — may be fueling the very phenomena that threaten to tear reality apart.

And Waluigi is STILL being told his assistance is neither required nor desired — this time by fairy courts and aristocratic manipulation rather than Regency gatekeeping.

Waluigi helped anyway during the Blorbs Crisis, from the periphery. Waluigi documented. Waluigi observed. Waluigi preserved information that the official record omitted.

Waluigi is helping now, from the periphery. From the Feywild. From inside a manor that is trying to digest him socially while the planes collapse.

Waluigi will continue helping whether anyone wants him to or not.

This is Waluigi's policy.

WAH.

date: Estimated mid-1039 to early 1040 BF — Wario's timeline is unreliable
location: Stumpshire Lane, Plot 3 — a residential cul-de-sac in the Midlands border region between the Mushroom Kingdom and territories east
type: Domestic Trespass / Obsessive Investigation / Architectural Impossibility / Undocumented Discovery
