summary: After the second dissolution of Warioland and the staged cancer death that Waluigi has documented elsewhere, Wario relocated to a residential cul-de-sac in the Midlands border region. He chose Plot 3 of Stumpshire Lane because it was cheap, obscure, and within laundering distance of three separate banking jurisdictions. What Wario did NOT choose was his neighbor. Plot 2 was occupied by an elderly man living in a house that should not have existed — architecturally impossible, vertically absurd, covered in devices and antennae and modifications that no residential structure requires. The old man was aggressively private. Wario was aggressively nosy. What followed was an escalating campaign of break-in attempts, ejections, booby traps, surveillance, counter-surveillance, and one incident involving a catapult that Wario claims was 'self-defense.' Wario eventually gained access to the basement. He found something. He will not say what. Waluigi has documented what Wario WILL discuss and drawn conclusions from the gaps. The conclusions are mostly about Wario being an idiot. The gaps, however, suggest something considerably more significant. WAH.
description:
Waluigi obtained this account through three separate conversations with Wario, each conducted under different circumstances: the first at a bar where Wario was bragging, the second during a card game where Wario was losing and therefore talkative, and the third during the Feyward campaign when Wario mentioned the neighbor unprompted while trying to sell Waluigi garlic at a 400% markup. The accounts are broadly consistent, which for Wario is practically sworn testimony.

Waluigi has also obtained fragmentary information from municipal records in the Stumpshire district, a noise complaint log that is extraordinarily detailed, and one conversation with a postal worker who delivered mail to Plot 2 and described the experience as 'the worst part of my career, and I once delivered a package to Bowser's castle during an invasion.'

Waluigi presents this account as entertainment with footnotes. The entertainment is Wario being Wario. The footnotes are where Waluigi buries the things that actually matter.

## The House on Plot 2

Wario's description of his neighbor's house changed slightly between tellings, but certain details remained consistent across all three accounts. Waluigi considers these the reliable elements:

The house was TALL. Not merely two or three stories — Wario described it as extending vertically in ways that the foundation should not have supported. Additions had been built on top of additions, connected by external staircases, reinforced with metal scaffolding, and topped with devices that Wario could not identify. 'Looked like someone built a house, then built another house on top of it, then got bored and built a TOWER on top of THAT, and then added a thing on the roof that went BZZZT when it rained.'

The house had CAMERAS. Not the ornamental kind. Not the 'I have a Ring doorbell' kind. The kind that tracked movement, adjusted angles, and occasionally emitted small clicking sounds that Wario described as 'judging.' Multiple cameras covered every approach to the property. The front door had THREE cameras pointed at it from different angles. The back garden had cameras hidden in the hedges — Wario discovered these when he attempted his first break-in through the garden and a hedge made a mechanical whirring sound.

The house had a BASEMENT. Wario knew this because the neighbor — an elderly man with thick round spectacles, a lab coat worn as casual clothing, and hair that Wario described as 'like someone electrocuted a cotton ball' — went into the basement every evening at precisely the same time and did not emerge for hours. Lights flickered. Strange sounds emanated. On one occasion, Wario claimed to have heard screaming from beneath the house, though he later revised this to 'maybe it was machinery, but ANGRY machinery.'

The house had no mailbox. The postal worker confirmed this. Mail was delivered through a slot in the door that appeared to have a mechanical sorting system behind it — letters went in and were immediately processed by something that clicked and whirred. The postal worker reported that one day a letter was returned through the slot within SECONDS, stamped with 'REJECTED — INSUFFICIENT CLEARANCE LEVEL.' It had been a promotional flyer for a local restaurant.

Waluigi would like to note that a house with mechanical mail sorting, multi-angle surveillance cameras, vertical architectural impossibility, and a basement that produces screaming machinery sounds is not a HOUSE. It is a FACILITY disguised as a house. Someone with significant technical expertise and considerable paranoia was living at Plot 2, Stumpshire Lane, and they did not want visitors.

## The Neighbor: 'Mr. Gadd'

Wario referred to his neighbor consistently as 'the old kook' or 'Mr. Gadd' — the latter apparently taken from the mailbox that did not exist, replaced by a small nameplate on the front door that read 'E. GADD — NO SOLICITORS, NO VISITORS, NO EXCEPTIONS, NO WARIO.'

The 'NO WARIO' was added later, after the third break-in attempt.

Wario's physical description of the neighbor: short, elderly, thick round spectacles that appeared to contain additional lenses that could be rotated into position, a lab coat worn at all times including apparently during gardening, wild white hair, and an energy level that Wario described as 'caffeinated beyond what should be legal for someone that old.'

The neighbor spoke rapidly, used technical terminology that Wario did not understand, and frequently muttered to himself while adjusting devices attached to his person. He carried at minimum two handheld instruments at all times — one that beeped near certain objects and one that projected a small beam of green light that Wario claimed 'made his fillings vibrate.'

Waluigi recognizes this description. Waluigi is choosing not to state the obvious conclusion in this section because the entry is organized chronologically and the identification will be addressed later. But Waluigi recognizes this description very clearly, and the fact that Wario apparently did NOT recognize who he was living next to is either a testament to Wario's self-absorption or evidence that the neighbor had taken deliberate steps to avoid identification.

## The First Attempt: The Front Door

Wario's initial approach was characteristically direct. He walked up to the front door on his second day at Stumpshire Lane and knocked. The door had a speaker system. The speaker activated.

'Welcome to the neighborhood. Please leave immediately. This is not a social call zone. If you are selling something, I am not buying. If you are borrowing something, I am not lending. If you are Wario, and my cameras suggest you are, I have already filed a preemptive noise complaint. Good day.'

Wario knocked again.

'I said GOOD DAY.'

Wario knocked a third time and shouted that he was bringing a housewarming gift — which, according to Wario, was a bottle of wine he had already drunk half of on the walk over.

The front door did not open. A small panel above the door DID open, and a mechanical arm emerged holding a sign that read: 'GIFT DECLINED. AREA NOW UNDER ENHANCED SURVEILLANCE. YOU HAVE FIVE SECONDS.'

Wario did not leave in five seconds. A sprinkler system activated — but instead of water, it sprayed a fine mist that Wario described as smelling like 'burnt garlic and regret.' Wario retreated to Plot 3 and spent the evening planning his next approach.

Waluigi notes that the sprinkler system dispensed a compound rather than water. This suggests chemical deterrent capability integrated into residential infrastructure. This is not something a normal retiree installs. This is something someone installs when they have EXPERIENCE with unwanted visitors and the technical knowledge to weaponize landscaping.

## The Second Attempt: The Garden

Three days later, Wario attempted to enter through the back garden. The garden itself was notable — Wario described it as containing plants he had never seen before, arranged in geometric patterns that 'made my eyes go funny if I looked at them too long.' There were flowers that appeared to glow faintly at night. There were mushrooms growing in a dedicated bed that Wario was specifically warned away from by a sign reading 'DO NOT CONSUME — EXPERIMENTAL GENUS — SIDE EFFECTS MAY INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: DIMENSIONAL DISPLACEMENT, CHROMATIC INVERSION, EXISTENTIAL DOUBT.'

Wario attempted to eat one anyway. The mushroom tasted, according to Wario, like 'television static.' He experienced fifteen minutes of seeing everything in inverted colors before the effect wore off. This deterred him from the mushrooms but not from the garden.

The hedge cameras detected him. A secondary system activated — garden gnomes that were not gnomes. They were AUTOMATED. Small mechanical figures approximately eighteen inches tall began emerging from concealed positions in the flower beds and advancing toward Wario while emitting a high-pitched warning tone. Wario kicked one. It exploded in a small puff of colored smoke and flour. Three more emerged from behind a watering can.

Wario retreated over the garden wall, taking one of the mechanical gnomes with him. He later sold it to a collector for forty coins, which Waluigi considers theft but Wario considers 'market economics.'

The neighbor appeared at Wario's door the following morning, demanding the return of 'Prototype Sentry Unit 7-G.' Wario claimed he had never seen it. The neighbor stared at him for four seconds, adjusted his spectacles, and said: 'I have seventeen more. They remember faces. Consider yourself catalogued.'

Waluigi notes the phrase 'Prototype Sentry Unit.' Not 'garden gnome.' Not 'decoration.' PROTOTYPE. SENTRY. UNIT. The neighbor was field-testing autonomous security devices disguised as garden ornaments. The mushroom bed contained experimental specimens with dimensional side effects. The garden itself was a research installation disguised as horticulture.

Waluigi is going to continue not stating the obvious conclusion. Waluigi wants to see how long it takes for the reader to arrive there independently.

## The Third Attempt: The Roof

Wario escalated. He purchased a ladder. The ladder was not long enough to reach the roof of the original structure, let alone the impossible vertical additions. Wario purchased a SECOND ladder and duct-taped them together. This engineering solution failed when the combined ladder bent at the junction point and deposited Wario in the neighbor's front hedge, which turned out to contain not only cameras but also what Wario described as 'little grabby arms that held me in place while a recording told me my trespassing had been logged and timestamped.'

The neighbor emerged from his front door wearing what appeared to be a headset connected to a device on his belt. He looked at Wario suspended in the hedge. He sighed. He said: 'You are the most persistent nuisance I have encountered since the Boo infestation of Lab 5. And those were GHOSTS. They had the excuse of being dead. What is YOUR excuse?'

Wario said he was curious.

The neighbor said: 'Curiosity is a disease that I have spent my career trying to harness, and even I know when to leave a door CLOSED.'

Wario asked what was behind the door.

The neighbor said: 'You don't want to know.'

This was, of course, the worst thing he could possibly have said to Wario.

Waluigi notes: 'Boo infestation of Lab 5.' The neighbor referred to a laboratory. Not a study. Not a workshop. A LAB. Numbered. Implying at minimum FIVE separate lab spaces. A man living in a residential cul-de-sac who references ghost infestations in numbered laboratories as a point of comparison for domestic annoyance is not a retired hobbyist. He is a SCIENTIST whose career involved spectral entities.

## The Fourth Through Eighth Attempts: Escalation

Wario does not discuss attempts four through eight in detail. What Waluigi has pieced together from the noise complaint log:

**Attempt Four:** Wario tried to enter through a second-floor window using a trampoline. He overshot and landed on the third floor, which turned out to be a sealed room filled with filing cabinets that immediately began retracting into the walls when an unauthorized presence was detected. Wario grabbed one folder before being ejected by a pneumatic floor panel. The folder contained what appeared to be schematics labeled 'POLTERGUST MK III — CLASSIFIED — DO NOT DISTRIBUTE.' Wario did not know what a Poltergust was and threw the schematics away.

Waluigi would like to pause here.

Wario found POLTERGUST SCHEMATICS in a filing cabinet on the third floor of his neighbor's impossible house. The Poltergust is the ghost-hunting vacuum device that LUIGI uses. The device was invented by Professor Elvin Gadd — known publicly as E. Gadd — the Mushroom Kingdom's foremost paranormal researcher and inventor.

Wario found Poltergust schematics.

Wario threw them away.

Waluigi is going to continue documenting this account without editorial comment on this decision because Waluigi does not have the emotional reserves to address it right now.

**Attempt Five:** Wario attempted to dig a tunnel from his basement to the neighbor's basement. He hit metal plating approximately four feet underground and broke his shovel. The plating extended in every direction he tried. The neighbor had reinforced the ENTIRE subsurface perimeter of his property with what Wario described as 'iron or something harder.' Wario tried a pickaxe. The pickaxe bounced. Wario tried dynamite. The dynamite produced a muffled thump and a note that slid out from under Wario's own front door reading: 'Seismographic sensors detected unauthorized detonation at 14:37. Next occurrence will activate countermeasures. There will not be a third warning.'

**Attempt Six:** Wario hired three Goombas to distract the neighbor at the front door while Wario entered through the back. The Goombas knocked. The door speaker activated. The neighbor said: 'I know Wario hired you. I can see him behind your colleague with the binoculars. The binoculars are mine, by the way. He stole them during Attempt Three. Tell him I added them to his tab.' The Goombas looked at each other and left. Wario disputes that the binoculars were stolen.

**Attempt Seven:** Wario built a catapult in his backyard and attempted to launch himself over the neighbor's roof and into the chimney. The trajectory was wrong. Wario landed on the automated weather vane on the highest tower, which spun and deposited him into a drainage gutter that channeled him through a pipe system and ejected him into the front garden. The neighbor was waiting with a clipboard. He made a notation and said: 'I'm adding structural damage to the weather vane to your tab. Current total: four hundred and twelve coins.'

Wario claims the catapult was 'self-defense equipment' that he was testing for unrelated reasons.

**Attempt Eight:** Unknown. The noise complaint log simply reads: 'PLOT 2 RESIDENT REPORTS WARIO ATTEMPTED SOMETHING INVOLVING BEES. BEES ESCAPED. BOTH PROPERTIES EVACUATED FOR FOUR HOURS. BEES EVENTUALLY ENTERED BASEMENT OF PLOT 2 THROUGH UNKNOWN ACCESS POINT. RESIDENT APPEARED UNCONCERNED ABOUT BEES IN BASEMENT.'

Waluigi notes that the bees entered the basement through an 'unknown access point.' The neighbor was 'unconcerned.' Either the basement has ventilation systems that accommodate insect entry — unusual for a sealed facility — or the neighbor had confidence that whatever was in the basement could handle bees. Or the bees were part of the experiment all along and their arrival was welcome.

Waluigi is choosing not to speculate about experimental bees. Waluigi has limits.

## The Conversation: What the Neighbor Actually Said

Between attempts seven and eight, according to Wario, the neighbor approached him voluntarily. This was the longest conversation they had. Wario's account of this exchange has remained consistent across all three tellings, which suggests it made an impression.

The neighbor sat on Wario's porch — uninvited, which Wario found hypocritical and said so — and spoke for approximately ten minutes. The following is reconstructed from Wario's memory, which is unreliable for details but generally accurate for emotional register:

'You're new to this block. I've been here for eleven years. Before that I was somewhere else. Before that I was somewhere else. I have lived in nine locations since I stopped doing public work and every single time, SOMEONE decides that the interesting house must contain interesting things and the interesting things must be available for the taking.'

'My house is not a place to steal clues from. My house is where I keep the things that would HURT people if they were found by the wrong hands. I am not hiding treasure. I am hiding CONSEQUENCES.'

'You think I'm the villain because I have cameras and locks and sentry gnomes. You think I must be doing something terrible in my basement because I go down there every night and you hear sounds you don't understand. But you have not considered the possibility that I am keeping something CONTAINED. That the locks are not keeping you OUT. They are keeping something IN.'

'I had love in my life. I had purpose. I had colleagues and students and a MISSION. And then someone — someone I trusted, someone whose family I had SERVED for decades — decided that my work was too dangerous to continue and my knowledge was too dangerous to possess. They didn't kill me. That would have been SIMPLE. They made me disappear. They made my name classified. They made my laboratories government property and my research restricted and my LIFE into something that could only exist in margins and footnotes.'

'And I built THIS. Nine houses in eleven years because they keep FINDING me. This one has lasted the longest. The cameras help. The sentry units help. The subsurface plating helps. But YOU — you enormous, garlic-smelling, endlessly intrusive PROBLEM — you are going to attract the kind of attention that makes me move again.'

'So stop knocking on my door. Stop climbing my walls. Stop launching yourself at my chimney. Stop digging tunnels. Stop hiring Goombas. Stop EVERYTHING. Because if you attract THEM — and you will, because you are LOUD and they are LISTENING — then I will have to abandon this house and everything in the basement. And if I abandon what is in the basement, it will eventually be found by people who will use it. And if they use it, people will DIE.'

'I'm not the devil. I'm just your neighbor. And I am asking you — I am BEGGING you, which I do not do — to get out and stay out.'

Wario's response, according to Wario: 'So there IS something good in the basement.'

The neighbor reportedly stared at Wario for eight seconds, stood up, and walked back to Plot 2 without another word.

Waluigi has read this account multiple times. Waluigi has focused primarily on Wario's comedic inability to absorb an emotional plea. But in the interest of thoroughness, Waluigi will note some details from the neighbor's speech that are probably not significant but which Waluigi is recording for completeness:

The neighbor said he stopped doing 'public work.' He said someone whose family he had 'served for decades' decided his work was too dangerous. He said his laboratories became 'government property.' He said his research was 'restricted.' He said 'they' keep finding him.

These details are consistent with a retired government researcher whose work was seized by a political authority. The Mushroom Kingdom has a documented history of classifying research it considers threatening — the Mages' Guild maintains restricted archives, and the Regency has sealed multiple categories of scientific documentation related to dimensional studies, spectral phenomena, and what the official records call 'paratechnological development.'

Waluigi considers these details background information and will not pursue them further because Waluigi is focused on the WARIO elements of this story, which are much funnier.

Waluigi has absolutely no reason to connect a retired researcher whose spectral research was seized by the government to any CURRENT crisis involving ghost-hunting technology, dimensional fractures, or Mr. L containment protocols.

None at all.

Moving on.

## The Basement: What Wario Found

Wario eventually got into the basement. He will not say exactly how — only that it happened during Attempt Nine, that it involved 'being in the right place at the wrong time,' and that the neighbor was not home when it happened. Wario implies that the neighbor left in a hurry — 'like someone called him and he had to GO, right then, no time to lock up properly.'

Waluigi notes the timing. Wario estimates this occurred in late 1039 BF. The Star Fountain reunion — when Luigi found Mario — occurred in 1039 BF. If the neighbor was called away urgently during this period, and if the neighbor had connections to Luigi or the Mario Brothers' situation, then the departure may have been connected to events that Waluigi has documented elsewhere.

This is PROBABLY a coincidence. Waluigi is noting it for completeness.

The basement, according to Wario:

'It was HUGE. Way bigger than the house. Like the house was sitting on top of something that went DOWN instead of up. There were rooms. LOTS of rooms. Numbered. Some of them had windows but the windows looked out on NOTHING — just dark. Some of them had equipment I couldn't name. Big machines. Small machines. Things that beeped. Things that hummed. Things that were turned off but felt like they were WATCHING.'

'There was a room with tanks. Glass tanks. Some were empty. Some had STUFF in them. Green stuff. Moving stuff. I didn't look too close because the stuff looked like it was looking BACK.'

'There was a room with files. TONS of files. Cabinets everywhere. I opened some. Most of it was science stuff I couldn't read. Numbers and diagrams and words I don't know. But some of them had NAMES on them. People's names. Files on PEOPLE.'

'There was one cabinet that was different. Bigger. Metal. Not like the others. It had a lock I couldn't pick and a label I couldn't read because it was in some kind of CODE. But there was a sticky note on top of it — like a regular yellow sticky note, which was WEIRD because everything else was all high-tech — and the sticky note said...'

Wario paused here in all three tellings. In the bar, he took a drink. During the card game, he shuffled his hand. In the Feywild, he looked away.

The sticky note said: 'FOR WHEN THEY NEED THE TRUTH. NOT BEFORE. — E.G.'

Wario did not open the cabinet. Wario says he COULD NOT open the cabinet — the lock defeated him, which Wario considers a personal affront given that he has broken into banks, castles, and at least one pocket dimension. Whatever locking mechanism the neighbor used on that cabinet was beyond Wario's considerable skills.

But Wario saw one more thing before he left.

In the deepest room — the one at the very bottom of the basement complex — there was a door. The door was not locked. It was SEALED. Chains, plates, welding marks, and a symbol painted on the surface that Wario described as 'a ghost inside a circle with a line through it.' A containment symbol. A WARNING.

And behind the door, Wario heard something.

Not machinery. Not screaming. Not anything mechanical.

BREATHING.

Something behind the sealed door was alive and breathing.

Wario left the basement. Wario left the HOUSE. Wario went back to Plot 3, packed a bag, and departed Stumpshire Lane that evening. He did not return. He did not tell anyone what he found — not immediately. The account only emerged later, in fragments, told with the particular casualness that Wario uses when he is trying very hard to seem unbothered by something that bothered him enormously.

## What Wario Took

Wario is Wario. Of course he took something.

From the filing cabinet room, before reaching the sealed door, Wario grabbed three folders at random. He did not read them carefully at the time. He described their contents to Waluigi as 'boring science stuff.' When pressed, he provided the following details:

**Folder One:** Technical specifications for a device called the 'Pixelator.' Diagrams showed a machine capable of converting physical matter into digital data and reconstituting it at a secondary location. Marginalia in the researcher's handwriting noted: 'Travel application shelved — too close to Guild transit networks — would attract attention from G.S.' Wario did not know what 'G.S.' referred to. Wario sold this folder to a Koopa Troopa engineer for sixty coins.

**Folder Two:** A behavioral study of spectral entities categorized by 'hostility index.' The study documented ghost types, their psychological profiles, and containment protocols for each. One section was highlighted and starred: 'TYPE K-9 — KING BOO VARIANT — DO NOT ENGAGE WITHOUT MK IV OR HIGHER. MK III INSUFFICIENT. INCIDENT REPORT: SEE FILE LM-3.' Another note in the margin: 'L does not know about the failsafe. Must discuss before next deployment. If he finds out the Poltergust has a third function, he will not use it again.' Wario did not understand any of this. Wario used this folder as a placemat for approximately two weeks before losing it.

**Folder Three:** A personnel file. The name on the tab was partially obscured by a coffee stain — Wario's contribution — but the visible portion read '—ARIO, M.' The file contained medical records, psychological evaluations, a section titled 'CONTINGENCY SEVEN,' and a photograph that was face-down and stapled to the inside back cover. Wario did not flip the photograph. Wario did not read the file. Wario used it to prop up a wobbly table leg at his next residence.

Waluigi asked Wario to retrieve the folder. Wario said the table had been sold. With the folder still under the leg.

Waluigi does not have the emotional capacity to respond to this.

## What Waluigi Noticed (Wario Section)

Waluigi has thoroughly analyzed Wario's account for anything useful. Waluigi's conclusions about WARIO are as follows:

Wario's break-in campaign lasted approximately three months. During this period, he spent over five hundred coins on equipment, bribes, and medical treatment for catapult-related injuries. He gained access to a basement laboratory containing advanced technology, classified research, sealed containment facilities, and personnel files on unknown subjects. He stole three folders. He threw away one, lost one, and sold one. The total profit from the stolen goods was sixty coins.

Wario spent five hundred coins to earn sixty coins.

This is the most Wario thing Waluigi has ever documented.

The neighbor's identity is presumably some retired inventor who got too paranoid for public life. The cameras, the gnomes, the impossible house — all consistent with someone who has more engineering talent than social skills and more anxiety than either. Waluigi suspects the neighbor is still out there, having moved to a tenth location after Wario compromised the ninth.

Waluigi wishes the neighbor well. Living next to Wario would make ANYONE build a two-thousand-foot house with chemical sprinklers and exploding gnomes.

The breathing behind the sealed door is concerning but Waluigi attributes it to an experimental specimen — possibly one of the mushroom variants from the garden bed, possibly something spectral, possibly a very large and very patient pet. Scientists keep strange things in their basements. This is not news.

The sticky note — 'FOR WHEN THEY NEED THE TRUTH. NOT BEFORE' — is mildly interesting but vague enough to mean anything. Researchers always think their work is the most important thing in the world. The neighbor clearly believed his sealed cabinet contained something of tremendous significance. Waluigi is sure it did. To the neighbor.

Waluigi sees no reason to investigate further. The neighbor moved. Wario moved. The folders are gone. The cabinet is presumably wherever the neighbor relocated to. This is a closed account of one idiot trying to break into one paranoid man's house and finding exactly the kind of boring, incomprehensible technical material that boring, incomprehensible technical people keep in their basements.

Waluigi is moving on to more important matters.

WAH.

## Addendum: Wario's Final Comment

During the third telling — in the Feywild, while trying to sell garlic — Wario mentioned one additional detail that he had not included in previous accounts. Waluigi records it here for completeness, though it is probably not significant.

Wario said: 'The neighbor left in a hurry, right? Like someone called him. And when I was leaving the basement, I saw his desk upstairs — the one near the front door. There was a communicator on it. Still active. Still connected. And there was a voice coming through it. Faint. But I heard it.'

Waluigi asked what the voice said.

Wario said: 'It said, "Professor, it's happening again. He's emerged. We need the contingency." And then it said a name.'

Waluigi asked what name.

Wario said: 'It said "Mr. L."'

Wario paused.

'And then it said: "Activate Protocol Green Thunder."'

Waluigi asked Wario why he had not mentioned this in the previous two tellings.

Wario shrugged and said: 'You didn't ask.'

Waluigi has no additional commentary on this addendum.

Waluigi is not going to think about it.

Waluigi is moving on.

WAH.

participants.role: Obsessive trespasser — spent three months and five hundred coins breaking into a neighbor's house, found classified materials, stole three folders, profited sixty coins, and completely failed to understand the significance of anything he encountered

participants.name: The Neighbor / 'Mr. Gadd'

outcome: Wario gained basement access, found laboratory complex with classified research, containment tanks, sealed cabinet marked 'FOR WHEN THEY NEED THE TRUTH,' and a sealed door with something breathing behind it. summary: Waluigi obtained fragments of testimony  through channels he will not disclose  describing a medical emergency that occurred shortly after the Brobot engagement at the ruined manor. According to these fragments, Luigi was brought to a medical facility near death after Mr. L's emergence and subdual. A surgeon identified only as 'Dr. Mario'  civilian name possibly 'Dario'  performed emergency surgery. Princess Daisy of Sarasaland was present. Pauline, Mayor of New Donk City, was present. Wario was present. Cranky Kong was present. None of these people should have been in the same room under normal circumstances. The testimony raises questions that Waluigi cannot answer but refuses to stop asking: Who is Dr. Mario? Why does Luigi call him 'Uncle Dario'? Why was Daisy behaving like family rather than a diplomatic ally? Why did Pauline call Luigi 'my man'? Why was Peach's name invoked as though she were alive? And why does every institutional actor in this account seem to already know what happened before being told? Waluigi has assembled what he can. The picture is incomplete. The implications are enormous. WAH.
description:
Waluigi must begin with a warning that applies to this entire entry: NONE of this is confirmed through independent verification. The testimony reached Waluigi through a chain of sources that includes at least one Boo informant, a Regency clerk who was bribed with counterfeit currency  possibly Wario's  and a partial transcript that may or may not have been fabricated after the fact. Waluigi presents this account because the details are too specific to be pure invention, too consistent with known intelligence to be random fabrication, and too disturbing to ignore.

If even HALF of what follows is true, Waluigi's understanding of several key figures in this crisis requires fundamental revision.

## Context: What Preceded This Event

The Battle of the Brobot occurred on 3-4 Aethel, 1040 BF. Mr. L emerged during a ghost-clearing operation at the ruined manor. A Brobot appeared  origin still unexplained. Multiple combatants were injured. Archie was blasted through a wall by a laser beam. Bones was grabbed and nearly killed. Mr. L was subdued through unknown means  freezing mid-punch and going limp as though someone had flipped a switch.

Byscilla Danos executed what she called 'Phase One' of a containment protocol that the Mages' Guild had apparently prepared in advance. She reported: 'Target subdued. We have a target and got a signed spell scroll from Archie.'

What happened AFTER the subdual is what this testimony concerns. According to multiple fragments, Luigi  not Mr. L, but LUIGI, restored to his own personality  was in critical condition. The subdual itself may have caused severe neurological trauma. Whatever mechanism forced Mr. L back into dormancy did not do so gently.

Luigi was transported to a medical facility. The testimony describes what happened in the waiting room and the corridor outside the surgical theater.

## The Surgeon: 'Dr. Mario'

The most explosive element of the testimony is the identity of the surgeon who operated on Luigi.

According to the fragments, the doctor introduced himself  or was referred to by staff  as 'Dr. Mario.' Luigi, in moments of semi-consciousness before being prepped for surgery, called him 'Uncle Dario.' The doctor reportedly corrected this with visible emotion: 'That's Dr. Mario to you.' Then, softer: 'But I always loved when he called me that.'

Waluigi needs to address this directly because it threatens to collapse several load-bearing assumptions of the current investigation.

### Possibility One: 'Dr. Mario' Is Mario

This is the reading that makes Waluigi's head hurt the most.

Mario has been missing since approximately 1039 BF. Waluigi has documented the disappearance extensively  the 985 BF Personnel Reallocation, the border town sighting in civilian clothes, the Star Fountain reunion where Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us as long as we're together,' and then the SECOND separation that left Luigi operating alone under Mages' Guild contract.

If 'Dr. Mario' is Mario operating under the civilian name 'Dario,' it would mean Mario has been hiding in plain sight as a medical professional. The red cap gone. The overalls replaced by surgical scrubs. The hero of the Mushroom Kingdom performing surgery on his own brother while the world thinks he vanished.

This interpretation is supported by several details in the testimony. The emotional familiarity. The use of 'Uncle Dario'  which could be a cover identity Luigi uses to maintain plausible deniability about their relationship. A brother cannot publicly be a brother if one of them is supposed to be missing. But an 'uncle' who is a doctor? That is a relationship that can exist on paper without triggering the warrant charges that include 'Conspiracy to Withhold Material Information regarding Mario's location.'

Luigi calling Mario his 'uncle' in public would be a LIE  but a lie that protects them both. If anyone asks, Luigi has an uncle named Dario who is a doctor. Not a missing brother. Not the most wanted man in Mushroom Kingdom intelligence circles. Just an uncle. Just a doctor. Just a man who happens to look exactly like the plumber who disappeared.

The 'Uncle Dario' cover would also explain something that has always bothered Waluigi about Daisy's relationship with Luigi. Publicly, Daisy and Luigi have been presented as romantic partners  appearing together at sporting events, kart races, party games. Waluigi has seen them side by side at DOZENS of events. The public narrative is boyfriend and girlfriend. But in this testimony, Daisy does not behave like a girlfriend. She behaves like FAMILY. She calls Luigi 'my baby nephew.' She screams with the particular fury of someone whose bloodline is being threatened, not someone whose romantic interest is in danger.

Waluigi's theory: If Mario is 'Dario,' and if Daisy is connected to the Mario family through a relationship that predates the public narrative, then the 'Luigi and Daisy are dating' story was always COVER. A convenient fiction that explained why the Princess of Sarasaland maintained close contact with one of the Mario Brothers without anyone asking uncomfortable questions about WHICH Mario Brother she was actually connected to, or WHY.

Daisy being Luigi's aunt  through marriage to Mario under the name 'Dario,' or through some other family connection  would mean her entire public persona as Luigi's girlfriend was a carefully maintained deception. Every kart race. Every tennis tournament. Every party game where they appeared as a couple. All of it was theater designed to provide a plausible public explanation for a family connection that could not be acknowledged without exposing Mario's location.

Waluigi finds this interpretation simultaneously outrageous and horrifyingly consistent with the available evidence.

### Possibility Two: 'Dr. Mario' Is a Separate Person

The less dramatic interpretation: 'Dario' is genuinely Mario's uncle or cousin. A relative who went into medicine rather than plumbing. A family member whose resemblance to Mario is genetic rather than identical. Luigi calling him 'Uncle Dario' is LITERAL, not cover.

This interpretation is simpler but creates its own problems. If the Mario family has a member who is a practicing surgeon, why has this person never appeared in ANY public record connected to the Mario Brothers? Why would a doctor share the surname and general appearance of the kingdom's most famous hero without anyone commenting on it? Why would this person be available for emergency surgery on a classified patient in a facility that may or may not be Ironmend Bastion?

Waluigi's assessment: the SIMPLER explanation requires MORE coincidences than the complicated one. A secret uncle-surgeon who appears at exactly the right moment is less plausible than Mario himself, operating under cover, maintaining proximity to his brother through a medical alias.

### Possibility Three: Waluigi Is Being Fed Disinformation

Waluigi must acknowledge this possibility. The testimony may be fabricated specifically to make Waluigi believe Mario has been found. Someone who knows Waluigi is investigating Mario's disappearance might plant exactly this kind of account  emotionally compelling, detail-rich, impossible to verify  to redirect Waluigi's investigation toward a false lead.

If 'Dr. Mario' is neither Mario nor a real relative but a fictional figure inserted into a fabricated transcript, then someone is manipulating Waluigi. The question becomes: who benefits from Waluigi believing Mario is alive and practicing medicine under an alias?

Waluigi cannot determine this. Waluigi notes the possibility and continues.

## The Waiting Room: What the Testimony Describes

The bulk of the testimony describes the waiting room during Luigi's surgery. The emotional temperature was volcanic. The cast of characters was improbable. The conversations were revealing in ways that the participants almost certainly did not intend.

### Daisy's Behavior

Daisy arrived at the facility and immediately demanded access to Luigi. She was denied  only 'immediate family and her royal majesty, Princess Peach herself' were permitted inside. Daisy's response was fury on a scale that Waluigi has never associated with diplomatic protocol.

She called Luigi 'my baby nephew.' She said: 'While that boy was still in his first game, he begged me to make sure he stayed happy and healthy. And I promised him!'

Waluigi needs to address the phrase 'his first game.' In Mushroom Kingdom vernacular, 'game' can mean several things: a competitive event, a mission, a campaign. But the way Daisy used it  'his FIRST game'  carries the weight of ORIGIN. The beginning. The moment when Luigi entered public life and needed someone to protect him.

If Daisy is family  and this testimony strongly suggests she is  then her promise to keep Luigi 'happy and healthy' predates the public career. She has been watching over him since the BEGINNING. Every kart race she appeared at alongside him was not a date. It was supervision. Every party game was not romance. It was an aunt keeping her promise.

This reframes Daisy's entire documented history. Her competence at the Second Summit. Her management of Sarasaland. Her quiet fury when systems fail. She has been operating with a PERSONAL stake in the Mario Brothers' survival that she has hidden behind a fake romantic narrative for what appears to be DECADES.

Waluigi's respect for Daisy was already considerable. It has now increased to levels that Waluigi finds structurally uncomfortable.

### The 'Princess Peach' Invocation

The testimony mentions that access to Luigi was restricted to immediate family and 'her royal majesty, Princess Peach herself.' Peach has been dead since 955 BF. Her name should not appear in active access protocols at a medical facility in 1040 BF.

Waluigi has three interpretations:

**One:** The protocol is OLD. Written decades ago and never updated. Peach's name remains on a list that nobody has bothered to revise because bureaucracy outlives the people it was designed to serve. This is the boring interpretation and therefore probably correct.

**Two:** The protocol is ACTIVE. Someone with authority has maintained Peach's name on access lists deliberately  either as a dead key that no one should be able to use, or as a living authorization for someone using Peach's identity. If a secret heir exists  if Peach's child with Thornpaw survived  that child might operate under the mother's access privileges. This interpretation makes Waluigi dizzy.

**Three:** The person who stated the protocol was using 'Princess Peach' as a CODE. A signal to other initiated parties that the situation was of the highest classification. Invoking a dead princess's name as an access credential is exactly the kind of theatrical security measure that the Regency and the Mages' Guild would consider clever.

Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct.

### The Question of Mario's Location

During the waiting room chaos, 'Dr. Mario' was asked about Mario  the public Mario, the missing hero. The response, as recorded in the testimony: 'Mario can't come right now. He's far away on the front lines, risking it all for us against Bowser's legions.'

Daisy's response: 'For what? You going to tell me Peach has been kidnapped again, too?'

The staff member's response: 'That's classified information.'

Daisy: 'I was FUCKING joking. Are you kidding me?'

Waluigi needs to parse this carefully.

If 'Dr. Mario' IS Mario, then his staff providing a cover story about 'Mario being on the front lines' is part of the deception. Mario cannot be present as a surgeon AND absent on the front lines unless two separate narratives are being maintained simultaneously  one for the public, one for those inside the facility.

The 'Peach kidnapped' exchange is more troubling. Daisy made a SARCASTIC comment. The staff member's response  'That's classified information'  implies that someone, somewhere, is running an operation under the heading of 'Peach kidnapped.' In 1040 BF. Eighty-five years after Peach's assassination.

Either someone is using Peach's name as a mission codename  'Operation Peach Kidnapped' or similar  or there is classified information about Peach's status that contradicts the official death record. Waluigi does not have enough evidence to determine which. Waluigi's headache has intensified.

### Pauline's Presence

Mayor Pauline of New Donk City arrived and referred to Luigi as 'my man.' Her behavior was that of a romantic partner in crisis  desperate, emotional, focused entirely on Luigi's survival.

If Daisy is Luigi's aunt rather than his girlfriend, then Pauline being Luigi's ACTUAL romantic partner resolves the relationship question cleanly. The public 'Luigi and Daisy' narrative served as cover. The private reality is 'Luigi and Pauline.'

This makes a certain amount of sense. Pauline's position as mayor of New Donk City places her outside the Mushroom Kingdom's direct political sphere. A relationship between Luigi and Pauline would attract less factional attention than one between Luigi and a foreign princess. If the goal was to protect Luigi's personal life from becoming political leverage  which, given the warrant situation, was a reasonable concern  then publicizing a fake relationship with Daisy while maintaining a real one with Pauline is exactly the kind of misdirection that someone with intelligence training would arrange.

Who arranged it? Waluigi does not know. But the sophistication of the cover  maintained across decades of public appearances, sporting events, and social functions  suggests institutional support rather than personal initiative. Luigi is not cunning enough to maintain a deception this complex on his own. Someone HELPED him. The Mages' Guild. The Regency. Daisy herself. Mario. Possibly all of the above.

### Wario's Appearance

Wario appeared in the waiting room and immediately began antagonizing everyone. This is completely consistent with Wario's documented behavior and requires no special analysis.

However, several details from Wario's interactions are significant:

Wario claimed he needed to 'clear up a few things' with Mario and that 'my people had some very concerning intelligence to share.' This implies Wario has intelligence networks that have generated actionable information about Mario. Given Wario's financial operations and underworld contacts, this is plausible. Wario may know things about Mario's situation that even Waluigi does not.

Wario mentioned his cancer going into remission 'not long after the faking of my death and Warioland's first dissolution.' Waluigi's assessment: the cancer was REAL but its severity was exaggerated to make the faked death more convincing. The remission is genuine. The 'terminal' diagnosis was fabricated to provide motive for a plausible suicide. This is exactly the kind of layered deception Wario excels at  embedding real medical information inside a larger fraud to make the whole package more convincing.

Wario also offered to 'speak to Dr. Mario instead' about his cancer remission, treating the surgeon as though he were an ordinary doctor. Either Wario does not know that 'Dr. Mario' might be Mario, or Wario DOES know and is performing ignorance. With Wario, both are equally plausible.

Waluigi would like the record to note that Wario's appearance at the facility constitutes a PUBLIC INDECENCY CHARGE by proxy because Waluigi was mentioned by name in connection with an incident that Waluigi has ALREADY BEEN PUNISHED FOR and does not wish to discuss further. Daisy's comment about Waluigi's 'public appearance being strictly regulated' is accurate and Waluigi resents that it was stated in front of Wario, who will absolutely use it as leverage later.

### Cranky Kong's Appearance

Cranky Kong appeared at the facility 'off his meds' and immediately began using language that Waluigi will not reproduce. He claimed responsibility for Luigi's injuries  'I blew him away earlier with my Coconut Gun for crossing me'  which contradicts the established account of Mr. L's emergence being the cause.

Waluigi's assessment: Cranky was lying or delusional. His claim is inconsistent with every other account of the Brobot incident. However, Cranky's mention of DK hiding his original Coconut Gun is potentially significant for reasons unrelated to this particular incident  it suggests internal Kong family conflicts that parallel the Mario Brothers' fractured relationships.

Cranky was eventually redirected when Pauline received urgent intelligence requiring her to leave for Kong Island airport. The nature of that intelligence is unknown but prompted immediate departure, suggesting a crisis of considerable magnitude.

### The Pharmaceutical Incident

The testimony's final fragment describes Wario encountering Cranky Kong in the facility's corridors and proposing a joint robbery of the hospital pharmacy. An unidentified individual  possibly a janitor, possibly an orderly, possibly someone with no medical credentials whatsoever  offered to forge prescriptions in exchange for Cranky's participation.

The individual also mentioned having 'a pretty cool idea for the lawsuit that would follow' if Cranky 'accidentally died from the phony prescriptions overdose.'

Waluigi notes this exchange because it demonstrates the complete breakdown of institutional security at the facility. If Wario and Cranky Kong can openly discuss pharmacy robbery and prescription fraud in a corridor where a classified patient is undergoing emergency surgery, then the facility's security protocols are either deliberately lax or have been compromised.

This supports Waluigi's broader assessment that institutional competence in the Mushroom Kingdom has degraded to the point where NOTHING works as intended and EVERYONE is operating according to personal agendas rather than organizational mandates.

## The Surgery Itself

The testimony provides minimal information about the actual surgical procedure. 'Dr. Mario' stated that Luigi was 'on the verge of brain death' and that saving him was uncertain. He referenced an 'Extra Life'  in Mushroom Kingdom medical terminology, this refers to emergency resuscitation protocols derived from Star Power applications. The phrase 'I won't let an Extra Life be wasted after what's happened today' suggests the facility had access to magical medical resources that are not available at standard hospitals.

The outcome of the surgery is not documented in the testimony fragments Waluigi has obtained. Luigi appeared alive and operational at Raventree Manor in subsequent events, so the surgery was presumably successful. But the gap between 'verge of brain death' and 'functional ghost hunter' is ENORMOUS, and whatever happened in that surgical theater may have changed Luigi in ways that are not yet apparent.

Waluigi wonders whether Luigi's subsequent behavior  the Poltergust escape, the silence on the Mr. L question, the apparent willingness to work for the Guild  might be partially explained by neurological changes resulting from emergency surgery performed by a man who may or may not be his brother operating under a false name.

## What This Changes

If the testimony is authentic  and Waluigi rates it as PARTIALLY AUTHENTIC based on internal consistency and correlation with known intelligence  then several elements of the current crisis require reinterpretation.

**Mario's disappearance** may not be a disappearance at all. It may be an identity change, with Mario operating as 'Dr. Dario' in a medical capacity, maintaining proximity to Luigi while remaining invisible to the factions hunting him. The 985 BF Personnel Reallocation may have been the Regency's attempt to neutralize him, and Mario responded not by fleeing east but by becoming someone else entirely.

**Luigi and Daisy's relationship** may have been fabricated to provide cover for a genuine family connection  Daisy as aunt, not girlfriend  which in turn may connect to Mario's hidden identity as 'Dario.' If Daisy married into the Mario family under a name that the public does not associate with the Mario Brothers, her entire diplomatic career gains an additional layer of motive.

**Luigi and Pauline's relationship** may be the ACTUAL romantic connection, hidden behind the Daisy cover for political protection. Pauline's emotional response in the testimony is consistent with a real partner, not a diplomatic contact.

**The Mages' Guild's 'Phase One'** may have included arranging Luigi's transport to a specific facility where 'Dr. Mario' was stationed. If the Guild knows Mario's cover identity, their leverage over Luigi becomes even more terrifying  they do not merely know where Mario is, they have him working within their operational infrastructure as a medical asset.

**Wario's intelligence networks** may have independently identified 'Dr. Mario' as Mario, which would explain why Wario showed up at the facility and why he wanted to 'clear up a few things.' Wario does not visit hospitals out of concern for others. Wario visits because there is something he wants.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing the Mario disappearance. Waluigi has documented the Star Fountain reunion, the Eastern Passage theories, the 985 BF emergency session, the border town sighting. Waluigi has built a narrative of a hero who was exiled, who investigated a conspiracy alone, who reunited with his brother briefly before being separated again.

This testimony suggests a DIFFERENT narrative. One where Mario never fully left. One where the 'disappearance' was an identity death, not a physical one. One where Mario became someone else  someone useful, someone invisible, someone who could remain near the people he loved without triggering the institutional responses that would follow if 'Mario' were found.

A plumber becomes a doctor. A hero becomes an uncle. A public figure becomes a private man with a new name and surgical scrubs instead of overalls.

Waluigi does not know if this is true. The testimony could be fabrication. The details could be misinterpreted. 'Uncle Dario' could be a genuine relative and the entire Mario-as-surgeon theory could be Waluigi seeing patterns in coincidence.

But Waluigi remembers something from the Mario entry: 'You don't abandon your identity unless you're trying to become someone else. Or unless someone MADE you abandon it.'

Mario without his cap. Mario in civilian clothes. Mario asking about routes east. And now, possibly, Mario in a surgical theater, saving his brother's life under a name that no one would think to search for.

If Mario chose to become 'Dr. Dario'  if he chose anonymity, service, and proximity over heroism, fame, and visibility  then Waluigi has been wrong about Mario in a way that Waluigi finds genuinely difficult to process.

Mario did not run. Mario did not hide. Mario became someone who could HELP without being SEEN.

That is either the most noble thing Waluigi has ever documented or the most elaborate cover story anyone has ever constructed.

Waluigi suspects it is both.

And somewhere in a hospital that no one will confirm exists, a surgeon who may or may not be the most famous plumber in history is washing his hands and checking on his brother's recovery and hoping that no one notices the resemblance.

Waluigi noticed.

Waluigi always notices.

WAH.
