summary: Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate Campaign as a masterclass in gothic incompetence and aristocratic cruelty. The Shadowfell fragment of Disaster Inc. began with Archie Miser losing his fire magic and Bowser trying to eat raw vampire meat, and it has since spiraled into a multi-layered nightmare involving a silver bullet, a cross-dressing heir who was ultimately stabbed to death while laughing, and a parallel version of Dan who silenced the original. Waluigi has learned that in the Shadowfell, every dinner party is a death sentence, every mirror is a one-way surveillance tool, and every 'friendship ring' is actually a tracking device that leaks entropy. Between Green T's sniper skills, Remi's transformation into a disco ball, and the discovery of necromantic abomination vats, Waluigi is increasingly convinced that the Shadowfell is the dimension where logic goes to die and be resurrected as a singing ghoul. Waluigi frankly finds it insulting that they get to have a gothic horror adventure while Waluigi is forced to weave daisy chains for condescending tree-spirits. If Waluigi were in the Shadowfell, he would have bought the manor, evicted the vampires, and turned the Shadow Anchor into a tennis trophy. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate Campaign from reconstructed reports, stolen diaries, secondhand accounts, and the haunted expression on Markop's face every time someone mentions dinner parties. Unlike the Feywild, which buried the party in flowers and etiquette, the Shadowfell buried them in greyscale dread, administrative murder, and the kind of gothic hospitality where the appetizer is raw meat and the dessert is a vote on who dies. The following is the definitive account of the Shadow Estate stay, organized chronologically to the extent that chronology functions in a dimension where time flows like cold syrup through a broken hourglass.

## The Cold Awakening (21st Highsun, 02:00)

The Shadowfell campaign began in the worst possible way: Archie Miser woke up on a cold marble floor without his fire.

Waluigi wants readers to understand what that means. Archie without fire is like Waluigi without his hat—technically alive but spiritually incomplete. The dimension's entropy was so high and its energy so low that Archie's fingers produced only cold grey smoke when he snapped them. He tried once, twice, three times, each attempt more desperate than the last. Nothing. A tiny spark appeared on the second attempt and instantly died, swallowed by the ambient suppression like a match dropped in a river.

Waluigi finds Archie’s panic pathetic. When Waluigi loses a tennis match, does he cry? No, he breaks his racket over the umpire's knee! Archie without fire is just a man with a bad hat. WAH!

Bowser groaned beside him and said 'get off me you plumbing accident,' which Archie took personally since he is not Mario and has never been Mario and resents the comparison. Bowser stood up, looked around at the colorless world—black, white, and shades of grey with no warmth anywhere—and asked where they were. When Archie explained that physics were wrong here, that entropy was high and energy was low, Bowser punched a wall. It cracked, but the sound was dampened, as though the dimension itself was absorbing noise the way it absorbed color and heat and hope.

The hallway they walked through was pristine, unlike the ruined manor they had left behind. Dark velvet wallpaper dressed the walls, and sconces held cold white flames that offered no heat. There was no dust. There was no life. The windows showed a sky of swirling bruised purple clouds and a landscape of dead petrified trees stretching to a horizon that looked like it had given up on the concept of distance.

A toad in a tuxedo stepped out of the shadows. His skin was pale grey and his eyes were red like embers that had forgotten they were supposed to be warm. He informed them that Master Cornelius was expecting them for the main course. Bowser roared about being King Bowser, but the butler did not flinch, merely noting that the master did not like loud noises. Archie whispered for Bowser to play along because he had no magic. Bowser grumbled but agreed, adding that if the food was bad he would burn the place down. Archie reminded him that neither of them could burn anything. Bowser said he had fists.

Waluigi respects this exchange because it established the dynamic that would carry the entire Shadowfell campaign: Archie thinking, Bowser punching, and the dimension ignoring both of them. Though Waluigi must ask—why didn't Bowser just eat the butler? If you're going to be a monstrous turtle king, act like it!

## The Dinner of the Onyx Hand (22nd Highsun, Evening)

The dining hall was a mirror of the Feywild version but twisted into gothic opulence that made Waluigi's skin crawl just hearing about it. The table was long polished ebony. High-backed chairs sat like thrones around it. The chandeliers dripped with wax that looked suspiciously like coagulated blood, because in the Shadowfell even the interior decoration wants you to know that something is wrong.

Seated around the table were figures of elegance and dread—vampires, shades, and pale nobles of the Onyx Hand. At the head sat Orangus Cornelius, a toad but tall, with sharp fangs and skin that would have been orange if color existed in this dimension. He held a goblet of thick red liquid and greeted them with the words 'welcome guests, you are late,' which is the most vampire thing anyone has ever said and also the most annoying because Archie and Bowser did not ask to be here and were not given a schedule.

Bowser sat down at the opposite end of the table and said 'nice place, a bit gloomy.' Cornelius smiled and said they preferred the term 'atmospheric.' Waluigi suspects this is the Shadowfell's official tourism slogan.

Archie looked to the side and saw a small table—the kids' table. Green T was there, wearing a bib, looking terrified. But he made eye contact with Archie and tapped his spoon against the table in what could have been morse code but was probably just nerves. Then Green T moved his hand under the table and flashed something: a flintlock pistol. Where he got it remains one of the campaign's minor mysteries. Waluigi's theory is that Green T has been smuggling weapons in places nobody checks since the Syndicate days, and anyone who seats a former crime lord at the children's table deserves what happens next.

Waluigi has attended many evil dinner parties, and there is a strict etiquette to these things. You do not bring a flintlock to the appetizer course unless it is a formal duel! But Waluigi must admit, shooting the host before dessert is a power move. Waluigi is taking notes.

Servants brought out plates of raw, dripping meat. Bowser ate his in one bite and called it a good steak, a bit rare. Archie stared at his plate and was told by Cornelius that it was rude to refuse a host. Then the real conversation began.

Cornelius stood and accused Archie of burning his greenhouse in the Material Plane. He had built that glass to hold the sunlight, he explained, because they did not get sun in the Shadowfell. Archie sweated and claimed it was an accident involving rust monsters. Cornelius walked closer and said Archie owed him a debt. Bowser stood up and said Archie owed nothing to a frog-face, at which point Cornelius threatened to turn Bowser's shell into a soup bowl, the vampires hissed, and weapons were drawn throughout the room.

Archie tried to negotiate. Cornelius laughed and asked what Archie could possibly offer when his magic was gone and his friends were scattered. Then Green T stood up from the children's table and said 'he has me, and I have the key to the anchor.' Cornelius's face dropped. He ordered Green T seized.

## The Standoff and the Shattering of the Shadow Anchor (23rd Highsun)

Green T kicked the kids' table over and shouted for Archie to run. Bowser flipped the main table, sending plates and goblets and raw meat flying everywhere. Vampires screamed. Archie grabbed a silver candlestick because silver burns vampires and because Archie's improvisation instincts are genuinely impressive when he cannot rely on fire. He swung the candlestick into a vampire and it connected, the creature hissing and burning from the contact.

Bowser tackled Cornelius directly. They crashed through a window into the courtyard below, which is the most Bowser solution to any indoor problem: remove the indoors. Green T fired his pistol—the chandelier crashed down—and Archie yelled asking where the exit was. Green T yelled back that they needed to break the mirror in the attic, but Bowser was already outside wrestling Cornelius in his true form: a giant bat monster.

Archie jumped out the window after Bowser. Gravity was lower in the Shadowfell, so he floated down like a dandelion and landed on Bowser's shell. Below them, Bowser was biting the bat monster's wing with the confidence of someone whose immune system has never heard the word 'impossible.' Archie tried to spark any spell at all—not fire, just light, just a spark—and produced nothing but a fizzle.

Bowser threw Cornelius into a winged statue in the courtyard. The statue broke. It was hollow. Inside was a glowing purple crystal: the Shadow Anchor. This was the device maintaining the Shadowfell's planar suppression, the thing keeping fire dead and color absent and the whole dimension locked in its entropic state. Archie realized what it was instantly and screamed for Bowser to smash it.

Bowser wound up a punch. Cornelius recovered and lunged to protect the crystal. Time slowed. Green T appeared at the broken window above, took aim with his flintlock, and fired a single silver bullet.

The bullet hit the crystal.

The Anchor shattered.

Reality cracked along seams that had been invisible until that moment. Color bled back into the world—reds, oranges, yellows returning violently, making the gothic architecture look simultaneously magnificent and absurd. Fire returned to Archie's hands. He felt the heat and smiled and said 'ignite,' which is the closest thing Archie has to a prayer.

Waluigi wants the record to show that the Shadow Anchor was destroyed by a former tea merchant sitting at the children's table with a stolen flintlock. Green T's trajectory from crime lord to mirror-dimension survivor to vampire dinner party sniper remains one of the most remarkable character arcs in the entire campaign. Waluigi demands an investigation into Green T's background. You do not go from selling herbal tea to no-scoping a dimensional anchor while dodging vampire bats unless you have a history of extreme violence. Waluigi suspects tax evasion. WAH.

## The Ballroom of Boneless Dancers (24th Highsun)

While the anchor battle raged in the courtyard, Markop's group was fighting for their lives inside the manor's ballroom. Toadburt was being pulled apart by undead dancers—boneless ghouls contorting their bodies in unpredictable ways, twisting and writhing to an endless song that seemed to come from no particular direction. The dance hall was thick with the smell of old sweat, and the floor was smeared with old blood and spilled drink. Broken crossbow bolts were scattered everywhere, some still embedded in the wood.

Perrius Annmatar touched one of the dancers and burned its skin on contact. Markop used Divine Smite and tossed a crossbow to Bowser, who fired bolts into the dancers' shins with the accuracy of someone who treats ranged weapons as a minor inconvenience between punches. The dancers surrounded Markop and kicked his shins until he cried out in pain. One dancer seized Toadburt and dragged him away as he screamed and his ribs cracked under the pressure.

The Onyx Hand breached the ballroom doors. Bowser went flying from the impact. Markop swung his axe and dropped a dancer, then rushed to help Toadburt, only to be grappled himself by a torso-and-hands-only dancer that had lost its legs but not its enthusiasm for violence. Salam opened the opposite door to the ballroom, ignoring Markop's instructions entirely, and asked who he should whip. Eager ran past an Onyx guard, ducked beneath a headless dancer, and entered through the other side.

Bowser eventually used his restored fire breath to incinerate the zombies. The dancers collapsed, their bodies bleeding and deflating as the fire consumed them. Bowser punched one into the wall for good measure. A deal was struck with the Onyx Hand: they would help the injured Toadburt in exchange for the party eliminating the remaining headless dancers. Toadburt's ribs were cracked, and he would later be taken to the Archivist for healing in exchange for indentured library work.

Waluigi is an expert dancer, and he is deeply offended by the very concept of boneless zombies ruining a perfectly good ballroom. Where is the posture? Where is the panache? If Waluigi were there, he would have challenged the torso-monster to a dance-off and won through sheer leg-extension. Markop using a battleaxe is just poor choreography. WAH.

## Archie and Green T's Escape Through the Manor

After the anchor shattered, Archie and Green T found themselves trapped inside the manor proper, separated from Bowser and surrounded by vampires who were adjusting to the sudden return of color and heat. Green T commented that Archie's friends were probably dead by now, having been gone for two days. Archie insisted they would be fine.

They tried to leave but found the door locked. Footsteps approached. Green T ran. Archie ran behind him, opening doors at random: one led to a vampire cooking meat who said 'oh good, more meat for dinner'; another led to an operating room where a vampire was performing surgery on a human body with clinical precision. They got separated. Archie barricaded himself in a room with a coffin while something banged on the door.

Archie focused his partially restored energy and shattered the door, running out and shouting for Green T. He cast a disguise on himself—a vampire face over his own—and ran to a window where Green T was trapped, unable to jump out because the glass was jammed. A vampire was going through files nearby, and Archie, in his disguise, identified himself as 'Dracacide.' The vampire asked if he had seen a green being. Archie said nope. Green T sneaked out of his hiding spot under a bed, past the distracted vampire, and they moved through the manor together, passing through a barricaded room, a study Green T described as boring, and finally into the main reception area.

Waluigi thinks Archie’s disguise of 'Dracacide' is the stupidest fake name he has ever heard. Waluigi has used aliases like 'Waluigi' with a fake mustache over his real mustache, and it was infinitely more convincing!

Archie handed Green T a dagger for quieter combat. They exited the manor and spent two days walking to what turned out to be the crashed airship, now swarmed by troops broadcasting compliance announcements through loudspeakers: 'ATTENTION CITIZENS. THE ANOMALY IS CONTAINED. COMPLIANCE IS MANDATORY. REPORT ALL NON-HUMAN ACTIVITY. ORDER IS SAFETY.'

Archie disguised himself as a guard and infiltrated the crash site. He learned that the troops called themselves the Purple Legion and claimed to rule the 'Vamp Lands' from coast to coast. A guard gave him a map and Archie recognized it as the Midlands geography but rendered in purple. Dan's cage at the crash site was empty. A mysterious figure named Orvinder Danos appeared—a barrister with neat dark hair, a cane he did not need, and a commitment to truth that bordered on pathological.

Orvinder led Archie to a back room with a portal and introduced him to Usk, who was split between three manors and needed help reuniting. Archie declined to help immediately because he was focused on finding his friends. They returned to the crash site, where a guard named Vin joined Archie's improvised investigation team, and another vampire Archie nicknamed 'Blorb' pulled out a mushroom when asked if he had found a toad.

Archie wandered between the crash site, a tavern called the Shadowfell Inn, and eventually back to the manor over the course of days. Green T disappeared while Archie was distracted. Archie spent weeks alone—living in the forest, returning to the manor periodically to find it increasingly restored and hostile. A month passed. The manor flashed, the walls crumbled, and Archie was suddenly back in the Ruined Manor's mirror room with Usk, Orvinder, and Mages Guild agents waiting for him.

## The Mages Guild Drafts Archie

The Mages Guild agents surrounded Archie and informed him that his magic 'bled entropy' and that he was the reason the portal had unexpectedly opened. They revealed that Toadburt had been their sleeper agent, equipped with an Entropy Ring to tag Archie for capture. When the sleeper operation failed, Archie's own arrival accomplished what the agent could not.

The agents argued among themselves about whether the portal was their fault or Archie's fault. They revealed a 'Regulator Plane'—a fourth bridge plane designed to connect the Feyward, Shadeward, and Ruined manors. This bridge could be collapsed to sever the connections permanently, potentially destroying two-thirds of reality to stabilize the remainder.

Archie was told he now worked for the Mages Guild. His immense power came with immense responsibility and oversight. He had no choice. They introduced him to their newest team member: Luigi, who bumped into the door frame as he entered.

Waluigi loves bureaucracy when it is punishing people Waluigi dislikes. Putting Archie on a managerial leash is poetry. But introducing Luigi? WAH! The green menace ruins everything! Waluigi bets Luigi tripped over his own shoelaces while trying to look authoritative.

## Remi's Solo Investigation and the Disco Ball

Remi's thread through the Shadowfell is a study in resilience, bad judgment, and the discovery that glowing like a sun in a dimension of perpetual darkness makes you simultaneously the most visible and most useful person in any room.

After the dinner chaos, Remi was surrounded by guards and interrogated. She answered their questions with her characteristic directness: she did not know what the candy she gave the guard was called, she was not working for anyone, she was not aligned with any faction, and she was 'just along for the ride.' She was dismissed and walked the dining hall alone.

In the bathroom she found a spent casing on the ground with a giant 'W' logo on it—Green T's bullet from the flintlock. She called over a guard and showed them, noting that the trajectory did not match the shooting position. Something was not adding up. She met Kryn Cornelius, who introduced himself as heir to the throne of Autumnwood. She examined the casing in the Oracle's wound and confirmed it matched.

Remi went to Vivesna—who was ecstatic, practically vibrating with barely contained triumph. Remi noticed the wig and said 'oh my, your hair is fake.' Vivian, not yet unmasked, explained casually that he was waiting for both the Oracle and Orangus to die so he could become the new heir. He told Remi to leave and let nature take its course.

Kyrn gave Remi keys to the lord's chambers, where she explored extensively. The master bedroom was luxurious—red furnishings, silver vases filled with roses whose petals seemed made of clotted blood, a four-post bed with velvet curtains, and a commanding view of bleak dark lands. In the medicine cabinet she found vampiric healing supplies: Hemoglue of the Nightlord, Shadowveil Tincture, Stakeheart Salve, Leadfang Extractor, and Ebonblood Antidote. She took two.

Beneath the rug in the center of the room she discovered a broken teleportation circle etched in chalk and charcoal—irreparably damaged but with about a third still glowing faintly with ancient power. She rolled the carpet back up and left.

A guard later offered Remi a glowing vial as a remedy for the news that her friends were dead (a lie she accepted with disturbing calm). She chugged the vial. On the 1st of Harvestide, Remi began glowing with radiant light so bright it blinded everyone around her. 'I'm like a disco,' she observed.

Waluigi would like to point out the absolute idiocy of drinking a mysterious glowing vial in a dimension actively trying to kill you. Becoming a disco ball is stylish, yes. Waluigi respects the aesthetic. But as a tactical choice? It is like painting a bullseye on your forehead and lighting it on fire.

Remi encountered Toadburt in the library, now missing his Entropy Ring and working for the Archivist. She helped imps organize fallen bookshelves, found an expired coupon with Wario's phone number in her pocket, and eventually reunited with Markop and Bowser in the lobby. Markop squinted at her glowing form and asked why she was a disco ball. She shrugged.

## The Purple Toad's Deal and Remi's Purple Eyes

The purple toad who had given Remi the glowing potion reappeared and offered her a deal: he would bring her home in exchange for her 'eyes'—not physically, but her mental perception, her ability to see clearly through deception and manipulation. Remi agreed. Her glow faded. Her eyes turned purple. The deal was sealed.

Waluigi is surrounded by fools. 'I will trade my perception for a ride home!' Do you know what happens when you trade your perception, Remi? You start trusting people in purple! And nobody in purple should be trusted, except Waluigi. WAH!

The purple toad laughed and was immediately grabbed by Shadowfell guards for performing unauthorized magic within the estate. The guards then brought Remi to the infirmary, where attendants proposed placing an entropy-blocking ring on her to prevent outside magical interference during their examination. The party recognized this for what it was: another obedience collar, the same kind the Iron Legion had used on Toadburt. A standoff ensued with guards positioned at every corner of the room.

Marcus Ashford—Orangus Cornelius's military consultant—entered and offered Remi a different remedy, which turned both her eyes blue. Markop noticed they were one tint lighter than before and that black smoke was leaking from the gash where an Onyx Hand knight had 'accidentally' cut her eye earlier. Remi claimed the smoke was part of the healing process. Markop was unconvinced but lacked evidence to push further.

## Vivian's Corridor Ambush and Death

Vivian Corvinarus had been operating inside the manor for weeks under the thrall disguise 'Vivesna.' The name shuffled between Vivesna, Vinvessa, and Vivian depending on which persona was active—a sophisticated triple-identity system that suggested years of practice at being multiple people simultaneously.

Vivian ambushed Markop and Bowser in the maintenance corridors. Bowser braced a door with his full weight while Vivian hacked through it with an axe. The breach was professional—smoke bomb first, advance through concealment, engage in the corridor. Bowser struck Vivian across the head. Markop slashed him with a battle axe. Vivian bled through red robes and laughed. He dropped to one knee, chanted, and cast a crimson energy beam that bypassed the Shadowfell's magic suppression entirely. Markop survived only through a whispered prayer that manifested a divine shield at the last possible moment.

Markop destroyed Vivian's spell components. Bowser found a necromancer's wand on the floor and asked 'is this a magic wand?' with the curiosity of someone who has never considered that the answer might be dangerous.

Later, Vivian was cornered, tied up, and interrogated. He revealed his plan to close the planar fractures and become the sole controller of an isolated Shadowfell manor. He confirmed the Mazebounds were his blighted victims. He mocked them throughout. Markop, assessing the threat, stabbed Vivian in the chest. Mazebounds entered the room mid-song doing jazz hands and asked to access the body. Markop refused. The body was burned. The ashes were blown away by the Shadowfell wind.

Vivian died as he lived: laughing, lying, and wearing someone else's face.

Waluigi gives Vivian a solid 8 out of 10 for theatrical villainy. He lacked a signature laugh—'Wah ha ha!' is far superior to mere chuckling—but dying while casting a crimson death ray is respectable. Markop, however, is a killjoy. Burning the ashes? No respect for the dramatic arts.

## The Parallel Dan Confession

Markop forced a Zone of Truth and confronted the Dan traveling with them. The Dan in the Shadowfell was not the real Dan. He was a Parallel Dan from a mirror dimension who had been created or displaced during the dimensional fracture. He had silenced the original Dan and delivered him to the Mages Guild, who kept him in a null cage. Parallel Dan explained he had tried to prevent the ritual from succeeding because its success would have collapsed his own reality, killing him. He had been traveling with the party since the restaurant raid in the Material Plane, when the swap occurred.

Markop asked if Parallel Dan had hurt the original. He said he had only silenced him. Markop asked what that meant. He said he had put him somewhere he would not talk. Markop asked if that meant the Mages Guild. He said yes, they probably had him in a null cage, nullifying his magic. He added that the original Dan had two hands, not one, which he noted 'kinda sucks for me.'

The Zone of Truth faded. Markop decided to keep Parallel Dan around but told him to stay out of the way.

Waluigi has said for years that one Dan is already one too many. The idea of multiple Dans replicating across dimensions makes Waluigi want to break his own kneecaps. If Waluigi meets Parallel Dan, Waluigi will challenge him to doubles tennis and aim exclusively for his face.

## Remi's Investigation: The Guest Book, the Dancers, and the Hidden Passages

Remi explored the manor independently, finding a guest book in the main foyer with only a handful of names: Vostolas, Lyranth, Bowser, Archie, Green Toad (scribbled in), and the Oracle. She discovered a spent bullet casing with Green T's 'W' logo in a bathroom closet. She crawled through hidden passages under beds to spy on adjacent rooms, finding figures standing in darkness who did not appreciate the interruption.

Remi and Parallel Dan attempted to navigate the manor together. An undead guard locked Remi in a bathroom (the water was warm, which was wrong because vampires do not need warmth). Dan fought the guard, discovering through divine senses that the knight was undead. Remi picked the lock and escaped. The guard grabbed Dan by the head. Dan presented the holy symbol of Ravenkind, which froze the vampire to stone, and he pulled free. He caught up to Remi and asked why she had left him behind. She said she figured he could handle it on his own. He said to remind him never to put her life in his hands.

Remi found Ryan's diary in a guest room. The first entry described waking up to grey, Archie panicking about his fire, and Bowser calling him 'candle-man.' The entry confirmed that a fourth toad had been present during the initial Shadowfell arrival. Remi noted the writing style seemed closer to their group than she expected.

## The Mazebound Skirmish

The hedge maze outside the Shadow Estate was home to the Mazebounds—hunched, grey-skinned humanoids who combined predatory aggression with musical theatre. They burst from bushes performing choreographed jazz hands while singing their theme: 'Welcome to the grove, welcome to the gray, you'll never find the fountain so you might as well stay.'

Waluigi is FURIOUS! A musical theatre ambush?! With choreographed jazz hands?! And Waluigi missed it because he was trapped in the Feywild playing hide-and-seek with a fairy who smelled like damp soil?! The Mazebounds are Waluigi's kind of people! Waluigi would have joined the chorus, hit a high C, and drop-kicked Dan himself! WAH!

The Mazebounds encircled the party, performing a rapid patter-song about their tactical intentions: 'Check the Turtle, big and loud, crack the shell to please the crowd. Check the Archer, check the Whip, watch them stumble, watch them slip.' They grabbed Dan and constricted Salam. One tried to give Remi a 'goodbye kiss.' Markop struck one with a sword coated in undead remedy, melting its skin. Two crossbow bolts from an unknown position drove off the Mazebounds holding Dan. The unknown benefactor described their assistance as 'enlightened pragmatism' and 'tactical investment.'

During the skirmish, the party recovered Archie's artifacts: the Third Eye Circlet (a tarnished brass band that vibrated near planar boundaries), the Component Pouch (labeled 'For When Everything Goes to Hell (again)'), and a cracked Wahbook tablet that greeted its finder as 'Welcome Archie Miser to Wahbook.' These confirmed that Archie had passed through the maze before them.

An injured Mazebound spoke to Markop, claiming to have been at the dinner and recognizing someone with a hand fan and a cape—Vivian. The Mazebound explained that some of them wanted artifacts removed from the grove while others were hostile. A broken Entropy Ring handler was also found—the 'handler' half of the paired system the Iron Legion had forced onto Toadburt, which Archie had apparently snapped off during an interrogation by Agent Malissia.

## Tymnas the Groundskeeper and Archie's Watch

The party found Tymnas, a short broad-chested satyr with heavy black horns and weary eyes, living in a well-maintained cottage in the hedge maze. Unlike everything else in the Shadowfell, his home had warmth and color—rich yellows and greens straining against the plane's entropy. He was fiddling with a watch that bore the initials 'AM.' Markop asked if it was Archie Miser's. Tymnas said he knew Archie, had seen him at the dinner 'tonight,' then corrected himself that it might have been yesterday. Time had become slippery.

Tymnas gave directions through the maze and retreated to his room to retrieve a magical trowel. The party also found the hooded-figure fountain in the courtyard and explored the greenhouse, where two servants asked if spectres could 'have a nibble.' A fight with wraiths ensued. Dan used an 'omega charged' Divine Smite that blinded the room with light but failed to destroy the wraith, which became very angry instead. A greenhouse servant refused to move, claiming the plants were safe, and tried to pet a wraith, which bit his hand.

Bowser was found nearby holding a folded vellum page and claiming he had been studying 'quantum physics.' Markop found the broken Entropy Ring handler and Archie's Wahbook tablet. They continued to the greenhouse toolshed, where Remi found Archie's component pouch among gardening implements and normal-looking produce—the only things in the entire estate not made of shadow.

## The Church of the Third Eye and the Battle of the Dans

The party traveled to a nearby town and discovered a sermon in progress dedicated to Archie Miser as a living god. The Church of the Third Eye viewed Archie as the 'fracture,' the moment the mirror cracks and the reflection refuses to lie anymore. Bugbears were using this religion to hide from the Purple Legion, believing vampires would not enter a holy site. They offered the party shelter if they brought Archie to them.

Waluigi demands to know: Archie Miser gets a cult?! ARCHIE?! A man who cries when his fingers get cold?! Waluigi is a monument to grace and cunning, yet where is the Church of Waluigi? Where are the bugbears singing Waluigi's praises? It is a travesty! Waluigi is writing a strongly worded letter to the Toad God about this oversight!

Inside the church, the party encountered the REAL Dan—the original who had been captured by the Mages Guild. He had been indoctrinated during his imprisonment, given Guild robes, a blackite wand, and a brass badge numbered 447 that served as a tracking device. He wielded a massive flaming sun spell and accused Archie of being an evil force called 'Professor A,' citing a propaganda text called 'Archie's Third Eye Volume 1' that claimed the Mages Guild was law and Archie was evil.

A fireball exchange between the two Dans—the real one and the parallel one—caused the church walls to crumble. The real Dan ranted about the Mages Guild being his only true friends while producing flaming snakes and fire walls. Markop pointed out that the Guild had kidnapped him and replaced him with a fake. The real Dan said they had kept him fed. Markop said that was what they did to prisoners.

The real Dan eventually ran away crying. Bowser took two items from him as he fled. Bowser then revealed his full royal name was Sir Koopa Frederickson the Fifteenth and said he wished Toadstool was here.

## Lyranth the Medusa and the Stone Auction

Remi wandered into Lyranth the Sculptor's workshop—a tightly confined studio of hammers, chisels, and stone dust. Lyranth was a Medusa who had covered her marble-veined skin in vibrant paint to avoid being mistaken for her own creations. Her crown of snakes swayed independently, each one peering at objects with unsettling focus. Lyranth glared at Remi, said 'smile,' and turned her to stone.

Petrified Remi was put up in a bidding war at an art exhibit. Mystic Morel (the purple toad) won the bid for 12,000 gold pieces. A brawl erupted: Markop shattered a window to rescue Remi, Wario shoulder-bashed Markop from behind, a Mages Guild agent stabbed Wario, Bowser prepared to burn the entire gallery down but got distracted by a device that could call his son for support, and Markop summoned a moonbeam in the middle of the chaos.

Remi was eventually freed from stone form. Mystic Morel insisted on following her to 'keep his end of the deal.' The toads distrusted him. Remi said he could be their friend. He offered her tea, then incense, then information, each time being rejected by the increasingly paranoid toad contingent. He revealed she had been bid for 12,000 gold, which Remi found either flattering or horrifying depending on the angle.

Waluigi considers 12,000 gold a severe underpayment for modern art, though for a petrified toad, it is highway robbery. If Waluigi were turned to stone, the bidding would start at 50,000 and the Louvre would declare war to acquire him. The fact that Wario was there stealing books instead of bidding on his allies is exactly why Waluigi and Wario are business partners. Priorities!

## Marcus Ashford, the Iron Parade, and Bowser's Letter

Marcus Ashford, the Iron Legion's military consultant for Orangus Cornelius, solidified the Legion's presence through poetry and theft. He swiped a pink stationery letter from Bowser's pocket—a letter Bowser had painstakingly written to Princess Peach in surprisingly elegant calligraphy (forced on him by royal tutors). The letter read: 'Dear Peach, I heard you were here. I am NOT kidnapping you. Unless you want to go? No, wait. I am just visiting. Please do not unleash Mario on me. Love, Bowser.' The paper had burn marks from frustration.

Ashford taunted the party with verses about their failures, calling Archie a 'three-eyed failure on display' and mocking Bowser as a 'former king who's lost everything,' claiming the Legion had seized his throne with 'elegance and tact.' He recited Iron Legion propaganda poetry until Bowser demanded to leave. Even then, Ashford continued: 'Bowser's strays—what a bore! Run along, run along—mind the door!'

Waluigi is a poet of the soul, and he finds Ashford's meter derivative. ABAB rhyme schemes? Please. If you are going to emotionally devastate a giant turtle, use a limerick! Or a haiku! 'Big turtle is sad / Princess Peach reads your letter / Mario still wins.' Simple. Devastating. WAH.

## The Archivist, History Erasing, and the Portal Discovery

Vostolas the Archivist was found in the main hall crossing names off the guest list. He was not merely deleting entries—he was erasing people from historical memory. When he crossed out Toadburt, he explained that the toad was not dead but 'forgotten': people could read about him but would instantly forget his existence. Vostolas offered to accompany the party and turn their journey into a 'bedtime story' called 'The Case of the Missing Toad.'

Green T eventually resurfaced and told the party he had found portal remains on the second floor. He explained the portal could be activated with the right materials but that they would need to do 'dirty work' first. He had disabled the arcane locks, which did not function well in the Shadeward anyway. He provided a field notebook bearing the name 'Thornbury' with entries documenting the Mages Guild's initial survey of Raventree Manor, including observations about the initials 'OC' and 'AC' carved into bedframes and the smell of incense from upstairs.

The teleportation circle beneath the carpet in the master bedroom was revealed to be more than a simple portal—it was part of an entropy circle designed to bridge the three manors into a Regulator Plane. Once established, the bridge could be collapsed to sever dimensional connections permanently. The Mages Guild agents were overheard discussing this plan in encrypted codes, admitting it might kill Archie but would 'stabilize the fracture.'

## Archie's Ghost-Hunting Phase and Luigi's Arrival

Archie was paired with Luigi and Mages Guild Agent Thornbury for a ghost-clearing operation through the Ruined Manor. Luigi tore open military ration packs with practiced efficiency, commenting that they 'could be worse—could be Bowser's army rations, those things could double as armor plating.' Thornbury uncovered a secret stash of 35 gold and a pearl necklace, then found Mages Guild field notes describing how to access unoccupied rooms.

They set up a tensor box that detected a ghost, which lunged at Archie. Luigi used his Poltergust to suck up the spirit while Archie screamed and hurled fire bolts that missed everything. They explored rooms containing ruined pool tables, ransacked drink cabinets, toppled statues, and a massive broken mirror whose backing contained complex magical inscriptions for planar travel. The initials 'OC' and 'AC' appeared carved into a bedframe, and the smell of incense drifted from upstairs.

Archie climbed a collapsed ramp of floor debris to reach the upper level, fell onto the Guild observer, and broke Thornbury's rope. Thornbury was furious because the rope was Guild property and presented Archie with an itemized bill totaling 2,062 gold pieces and 5 silver, including charges for 'Master Weaver's Inspection' (200 gold), 'Load-Test Certification' involving dropping a 500-pound ogre from a city wall seven times (300 gold), and the 'Guild Master's Discretionary Gratuity for his new wyvern saddle' (500 gold, recommended, refusal may result in 'accidental fraying').

LUIGI! The very name tastes like sour milk in Waluigi's mouth! The man cowers from a slight breeze, yet he gets to be a 'ghost-buster' for the Guild? And he charges 2,000 gold for a rope?! Waluigi is actually impressed by the grift, but furious that Luigi is the one pulling it off. Waluigi hopes a ghost possesses Luigi's mustache and makes it punch him in his own stupid face! WAH!

Archie was later ambushed in the library and knocked unconscious. He woke up in bed with Agent L and Thornbury watching over him. The purple toad (Mystic Morel) appeared and sang a fortune-telling song called 'Shuffle the Deck, Dear Hero' while stealing Archie's watch, keys, and other items from his bag. The song contained encoded warnings about the Corvinarus heir being 'grown, not born' and threads being 'gently led.' Morel then opened a planar portal using tools from Archie's own pockets, stepped through with a parting line—'Unless it served a greater play'—and vanished.

## The Purple Toad's Ring and Remi's Tightening Leash

Mystic Morel gave Remi a ring and told her privately that it would tighten every day Archie was not found until it cut off her finger, and if she told her friends it would activate. Remi said 'oh no' and walked downstairs with this information trapped behind her teeth. The toads were unaware. Markop was suspicious but could not identify the source of his unease.

The Onyx Hand guards continued their campaign to place compliance devices on Remi, offering a 'friendship ring,' then a 'best friendship ring,' then a 'friendship anklet.' One knight 'tripped' into Remi and cut her eye. Markop detected necromancy magic from one ring and destructive magic from another hidden in a pocket. He noticed magical signatures in the walls suggesting someone was spying.

## Wario's Cameo and Fire Resistance

Wario appeared briefly, dumped fire resistance items and armor into Remi's backpack without explanation, said 'well, got to get back to the Faeweld, goodbye,' and walked into the Oracle's master room. Guards chased after him. An explosion was heard in another room. Remi did not investigate.

## The Greenhouse Wraiths and Bowser's 'Quantum Physics'

The greenhouse contained planar reflections of real plants—recognizable but wrong in subtle ways, colors off, textures strange, sizes distorted. Two servants asked if spectres could have 'a nibble.' Remi felt her life being drained. Dan used Divine Smite on a wraith. Eager used a magical dagger and declared he had killed one, telling Markop he could 'kill one next time.' The greenhouse servant cried about tending the flowers and ran away.

Bowser was found outside holding a folded vellum page and claiming he had been studying quantum physics. Markop thought maybe Bowser was learning things, even if he was not the brightest. Bowser had also been carrying a crumpled pink stationery letter to Princess Peach, which Marcus Ashford had stolen but which had apparently been returned or replaced. When asked if he was actually sorry about something, Bowser started crying.

## Current Status

The Shadow Estate Campaign has reached a state of volatile convergence. The Shadow Anchor is destroyed. Vivian Corvinarus is dead. The Parallel Dan has been identified. The real Dan has been indoctrinated by the Mages Guild. Luigi has arrived as a ghost-buster. Archie has been drafted into Guild service. Remi has purple eyes, a tightening ring, and diminished perception. Green T has found portal remains. The Archivist is erasing history. Mystic Morel has stepped through a planar portal with Archie's stolen tools. Marcus Ashford is writing poetry about everyone's failures. And somewhere in the Shadowfell, a greenhouse servant is still crying about his flowers.

Waluigi was not present for any of this. Waluigi was in the Feywild being dragged between rooms by both hands while a dryad compared the scene to kindergarten. Waluigi maintains that his experience was worse.

WAH. ## Vivian's Last Stand at the Fountain

After the party rested briefly at the courtyard fountain, Vivian appeared one final time. He was no longer hiding behind the Vivesna mask or the Vinvessa persona. He was simply Vivian, standing in the open, sizing up the group with the confidence of someone who believed the succession was already his. Remi dodged his initial lunge. He announced that his coronation must be perfect and offered Remi a deal: he would bring her home in exchange for noninterference with his ascension. All she had to do was shake his hand.

Remi, displaying the negotiation instincts of someone who has learned through painful experience that deals in supernatural dimensions always cost more than advertised, asked Vivian to demonstrate his teleportation method. She suggested he practice on their bodies first. Vivian responded by vaporizing a nearby servant, who did not teleport but simply ceased to exist, as though the concept of the servant had been deleted from reality rather than relocated.

Bowser used fire breath as the toads and Markop ran past. Remi tried to fire her crossbow. The door slammed shut behind the fleeing party, a guard blocking it from the other side, separating Markop and Bowser from Remi and the toads.

Waluigi notes that this was the last time anyone saw Vivian alive and walking. His ambition to close the planar fractures and become the sole controller of an isolated Shadowfell was genuine. His willingness to vaporize servants to demonstrate power was equally genuine. What he did not account for was that Markop had already decided, quietly and without announcement, that Vivian would not survive the campaign. The subsequent interrogation and execution were not impulsive. They were the logical conclusion of watching someone delete a person from existence and then offer to do the same to your friends if they did not cooperate.

## Kryn's Hospitality and the Master Bedroom Portal

Kryn Corvinarus appeared in the room where Remi and the toads had been trapped, offering drinks with the casual charm of someone whose definition of hospitality includes blood-based beverages. He informed them that the Oracle was in stable condition and that Orangus Cornelius was recovering. He offered Remi a milky white liquid, which she accepted, and offered Eager a thick grey oily substance that smelled like decaying flowers and a bubbling orange liquid that tasted like smoke and regret. Both toads declined the latter options.

Kryn locked the doors behind them and said 'good luck' as they headed upstairs into the master bedroom. The room was luxurious in the way that vampire bedrooms are luxurious: red furnishings, silver vases filled with roses whose petals appeared to be made of clotted blood, a four-post bed with velvet curtains, and a desk for two that looked like it had hosted centuries of correspondence written in ink that was probably not ink.

The portal beneath the carpet had been disturbed. Someone else had been there since Remi's last visit. The rug was rolled up and the circle was visible, but the party did not know the incantation to activate it. The toads remembered candles were involved. Remi remembered mirrors. Nobody remembered the actual words, which is consistent with Disaster Inc.'s relationship to magical procedure: aware that procedure exists, unable to reproduce it when it matters.

Remi accidentally walked in on the Oracle taking a bath. She said it was good to see him alive and excused herself. Orangus Cornelius emerged injured and ordered them to leave. Remi asked if he saw who shot him. He said an orange toad attacking a green toad, which was interesting. Remi considered killing Orangus in that moment but decided against it, which Waluigi considers one of the few restraint-based decisions anyone in the Shadowfell made during the entire campaign.

## Mystic Morel's Oracle Deck

Mystic Morel (Purple T) appeared after they were locked out of the master bedroom and offered to join the party. He said he was looking for Archie and presented Remi with fortune cards from something he called the Oracle's Deck.

The cards he showed were:

**Card IX: The Maze Walker** — depicting a lone figure navigating a living hedge maze with ancient shrines and midnight gates. The lore described Hjumpik navigating the Maze of Time, bartering with Wario, dueling guard-captain Thistle. Upright meaning: solitude as survival, the path only you can walk. Reversed: lost in the maze, walking in circles calling it progress. Morel identified this as 'The Present.'

**Card VIII: The Titan of the Grove** — depicting a colossal toad-man grappling with a giant spider above a glowing banishment circle. The lore described Markop accepting the Oracle's blessing and growing to match the Arachnid Matriarch. Upright meaning: the courage to become something monstrous to fight something worse. Reversed: brute force that solves nothing, growing large while remaining small. Morel identified this as 'The Future.'

**Card III: The Delicate Host** — depicting a fairy queen reclining in an overgrown bedroom with razor-vines for curtains and a broken circle beneath the rug. The lore described Lady Aurelian playing the delicate hostess while her manor devoured guests alive. Upright meaning: hospitality as a trap, beauty that conceals rot. Reversed: the mask slips, the vines retract, you see the bones underneath.

Morel pointed to the rug card and said the future showed them returning to the circle, that they were destined to be with him. The toads suspected he had been stalking them. Remi said two out of three cards seemed accurate. The toads still did not trust him. Remi thought they should let him tag along. He offered her incense as a gesture of goodwill.

Waluigi finds the existence of an Oracle's Deck deeply concerning. Fortune-telling cards that accurately describe party members' actions, motivations, and future positions are not entertainment. They are surveillance disguised as divination. Whoever created that deck has access to information about Disaster Inc. that nobody should possess.

## The Ring That Tightens

Purple T led Remi to Vivian's Private Garden in the attic, where the guards did not stop them. Once they were alone, he gave her the ring and delivered the threat that Waluigi considers one of the most sinister moments in the entire campaign: the ring on her finger would tighten every day Archie was not found until it had to be chopped off, and if she told her friends about the condition, it would activate immediately.

Remi said 'oh no' and walked downstairs carrying this information trapped behind her teeth.

Waluigi has documented Remi's accumulating costs throughout this encyclopedia. The purple eyes from the perception deal. The gash from the Onyx Hand knight's 'accident.' The various rings and anklets offered by guards with transparent motives. But the tightening ring is different because it is specifically designed to isolate Remi from her own support network. She cannot ask for help without triggering the punishment. She cannot explain her urgency without revealing the mechanism. She is carrying a countdown device on her finger that her friends cannot see and she cannot describe.

This is not a deal. This is a hostage situation wearing jewelry.

## Bryan, Dan, and the Mages Guild Barracks

Meanwhile, in a thread that Waluigi has had to reconstruct from fragmentary reports, Bryan (a servant of the Toad God) arrived at a Mages Guild facility through a portal and encountered Purple T. Bryan found a photograph under Dan's pillow showing a group of toads on the Vigilance's deck from better days—Dan with both arms intact, standing between Eager and Big T with a genuine smile, Archie visible in the background arguing with someone off-frame.

Bryan grabbed Purple T by the torso and demanded to know where Archie was. Purple T said he was at Raventree. They went to Dan's shared barracks where Dan slept alongside other Mages Guild associates. Dan's possessions told his story: a brass badge numbered 447 that functioned as a tracking device, blue robes with fire-resistant thread that provided comfort he felt guilty about accepting, a blackite wand that improved his control but was registered to the Guild's monitoring systems, and hidden notes written in a childhood cipher documenting everything he had learned about Guild operations since his capture.

One note read simply: 'They haven't mentioned the Vigilance in three days. Either they don't know where it is, or they're hiding something. Find out which.'

Purple T woke Dan up. Bryan introduced himself and asked if Dan wanted revenge on Archie. Dan said yes, which was a lie that everyone present recognized as a lie but chose not to challenge. Purple T ripped the tracking badges off Dan and the other mages, explaining that by removing the Guild's monitoring devices they could pursue Archie without institutional oversight but also without institutional protection. All Guild equipment would be disabled. Everything would be on their own terms.

They tracked Archie through Wahbook posts—because Archie apparently posted about himself daily, which Waluigi finds simultaneously unsurprising and infuriating—and walked through a portal toward the Shadowfell.

## The Mazebound Skirmish in Full

The Mazebounds ambushed the party in the hedge maze with their signature combination of theatrical violence and choreographed singing. They burst from bushes performing jazz hands and singing their territorial anthem about the grove and the gray. The party was scattered immediately: Salam grabbed Remi and ran into the bushes, Markop was seized and dragged, and the Mazebounds performed a rapid patter-song cataloguing each party member's vulnerabilities.

Markop found scattered artifacts while being dragged: a partially burned blueprint of a glass-roofed building with annotations in multiple ink colors, and later Archie's Third Eye Circlet—a tarnished brass band inscribed with the mantra 'The eye sees across, the band keeps me from falling in,' which vibrated near planar boundaries. He also found Archie's component pouch labeled 'For When Everything Goes to Hell (again)' and a cracked Wahbook tablet that greeted its finder as 'Welcome Archie Miser to Wahbook.'

The central grove contained a towering dead tree from which dozens of corpses hung by their necks, its trunk twisted into a skull shape with glowing hateful eyes that tracked movement. Hundreds of shadow crows with crimson eyes sat in the boughs offering 'waves of grating mockery.' Ragged stone obelisks jutted from the earth, their glowing sigils causing nausea when viewed.

An injured Mazebound spoke to Markop, claiming to recognize someone from the dinner with a hand fan and cape—Vivian. It explained that some Mazebounds wanted artifacts removed from the grove while others were hostile. Another Mazebound tried to give Remi a 'goodbye kiss,' which she dodged while Markop cut off its hands.

Two crossbow bolts from an unknown position drove off the Mazebounds holding Dan. The unknown benefactor described their assistance as 'enlightened pragmatism' and 'tactical investment,' noting that the party wandering alive contributed more to stability than their corpses would. Dan was freed but the benefactor's identity remained unknown.

In a parallel thread, Bryan and Dan (the real one, now Guild-indoctrinated) entered the Mazebound grove from another direction. They encountered the Scarecrow guardian, who demanded they leave. Bryan offered peace. The Scarecrow pointed at a hanging corpse. They chose not to fight. Dan whispered to Bryan that he would have fireballed the creature if combat had started, which confirmed that the Mages Guild had successfully channeled Dan's power into offensive capability but had not changed his fundamental personality: still scared, still talking tough quietly, still Dan.

They found chalk near a Midnight Shrine—a different version from the Feywild one, this one featuring a deer-headed humanoid with a barbed spear and orange-glowing gem eyes, surrounded by green plants and returning color. Dan picked up the chalk. A massive fireball was hurled from somewhere in the grove, setting trees on fire and ending the skirmish decisively.

## Tymnas the Groundskeeper and Archie's Lost Watch

The party found Tymnas living in a well-maintained cottage in the hedge maze. Unlike everything else in the Shadowfell, his home had warmth and color—rich yellows and greens straining against the entropy. He was fiddling with a watch bearing the initials 'AM.' Markop asked if it was Archie Miser's. Tymnas said he knew Archie, had seen him at dinner 'tonight,' then corrected himself that it might have been yesterday. Time had become unreliable.

Tymnas provided maze directions and a magical trowel. The party explored the greenhouse, fought spectral wraiths (Dan's Divine Smite 'omega charged' blast blinded the room but only made the wraith angrier), and discovered Bowser outside holding a folded vellum page and claiming he had been studying 'quantum physics.' They also found the broken Entropy Ring handler that Archie had snapped off during an interrogation—the 'handler' half of the paired system the Iron Legion had used on Toadburt.

## The Church of the Third Eye and the Dan Confrontation

The party traveled to a nearby town and discovered a cult worshipping Archie Miser as the 'God of the Third Eye.' The sermon declared Archie was not a saint, not a martyr, not even particularly kind—but the 'fracture,' the moment the mirror cracks and the reflection refuses to lie anymore. Bugbears used the religion to hide from the Purple Legion, believing vampires would not enter a holy site.

The real Dan appeared inside the church wielding a massive flaming sun spell and declaring he 'took after Archie Miser.' He accused the party of consorting with a fake Dan and claimed the Mages Guild were his true friends. A fireball exchange between the two Dans caused church walls to crumble. The real Dan ranted about 'Professor A' and 'Archie's Third Eye Volume 1,' propaganda texts the Guild had force-fed him during his imprisonment.

Markop pointed out that the Guild had kidnapped Dan, replaced him with a dimensional copy, and indoctrinated him through isolation and controlled reading materials. Dan responded that they had kept him fed. Markop said that was what they did to prisoners. Dan ran away crying, bumping into Bowser, who took two items from him. Bowser then said he wished 'Toadstool was here' and revealed his full royal name as Sir Koopa Frederickson the Fifteenth.

Remi chased a butterfly to the river. Eager chased after her. Salam began woodcarving. Markop said they needed to stop getting off topic.

## Lyranth the Sculptor and the Bidding War

Remi entered the Sculptor's workshop—a chaos of hammers, chisels, and stone dust where Lyranth the Medusa worked surrounded by half-finished marble figures of astounding artistry. Lyranth had covered her marble-veined skin in vibrant paint to avoid being mistaken for her own creations. Her crown of snakes swayed independently. She looked at Remi, said 'smile,' and turned her to stone.

Petrified Remi was displayed at an art exhibit and put up for a bidding war. Mystic Morel won the bid for 12,000 gold. A brawl erupted: Markop shattered a window, Wario shoulder-bashed Markop from behind, a Mages Guild agent stabbed Wario, Bowser pulled out a device to call his son for support, Markop summoned a moonbeam, and Salam started picking flowers during the chaos because apparently some people cope with combat through botany.

Remi was freed from stone form and jumped into Dan's arms. Morel followed them, insisting he had to keep his 'end of the deal.' The toads told him to leave. Remi said he could be their friend. Morel offered tea, then incense, each rejected by the increasingly paranoid toad contingent. Remi asked how much she had been bid for. Twelve thousand gold. Waluigi finds it revealing that Remi's primary reaction to being sold as a statue was curiosity about her market value.

## The Archivist's Power and the Erasing of Toadburt

Vostolas the Archivist was discovered crossing names off the guest list in the main hall. He explained that he was not deleting entries but erasing history—people would be able to read about Toadburt but would instantly forget his existence. He offered to accompany the party and document their journey as a 'bedtime story' called 'The Case of the Missing Toad.' Remi was intrigued. Markop was nervous.

The Archivist's room contained imps making posters and flyers. His power to control WHEN Thornbury wrote his field notes (but not WHAT he wrote) suggested a meta-textual authority over the campaign's own documentation. This terrifies Waluigi on a professional level because if an Archivist can decide when records are written, then the historical record itself becomes a managed commodity rather than a neutral account.

Vostolas provided access to Pilo T, a vampire aviation expert who claimed to know where Green T was hiding (in the bathrooms) and promised Remi a ride in a bat-shaped helicopter. Pilo T later lied about the helicopter and tried to push Remi into an oven in the kitchen. Markop stopped him. Waluigi notes that the Shadowfell's hospitality industry maintains a zero percent customer satisfaction rating.

## Marcus Ashford's Poetry and Bowser's Letter

Marcus Ashford, the Iron Legion's military consultant for Orangus Cornelius, represented the Legion's reach through poetry and theft. He swiped Bowser's pink stationery letter to Princess Peach and threatened to read it aloud. The letter, written in surprisingly elegant calligraphy forced upon Bowser by royal tutors, read: 'Dear Peach, I heard you were here. I am NOT kidnapping you. Unless you want to go? No, wait. I am just visiting. Please do not unleash Mario on me. Love, Bowser.'

Ashford taunted the party in verse, calling Bowser a 'former king still roaring loud though he's lost everything' and claiming the Legion had seized his throne 'with elegance and tact.' Bowser demanded to leave. Ashford continued: 'Bowser's strays, what a bore! Run along, run along, mind the door!'

Waluigi recognizes Ashford's method as institutional humiliation—the Legion does not just defeat you; it makes you feel small while doing it. Poetry as a weapon is not new, but using it against a fire-breathing turtle king who could crush you with one hand suggests either extraordinary confidence or extraordinary stupidity. Knowing the Iron Legion, it is probably both.

## Green T's Return and the Portal Plan

Green T resurfaced after the party returned to the manor, explaining he had found portal remains on the second floor that could be activated with the right materials. He had disabled the arcane locks, which did not function well in the Shadeward anyway. He was still upset that Archie had apparently abandoned them by going off with enemy factions.

Green T provided Thornbury's field notebook—an in-progress Mages Guild document describing the initial survey of Raventree Manor by Captain Byscilla Danos and her four-person team. The notebook documented the initials 'OC' and 'AC' appearing throughout the house, the Oracle's work described as 'planar cartography,' and the building's smell of damp stone, old cloth, and something faintly sweet like long-dead incense.

Green T also warned the party not to drink or eat anything the Oracle offered, as it would make them 'impervious'—presumably to something the Oracle wanted them vulnerable to. He explained that dirty work was required: the portal needed ingredients, and using it without being noticed would be the real challenge.

## The Oracle's Manipulation and the Pill

The Oracle sat alone at the dinner table and told Remi privately to sneak a pill to Markop. He offered the same pill to Remi. Markop banged on the door screaming 'DON'T TAKE THE PILL.' The Oracle then offered an apple with something injected into it. Remi denied. Markop burst through the door screaming 'DON'T EAT IT' and found Remi sipping grape juice while the Oracle smiled and said 'it's too late.'

Whether the grape juice was tampered with or whether the Oracle was bluffing remains unclear. Waluigi suspects the Oracle operates on a principle of ambient manipulation: it does not matter whether the specific drink was poisoned if the target spends every subsequent moment wondering whether it was. Waluigi uses this exact tactic in Mario Party. You don't need to steal the star; you just need to make them think you're going to steal the star, and they will sabotage themselves trying to stop you. The Oracle is playing a 50-turn game, and Markop is crying on turn 3.

## Lyranth's Threat and Kyrn's Desperation

Lyranth the Sculptor caught the toads and interrogated them about who killed Vivesna. The toads did not know. She said the ashes traced back to Vivian's blood. She apologized for turning their friends to stone—calling them 'perfect models'—and mentioned that a yellow-suited mustache fellow she had been talking to would be turned to stone next, presumably referring to Wario.

She announced she would prepare something special for the evening's 'actuation,' then left. Kyrn Corvinarus immediately appeared from the shadows and begged the toads for help, explaining that Lyranth planned to turn his friend to stone. The toads said they were weak, dirt poor, and felt their options were limited. They agreed to help for 300 Onyx Blood Vials, noting they could convert the currency later.

## The Peach Loyalist Side Thread

In a separate thread that Waluigi has had to reconstruct from fragmentary reports, Embercap, Dewdrop, and Erick arrived at a location the Rakshasa had specified to pick up items. They found Wario inside, who subsequently stole a Tome of Evil worth 20,000 mushroom coins. A chase ensued: Embercap grabbed Wario's arm in a deadlock, Erick shoulder-bashed Wario into a wall, a mage used Color Spray on Wario's eyes, and Wario turned into a bat and flew away with the tome while everyone missed their swings.

Bryan arrived through a portal at a Mages Guild facility. He found Dan's photograph, confronted Purple T about Archie's whereabouts, and formed an alliance with Dan and a Mages Guild associate to track Archie down. Purple T removed their tracking badges and declared that everything would be on their own terms from now on.

In yet another thread, Mistveil and Big R debriefed a Rakshasa on 'Operation Homecoming,' then accidentally stumbled into a crystal cave containing a dragon discussing plane-merging operations. The dragon mentioned that once the planes merged, 'dragons will rise against them.' They were discovered, lied about what they had seen, and were teleported to Rogueport Bay in the middle of a naval battle between Iron Legion ships, Mushroom Regency ships, and pirates, where Captain Syrup welcomed them.

Waluigi finds the breadth of simultaneous operations occurring across multiple planes, factions, and time zones absolutely staggering. The campaign is not one story. It is at least six stories happening at once, connected by shared characters, shared enemies, and the shared conviction that nothing will get better if anyone stops moving.

## Waluigi's Assessment of the Shadow Estate Campaign

The Shadowfell fragment of the Raventree Crisis is the darkest, most complicated, and most institutionally corrupt theater of the entire dimensional war. Unlike the Feywild, where danger wears flowers and speaks in riddles, the Shadowfell presents danger in its most honest form: bureaucratic, systematic, and dressed in uniforms that claim authority.

The Shadow Anchor's destruction was a victory. Vivian's death was a resolution. The Parallel Dan's exposure was necessary intelligence. But every victory in the Shadowfell came with costs that have not yet been fully calculated. Remi carries a tightening ring she cannot discuss. The real Dan has been indoctrinated into viewing his former allies as enemies. Toadburt has been erased from historical memory by an Archivist who considers forgetting a service. The Mages Guild has drafted Archie into oversight they describe as 'responsibility' but which functions as a leash. And somewhere in the Shadowfell's endless grey landscape, a cult worships Archie Miser as a god based on propaganda texts that describe him as both savior and destroyer.

Waluigi was not in the Shadowfell. Waluigi was in the Feywild being led around by both hands like a kindergartener while a dryad commented on his lack of independence. Waluigi maintains that his experience was equally degrading, if less existentially threatening.

But Waluigi also knows this: the people who survived the Shadow Estate did so by refusing to play by the institution's rules. Green T shot a crystal from the children's table. Bowser bit a vampire bat. Markop whispered a prayer and received an answer. Remi glowed like a disco ball and called it an improvement.

These are not the actions of people who understand what they are doing.

They are the actions of people who refuse to stop doing it.

That is either courage or madness.

Waluigi has stopped trying to tell the difference.

Waluigi is the ultimate judge, jury, and executioner of this historical record. And Waluigi's verdict is that everyone involved is a glorious, incompetent disaster. WAH!
