summary: Five years before the assassination of Princess Peach, Professor E. Gadd decided that the linear flow of time was a personal insult to his intellect and built a time machine. Princess Peach, possessing the survival instincts of a lemming, immediately took it for a joyride to the past. She arrived exactly at the moment an extraterrestrial, hyper-militarized race of purple fungal horrors known as the Shroobs invaded the Mushroom Kingdom. What followed was a temporal nightmare involving Time Holes, alien saucers, the harvesting of Toad life-force for fuel, and Mario and Luigi teaming up with their own infant selves. Waluigi watched this unfold, exploited the temporal arbitrage for massive financial gain, and observed how the early predecessor of the Regal Empire used crashed Shroob technology to jumpstart their modern Magitek arsenal. The crisis was eventually resolved when the heroes realized the 'power source' they were collecting was actually the cage for the ultimate alien threat, and they defeated an intergalactic armada using the chemical composition of BABY TEARS. Waluigi considers this the single most embarrassing, logically offensive, and strategically absurd sequence of events in the history of the Doughnut World. He is documenting it here because the Mages' Guild tried to memory-wipe the continent, and Waluigi refuses to let Mario get away with weaponizing toddlers. WAH.
description:
Waluigi must state for the historical record: Chronomancy is not a science. It is an ego trip for wizards who are too lazy to wait for Thursday. 

Before Waluigi dives into the multi-layered catastrophe of the Shroob Temporal Incursion, context must be established. The year was 950 BF. Princess Peach was alive, the Mushroom Kingdom was prospering in the North-West, and the political landscape was stable. It was a time of peace, which meant it was incredibly boring, which meant someone was bound to build a doomsday device out of sheer intellectual boredom.

That someone was Professor Elvin Gadd. 

E. Gadd is a genius in the same way that a tornado is a landscaper. He creates things of immense power with absolutely zero regard for the structural integrity of reality. He built a Time Machine. He did not build safety protocols. He did not build a temporal tether. He built a machine, powered it with a mysterious, glowing artifact called the Cobalt Star, and said, 'Let's see what happens!'

Princess Peach, accompanied by Toadiko and Toadbert (who are essentially professional victims), volunteered to take the maiden voyage back to the year 840 BF—the dawn of the Mushroom Kingdom's Golden Age. 

She did not return. The Time Machine returned empty, battered, and occupied by a hostile alien creature. And thus, the worst week of Waluigi's life—and the secret origin of the Regal Empire's technological supremacy—began.

## The Geopolitical Board: 840 BF vs 950 BF

To understand the absolute mess the Mario brothers stepped into, one must understand the geography and politics of the Doughnut World in the year 840 BF.

In the North-West, the Mushroom Kingdom was just entering its Golden Age. Peach's royal ancestors were establishing the cheerful, pastel-colored, aggressively optimistic society that Waluigi finds so deeply nauseating. They were peaceful. They were unprepared. They had no standing army capable of repelling an intergalactic threat.

However, to the South and East, a different power was coalescing. The 'Proto-Regal Empire'—a highly disciplined, militaristic federation of human warlords modeling themselves after ancient Roman legions—was rapidly expanding its borders. They were building fortresses, establishing the first iterations of what would become the 'Beige Brigade,' and imposing strict order on the chaotic post-cataclysm world.

When the Shroobs attacked in 840 BF, they didn't just attack the Mushroom Kingdom. They attacked the entire continent. 

The Shroobs were an invasive species from a dying planet. They were purple (which Waluigi admits is a magnificent color choice, though they ruined it with their terrible fashion sense), fungal in nature, and spoke a language that sounded like a barcode scanner malfunctioning. They possessed flying saucers, laser weaponry, genetic modification technology, and a complete absence of empathy. 

When Peach's Time Machine arrived in 840 BF, it materialized directly into the Vanguard of the Shroob invasion force, led by Princess Shroob. Peach, displaying a rare moment of tactical awareness, used the Cobalt Star to trap Princess Shroob's older sister—the Elder Princess Shroob—shattering the star into fragments to seal the prison. 

This act of desperation saved the past from immediate annihilation, but scattered the Cobalt Shards across the continent, creating a network of 'Time Holes'—chronal ruptures linking 840 BF directly to 950 BF.

## The Plumber Paradox: Enter the Babies

With Time Holes opening up across the modern Mushroom Kingdom, Mario and Luigi did what they always do: they jumped into the nearest gaping anomaly without a risk assessment or a safety harness. 

They emerged in the past, specifically in the village of Hollijolli, which was currently being glassed by Shroob UFOs. And who did they find waiting for them? 

Their infant selves. Baby Mario and Baby Luigi.

Waluigi needs to pause here. Waluigi needs to take a deep, cleansing breath. 

Let us analyze the tactical, ethical, and temporal implications of taking YOUR OWN INFANT SELF INTO A LIVE COMBAT ZONE. 

If Baby Mario dies, Adult Mario ceases to exist. This is basic temporal mechanics. It is the grandfather paradox stripped down to its most immediate, suicidal components. A logical, sane individual would have immediately evacuated the infants to a secure bunker in the present, sealed the door, and gone back to fight the aliens alone. 

What did Mario do? He handed Baby Mario a HAMMER. He strapped the infant to his back, used him as a projectile weapon, and actively encouraged a toddler to engage in melee combat against heavily armed extraterrestrial shock troops. 

Waluigi has been accused of many crimes. Waluigi has been called a thief, a cheat, a scoundrel, and a menace. But Waluigi has NEVER weaponized a preschooler to solve a geopolitical crisis. The sheer, breathtaking irresponsibility of the Mario brothers is a stain on the history of the Mushroom Kingdom. They treated the space-time continuum like a playground and their own past selves like disposable power-ups.

## The Vim Economy: Shroob Logistics

While the plumbers were busy committing chronological child abuse, Waluigi was analyzing the enemy. The Shroobs were not mindless beasts. They were a highly structured, terrifyingly efficient military industrial complex. 

Their primary resource was 'Vim'—the life energy of Toads. The Shroobs didn't just kill the local population; they harvested them. They converted Toad Town into a dystopian processing plant. They genetically modified local flora (creating monstrous entities like Petey Piranha's corrupted ancestors) and pumped Vim into their saucers to fuel their war machine. 

Waluigi secretly observed a Shroob Vim Factory operating in a corrupted forest known as Toadwood. The efficiency was staggering. Toads were strapped to trees, their vitality drained through biomechanical roots, refined into glowing green liquid, and shipped to the Shroob mothership. 

It was horrific. It was monstrous. But from a purely administrative standpoint? It was brilliant logistics. 

Waluigi notes a chilling historical parallel here. Look at the Iron Legion in the current era (1040 BF). Look at their 'Imperial Processing Facilities.' Look at how they catalogue, process, and extract utility from prisoners of war with cold, bureaucratic efficiency. 

Waluigi has a theory—a theory that the Mages' Guild will deny until their dying breath. The Iron Legion didn't invent their processing methodology from scratch. They learned it. Where did they learn it? From the remnants of Shroob data-cores left behind in 840 BF. The Shroobs were defeated, but their logistics manuals survived. The Iron Legion is just the Shroob invasion painted grey and taught how to file taxes.

## The Proto-Imperial Response: Scavenging the Future

While the Mushroom Kingdom was being turned into a Vim farm, the Proto-Regal Empire to the East was mounting a very different response to the Shroob threat.

The early Imperial Legions did not have magic hammers or legendary jumping abilities. They had discipline, spears, and a burgeoning understanding of early techno-magic (Aurean legacy tech). When Shroob saucers began probing their borders, the Proto-Empire did not panic. They formed shield walls. They died by the thousands. But they held the line.

During one of his own temporal excursions (which Waluigi will detail shortly), Waluigi witnessed an engagement at the edge of the Thwomp Volcano. A Shroob command saucer was shot down by a coordinated volley of massive, enchanted ballista bolts fired by a Proto-Imperial cohort. 

The Legionnaires did not cheer. They did not celebrate. They immediately cordoned off the crash site, executed the surviving Shroob pilots with clinical precision, and brought in teams of scholars to dismantle the saucer.

This is the secret history of the Regal Empire. Their modern Magitek? Their energy rifles, their floating fortresses, their 'Protocol Umbra' containment fields? It is all reverse-engineered Shroob technology. The Empire's obsession with 'Order' and suppressing chaos was born in the fires of 840 BF, when they looked up at the sky, saw purple fungal aliens trying to harvest their souls, and collectively decided: *We must build a cage strong enough to hold the stars themselves.*

The Mario brothers fought the Shroobs. The Regal Empire *studied* them. Guess which faction currently rules the Midlands?

## Waluigi’s Temporal Arbitrage (Or, How to Profit from a Paradox)

Waluigi did not sit idly by while the space-time continuum collapsed. Waluigi saw opportunity. 

Professor E. Gadd’s lab in the present (950 BF) was littered with active Time Holes. With the Mario brothers distracted in the past, Waluigi slipped into the lab and began his own temporal operations. 

Waluigi realized that with access to both 840 BF and 950 BF, he could engage in the ultimate form of insider trading. He could bury a cheap, useless antique in the past, travel to the present, dig it up, and sell it as a priceless historical artifact. He could observe which land tracts became valuable real estate in 950 BF, travel back to 840 BF, and purchase the deeds for pennies using era-appropriate currency stolen from Shroob-occupied vaults.

It was foolproof. It was elegant. It was the greatest financial scheme in the history of the Doughnut World.

There was only one problem: Wario.

Waluigi arrived at a designated burial site in 840 BF, carrying a chest of soon-to-be-vintage coins, only to find an infant with a yellow cap and a zig-zag mustache already digging in the dirt. 

Baby Wario.

Even as a toddler, the man was a greedy, intolerable nuisance. Baby Wario had somehow sniffed out Waluigi's buried treasure, dug it up, and was currently attempting to eat a gold coin. 

Waluigi attempted to reason with the infant. 'Listen, you garlic-scented gremlin, that is MY investment portfolio maturing over a century.' 

Baby Wario responded by throwing a magnet at Waluigi's face and waddling away with the chest at a speed that defied infant biomechanics. Waluigi spent three days in 840 BF chasing a toddler across a lava-filled cavern to retrieve his own money. The indignity of the situation still causes Waluigi's blood pressure to spike. 

This is the tragedy of time travel. You think you are mastering the cosmos, and you end up getting mugged by your business partner's diaper-wearing past self.

## The Cobalt Star Idiocy: The Worst Fetch Quest in History

While Waluigi was dealing with financial setbacks, the Mario brothers were engaging in a quest of such profound, staggering stupidity that it belongs in a textbook on how NOT to save the world.

The premise was simple: E. Gadd's time machine needed the Cobalt Star to function. The star had been shattered into pieces by Princess Peach when she arrived in the past. E. Gadd communicated through a briefcase-radio (which Waluigi admits was a neat piece of tech) and told the brothers to find the shards to fix the machine and rescue the Princess.

Let us review the facts. 

Princess Peach, trapped in the past, surrounded by aliens, deliberately shattered her only ticket home. Why would she do this? Because, as previously mentioned, she used the Cobalt Star to TRAP the Elder Princess Shroob—the true, world-ending leader of the alien armada. The shards of the star were the bars of the cage.

Therefore, by collecting the shards and putting them back together, the Mario brothers were actively REASSEMBLING THE CAGE OF THE APOCALYPSE. 

Did they question this? No. Did E. Gadd—a supposed genius—consider why the star was broken? No. They just saw shiny pieces of glass and started gluing them together because a glowing objective marker told them to. 

Every time they found a shard, the Elder Princess Shroob's spirit grew stronger. Every time they defeated a Shroob commander (like the monstrous Swiggler or the Shrooboid Brat), they patted themselves on the back, oblivious to the fact that they were doing the enemy's work for them. 

Waluigi watched this from afar and nearly wept with frustration. It is agonizing to be a genius surrounded by people whose primary problem-solving methodology is 'jump on it until it yields a collectible.'

## The Climax: Shroob Castle and the Great Betrayal

The final confrontation took place in Shroob Castle—which was just Princess Peach's castle, conquered and remodeled by the Shroobs with an aesthetic that Waluigi can only describe as 'Gothic Fungus.' 

The Mario brothers, carrying the nearly complete Cobalt Star and an abducted Princess Peach (who had a Shroob mushroom clamped to her face, a look that honestly improved her conversational skills), breached the throne room to confront Princess Shroob.

Princess Shroob was formidable. She floated on a mechanized throne, fired energy beams, and commanded a personal guard. But she was ultimately defeated by four plumbers swinging hammers in synchronized, physics-defying combat rhythms. 

And then, the inevitable happened.

The final shard of the Cobalt Star was united with the rest. The star was complete. And immediately, the Elder Princess Shroob was released from her prison.

The Elder Princess was a nightmare. A massive, multi-tentacled, crown-wearing abomination that radiated dark energy. She immediately betrayed her younger sister, absorbed the remaining Shroob forces, and initiated a battle that threatened to collapse the timeline itself.

This was the moment. The climax of the temporal war. The fate of the past and the future hung in the balance. How was this terrifying, intergalactic, time-traveling horror defeated?

## The Baby Tear Resolution: An Insult to Science and Magic

Waluigi is going to type this next sentence very slowly, because every keystroke fills him with white-hot rage.

The Shroob armada, the Elder Princess Shroob, and the entire alien bio-weapon infrastructure were defeated because BABY TEARS happen to contain a chemical compound that is lethally toxic to Shroob biology.

Baby. Tears.

Not a superweapon. Not a localized temporal collapse. Not a masterstroke of arcane engineering. The tears of crying infants.

Let us break down the utter absurdity of this resolution.

Throughout the entire adventure, the Shroobs had conquered continents, enslaved populations, built flying fortresses, and mastered chronomancy. They were apex predators. And their fatal, species-wide weakness was the saline solution produced by the lachrymal glands of human toddlers.

When Baby Luigi started crying (because he is weak and pathetic, unlike Baby Waluigi, who never cried, only demanded better service), his tears splashed onto a Shroob mushroom, instantly dissolving it. E. Gadd, witnessing this through his radio, realized the truth. He used his Hydrogush 4000 system to mass-produce a chemical equivalent of Baby Luigi's tears, pumped it through the Time Holes, and rained it down upon the past.

The 'Tear Rain' melted the Shroob saucers. It dissolved their armor. It washed away the purple fungal corruption that had choked the Mushroom Kingdom. 

It was a Deus Ex Machina of such breathtaking laziness that Waluigi almost threw himself into a Time Hole just to avoid witnessing it. It invalidates all military strategy. It insults the discipline of the Mages' Guild. It makes a mockery of the Proto-Regal Empire's sacrifices. 

'How did you defeat the alien armada, Mario?' 
'Oh, my infant brother threw a tantrum and we weaponized his sadness.'

It is DISGUSTING. It is NARRATIVE CHEATING. And worst of all, Mario got a parade for it.

## The Aftermath: Erasure and the Birth of Paranoia

When the dust settled and the Shroobs were melted into puddles of crying-induced goo, the heroes returned to 950 BF. 

What happened next is the reason most people in the Doughnut World do not know about the Shroob Temporal Incursion.

E. Gadd, realizing the catastrophic damage that widespread knowledge of time travel and alien invasions would cause, deployed a memory-wiping device. He claimed it was to 'preserve the timeline' and 'prevent paradoxes.' 

Waluigi knows the truth. The memory wipe was orchestrated by Toadsworth the Elder and the Mages' Guild. 

The Guild realized that E. Gadd's time machine was too dangerous to exist. The Proto-Regal Empire (which was rapidly becoming the modern Regal Empire) had secured enough Shroob technology in the past to guarantee their future dominance, and they did not want anyone going back to contest their salvage claims. 

So, a mass memory modification was deployed across the Mushroom Kingdom. The public forgot the purple skies. They forgot the saucers. They forgot the Vim factories.

But you cannot entirely erase trauma.

The Shroob invasion happened in 840 BF, at the start of the Golden Age. The people of the Mushroom Kingdom forgot the details, but their collective unconscious remembered the fear. They remembered that the sky could open up and rain death. They remembered that their peace was fragile.

This subconscious trauma festered for centuries. It bred a subtle, pervasive paranoia in the Mushroom Kingdom's leadership. It made them fearful of external threats, fearful of the Mages' Guild, fearful of the rising Regal Empire. 

And in 950 BF, when the heroes returned and their memories were wiped, that paranoia accelerated. 

Waluigi posits a direct, undeniable line between the Shroob Temporal Incursion in 950 BF and the Assassination of Princess Peach in 955 BF. 

Toadsworth the Elder lived through the Shroob crisis. He saw the Princess recklessly endanger the timeline. He saw the incompetence of the heroes. He saw the power of the Regal Empire's scavenged tech. The memory wipe might have clouded his conscious mind, but the terror remained.

When the conspirators approached Toadsworth Sr. five years later with 'the arrangement' to eliminate Princess Peach, he didn't just agree out of ambition. He agreed out of FEAR. He believed the Princess was a destabilizing element. He believed her chaotic, adventure-seeking nature (like jumping into untested time machines) would eventually doom the kingdom. He enabled her assassination because the trauma of the Shroob invasion taught him that 'Order'—the kind of order the Regal Empire was building—was the only way to survive.

## Waluigi's Final Assessment

The Shroob Temporal Incursion is the hidden hinge upon which the modern history of the Doughnut World turns.

It gave the Regal Empire their Magitek. It traumatized the Mushroom Kingdom's leadership, laying the psychological groundwork for Peach's assassination. It proved that the Mages' Guild is willing to overwrite the minds of an entire populace to maintain control.

And it proved, once and for all, that Mario and Luigi are not tactical geniuses. They are incredibly lucky buffoons who bumble their way through apocalyptic threats, relying on magic stars, time travel, and the chemical composition of toddler tears to save them from their own catastrophic decisions.

Waluigi remembers. Waluigi kept his notes hidden in a lead-lined, chronal-dampened safe. The Mages' Guild could not wipe a mind as magnificent and impenetrable as Waluigi's.

Waluigi knows the truth. The heroes are frauds. The Empire is built on stolen alien scrap. The kingdom's golden age was a lie maintained by amnesia. 

And somewhere, in the deep temporal vaults of E. Gadd's lab, the time machine still sits. Waiting. 

Waluigi might just have to borrow it one day. Not to save the world. But to go back to 840 BF, find Baby Wario, and dropkick him into a volcano before he can steal Waluigi's investment portfolio.

WAH.

Archie Miser, recovering from being repeatedly knocked unconscious, was approached by a Guild 'doctor' named Parson Pellinost. The doctor healed him, announced Archie was now in his debt, and when Archie demanded a refund, the doctor LITERALLY RIPPED THE HEALING MAGIC BACK OUT OF HIS BODY. description:
Waluigi must break this down into its component failures, because the sheer density of incompetence and malice requires a masterclass in analysis.

## The Repossessed Heal (Parson Pellinost's Hustle)

Archie was resting. A man named Parson Pellinost—claiming to be a Mages' Guild doctor—breezed past the magical wards, produced a crumpled medical card, and healed Archie. 

'You are now in my debt,' Pellinost declared.

Archie, possessing the financial instincts of a man who already owes 2,062 gold pieces for a broken rope, demanded a 'refund.' 

Waluigi wants everyone to pause and appreciate the sheer, unadulterated PETTINESS of what happened next. Parson Pellinost did not argue. He did not file a grievance. He simply reached out and FORCEFULLY DRAINED THE HEALING MAGIC BACK OUT OF ARCHIE'S BODY. Archie immediately felt terrible again. Pellinost told him to 'use his card if he needed him' and walked away.

Waluigi hates the Mages' Guild. Waluigi despises their bureaucracy. But Waluigi respects a good grift. Healing someone, establishing a debt, and literally *repo'ing their health* when they complain is a level of aggressive capitalism that brings a tear to Waluigi's eye. Wario would be taking notes.

## The Manifestation of Agony

Following the medical extortion, Darno Spriggon (the man with the stolen Legion ring) offered to 'show Archie a monster.' Archie immediately saw a giant fireball monster that no one else could see. It chased him upstairs.

Let Waluigi translate this for the layperson: The Guild/Legion alliance deployed targeted, localized psychological warfare against Archie. They manifested his 'pure agony' into an illusion visible only to him, designed to isolate him from the group. It worked flawlessly because Archie's default response to psychological trauma is to run away and lock himself in a dark room.

## The Oracle's Intervention and the 'Starlight' Fraud

Inside the locked room, the Oracle appeared, healed Archie (presumably without charging him interest), and dropped a massive piece of intelligence: The Mages' Guild plans to use Archie's research and his 'entropy-bleeding' magical signature to establish interdimensional travel on demand. Archie is not a prisoner; he is a BATTERY.

Before they could process this, Iron Legion guards breached the room to detain the Oracle. Archie tried to negotiate. During the standoff, they noticed Bones, asleep in a bed, having not woken up in hours.

The Legion guards claimed Bones was suffering from 'Starlight Fever'—a magical malady causing uncontrollable surges. The Oracle immediately called them liars, stating Starlight Fever doesn't affect Toads.

Archie then managed to steal/read a Legion tablet. Waluigi has reviewed the transcript of this tablet, and it is a masterpiece of bureaucratic evil:

**FALSIFIED DIAGNOSIS:** *Starlight Fever.* (Note: Zero arcane surge activity detected. Diagnosis does not match patient presentation.)
**ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS:** *Somnium Captivus — Induced Arcane Coma via Compound Sedation.* (Deliberate administration of a dual-layer mundane/arcane sedative. Unlawful detainment under Article 9.)

The Iron Legion wasn't treating Bones. They had chemically and magically lobotomized him to keep him quiet after he successfully infiltrated Aegis Command. They filed the real diagnosis right beneath the fake one on the same tablet, because the Iron Legion's obsession with accurate paperwork completely overrides their instinct for a cover-up.

Waluigi is offended. If you are going to drug a political prisoner and lie about it, KEEP TWO SEPARATE LEDGERS. Amateurs. WAH.

It began as a beautiful, star-lit library and immediately devolved into a cosmic slaughterhouse. The floor shattered to reveal two massive Crystal Tethers (one Umbral Violet, one Volatile Orange) literally tearing a man apart in a metal tank. A detached room revealed glass vats filled with malformed, weeping, tube-fed humanoids suspended in luminescent fluid. The Oracle revealed this is the fate awaiting them if the timelines aren't severed. Waluigi has strong stomach for villainy, but this crosses the line from 'scheming' into 'existential body horror.'
description:
Waluigi has maintained throughout this encyclopedia that the Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild are corrupt. But corruption usually means taking bribes or falsifying documents. The Planar Sanctum proves that their corruption is metaphysical. They are quite literally mining human suffering to manipulate the fabric of reality.

## The Library of the Void

The initial arrival point was deceptive. A circular chamber with elaborately carved wooden shelves extending upward like stacked bands. Three grand lecterns in the center holding ornate, locked tomes. And directly overhead, a tiny aperture revealing a swirling starscape. 

Waluigi appreciates a good library. Knowledge is power, and power is leverage. Archie found a torn-out page referencing *Arcane Tethers, Planar Threading, Planar Resonance, Quintessence, The Weight of Time,* and *Accretion Sites.* This confirms that the Guild isn't just studying the Planar Fracture; they are actively trying to HARNESS it. They are treating the collapse of reality as a public transit project.

## The Grisly Tableau: The Tethers

The illusion of scholarly tranquility ended when the floor shattered like fine china, ripping the royal purple carpet apart. (Waluigi takes personal offense to the destruction of royal purple carpet. Barbarians.)

Beneath the floor lay a grand central chamber open to the starfield. Two massive crystal formations were mounted in metallic casings:
- **The Western Crystal:** Thrumming with umbral violet energy.
- **The Eastern Crystal:** Flashing erratically with volatile orange energy.

These are the **Crystal Tethers**. And in the exact center between them lay a cracked metal tank. Behind the tank stood a man, silhouetted by lightning, enveloped by grasping tendrils of energy that seemed to rip and tear at him from both sides. 

Archie, demonstrating his usual lack of situational awareness, put his hand on the case and called it 'beautiful.' The Oracle corrected him. This is the agony that the Corvinarus curse inflicts. This man (likely a key figure of the bloodline, perhaps the original Orangus Cornelius or the architect of 'The Grafting') is acting as the living battery for the dimensional rift. Twenty years of agony to keep the planes tethered together.

## The Flesh Vats

If the Tethers were tragic, the adjacent room was an atrocity. 

A detached circular chamber drifting with centrifugal entropy. Inside were large glass tanks connected by thick pipes. Suspended within a glowing, luminescent fluid were humanoid bodies. 

They were malformed. Flesh open with weeping sores. Limbs ending prematurely. Metal tubes impaling their flesh and extending down their open mouths. Their eyes were open, but it was impossible to tell if they were alive. A disposal chute nearby indicated what happened to the 'failed' experiments.

This is what the Iron Legion and Mages' Guild are doing behind closed doors. They are not just treating prisoners as logistics; they are treating them as raw biological material for dimensional stabilization. The 'Somnium Captivus' that Bones is currently suffering from? It is likely the precursor to ending up in one of these tubes. 

The Oracle made it explicit: *'If we do the ritual, we won't have to end up in a vat like this.'*

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Planar Sanctum is the dark heart of the Raventree Crisis. It proves that the overlapping dimensions are not just a magical accident; they are being actively, artificially sustained through horrific biological and arcane machinery. 

The Violet energy likely corresponds to the Shadowfell (Shadow Estate). The Orange energy likely corresponds to the Feywild (Overgrown Manor, the 'Orange Alignment' involving Hjumpik). The man in the middle is the anchor.

Waluigi has stolen from museums. Waluigi has rigged go-kart races. Waluigi has even scammed desperate Toads with useless corsets during a biological pandemic. But Waluigi has NEVER put a sentient being in a flesh vat to harvest their soul for a dimensional subway system. 

There is evil, and then there is *this*. The Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild must be dismantled. Not because Waluigi is a hero. But because Waluigi refuses to live in a universe where the ultimate authority is this utterly devoid of style and basic decency.

WAH.

summary: Waluigi is going to describe the Overgrown Manor Campaign as one continuous, exhausting, temporally incoherent experience because that is what it was. The dates do not make sense. The Feywild calendar jumped from Harvestide to Highsun and back again like a drunk hopping between bar stools, and Waluigi stopped trying to reconcile the timestamps after the third contradiction. What matters is the sequence of events and not the numbers attached to them, because the numbers are lying and the events are not. The campaign began when the Planar Fracture scattered Disaster Inc. across three hostile dimensions and deposited Waluigi, Hjumpik, Toad Lee, and eventually Wario into the Feywild reflection of Raventree Manor. It has not ended. It may never end, because the Feywild does not believe in endings the way civilized dimensions do. The Feywild believes in obligations, and obligations compound. Over the course of this campaign the party dealt with a people-eating shambling mound that the manor called a mascot, a mermaid-hag dispute over a transformed quartz skull, a ghost who remembered being killed by a three-eyed mage, a Revel entity made of mouths and limbs assembled from the bodies of deceased party guests, Wario attempting to bomb a giant dragonfly for treasure, two Rakshasas playing identity games, an Iron Legion sergeant whose entire squad was dead but who somehow was not, Lady Aurelian pretending to be too fragile to fight despite having draconic elemental resistances, Toad Lee getting swallowed by a bathtub plant monster, a hidden diary confirming the Iron Legion watched the Grafting ritual in 988 BF with approval, a five-night deadline that may have already passed depending on which leaf you count, and Waluigi being physically led between Toad Lee and Lady Aurelian like a child between two parents at a shopping center while a dryad commented that it reminded her of kindergarten. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Overgrown Manor Campaign as a single continuous record because splitting it into individual nights implies a kind of temporal coherence that the Feywild refuses to provide. The Feywild is not interested in nights as a unit of measurement. The Feywild measures time in obligations, performances, and the number of things you have accidentally agreed to.

## The Play, the Library, and the Rakshasa Who Was Acting Strange

The evening of the 24th Highsun began with Waluigi attending a play, because Waluigi is a person of culture trapped among people who think culture means hitting things with warhammers. The performance was held in the manor small theater alcove where sprites and goblins reenacted stories from the library collection on a stage barely fifteen feet wide, with a reading plinth at its center and stone riser benches on the outer edges for observers. Waluigi found it charming in the specific way that fairy theater is charming, which is to say beautiful on the surface and deeply unsettling if you think about it for more than thirty seconds.

Hjumpik found Waluigi in the theater and whispered with the subtlety of a man who has never successfully whispered in his life. Azure the Rakshasa, who had been watching the performance with genuine delight, became giddy afterward and tugged Hjumpik arm with strength that he could not resist, which is saying something because Hjumpik arms are attached to a dwarf who swings a warhammer for recreation. They ended up in the library, which was one of the most extraordinary rooms in the manor: a massive animated tree served as both librarian and architectural feature, its roots embedded into floors, walls, and bookcases, rearranging the layout at will while golden-red autumn leaves rustled overhead and strange colorful birds carried news between its branches. Small sprites tended dozens of hanging fruit-shaped books from its boughs while goblin servants ferried volumes back and forth below.

Waluigi grabbed a book to read. The entire shelf collapsed on him. A fairy named Prixie flew overhead and thanked Toad Lee for helping pick up the volumes, suggesting he speak to Woodfellow the tree-librarian. Toad Lee politely declined because Toad Lee has the rare survival instinct of not accepting favors from fairy entities in enchanted libraries, which is one of the more valuable instincts available in this dimension.

Azure walked off with purposeful energy that did not match her earlier performance-induced bliss. Toad Lee tried to stop her but could not match her strength. Hjumpik noted quietly that she was acting unusually powerful, and Waluigi agreed that something about her behavior had shifted since the play, as though the performance had activated or amplified something in her that was not purely recreational enthusiasm. This theory remained unconfirmed because nobody asked her directly and she did not volunteer the information.

## The Foyer, the Statue, and Waluigi Being Correct Again

The grand foyer of the Overgrown Manor was dominated by a massive tree growing from a stone planter barely large enough to contain its trunk, around which a stone statue of a toad with great feathered wings spread its arms protectively over the space. Gnarled roots crawled from the planter like fingers reaching for ankles, and the ceiling above was crisscrossed with ivy and flowering vines from the floor above, blooming with countless bright and strange flowers that Waluigi could not identify and did not trust. The walls were adorned with paintings and tapestries that had been partially consumed by the encroaching plant life, and the whole space smelled of deep forest and something older underneath.

Hjumpik launched himself over the roots with unnecessary acrobatic enthusiasm and then grabbed Toad Lee and flipped him across as well. Waluigi walked over them like a reasonable person and snapped a twig, which he considers an acceptable price for maintaining dignity. Hjumpik had a feeling the statue was connected to someone he had encountered before, something to do with the sleeping dragon from earlier in the campaign, though he could not articulate the connection clearly.

Waluigi sensed magic throughout the foyer, thick and omnipresent, but this was not school-based magic, not the clean arcane categories that the Mages Guild organizes into filing systems. This was natural magic, old and unbothered by classification. Toad Lee said it felt like a fairy tale. Hjumpik said the place was deeper than it appeared. Waluigi agreed with both assessments while filing away internally that neither of them had noticed the specific resonance pattern he had been tracking through the vine-covered walls since their first arrival, which was a different and more deliberate kind of presence than mere ambient enchantment.

## The Lord Chamber and the Lady with Questions

After exploring upward through collapsing ceilings and rotted hallways where the floors had partially given way to reveal steep drops to the library gangways below, the party reached the Lord Chamber, which had been transformed into a makeshift feasting hall and thoroughly trashed by its current occupants. A roaring fire pit dominated the center, spewing smoke and embers upward to blacken the high rafters with soot. Grimy hoof prints circled the pit in thick overlaying paths. Tables around the edge held half-finished meals and laid-out buffets of greens and nuts and fruits and breads and cheeses, while racks and full barrels of wine stood ready to fuel whatever the satyrs considered an appropriate evening.

The woman waiting for them pointed at the Entropy Regulator Ring on Hjumpik wrist and asked for it with the directness of someone who had decided social grace was optional. Hjumpik did not know what it was. She explained it made all things collapse to one, which is the kind of explanation that sounds profound until you realize it provides no actionable information. Hjumpik refused to hand it over on the reasonable grounds that they had just met and he did not give magical artifacts to strangers who pointed at his accessories. She asked if they were there to kill her. Hjumpik said maybe. She said not with that ring he was not. She reached for the ring and Hjumpik said he would not let someone touch a man on the first date, which combined genuine caution with accidental romantic framing in a way that only Hjumpik achieves.

She explained the satyr situation: a group had arrived expecting a few days stay and had instead taken over entirely. Her guards had been sent to address the problem and had come back hours later, drunk, now drinking buddies with half the satyrs. She wanted the party to evict them. She set a deadline of five nights to get the satyrs out and end the party, which Waluigi noted was the first firm commitment anyone in the Feywild had offered them.

A fireball formed in Waluigi hand during this conversation as he assessed the tactical calculus of whether their assigned mission was actually to kill this woman. He mentioned it to Toad Lee. Toad Lee said no. Waluigi says he was being thorough and not irresponsible, and he maintains this position.

Hjumpik laughed nervously and dragged both of them into a guest room before the situation could develop further.

## Saedia Three Quests and the Music Box That Never Stops

Saedia the dryad Seneschal presented three tasks in exchange for unaging Hjumpik deteriorated papers, doing so with the practiced exhaustion of someone who has been managing a household where half the staff are mythological and the other half are impaired. She rubbed her temple like someone soothing a headache that had become a permanent resident of her skull.

The first task concerned Herniva the mermaid and Stuckina the hag, who had been screaming at each other from opposite sides of a pond in the maze for over a day. Saedia had tried to mediate and failed. She described Herniva as kind with a mean streak and Stuckina as someone she would like to call a friend even if she was a bit off-putting, and concluded by comparing the two of them to harpies shrieking at each other, which is the most diplomatically honest thing Saedia said during the entire campaign.

The second task concerned Shambly, the shambling mound kept for waste disposal, whose keeper Tymnas had disappeared and who had since wandered indoors and begun eating staff. Saedia was emphatic about not killing it. The Revelmaster considered it a prized mascot, which is the most Feywild sentence in this encyclopedia because only in a fairy dimension is a people-eating plant monster considered an institutional treasure.

The third task involved clearing satyrs from the audience hall.

Hjumpik offered a dwarf promise. Saedia wound up a music box that played a melody which lodged itself in Waluigi head and has not left since. She said to come back anytime. The music box kept turning as they left. Waluigi believes it never stops. Waluigi has dreams about the music box. They are not pleasant dreams.

A dead goblin was found in the corridor immediately after, apparently killed while eavesdropping on the quest briefing. Aurelian checked the body and confirmed it dead. A satyr offered to carry it. Aurelian snapped her fingers. The satyr vanished. She snapped again. The body vanished. Three snaps, three disappearances, zero visible concern from anyone except Waluigi, who was the only person in the group who considered casual body disposal through finger-snapping to be worth noting.

## The Shambly Crisis Across Three Days

Toad Lee described Shambly from his previous encounter: green and almost beautiful when dormant, menacing dark purple when active, simultaneously gorgeous and disturbing in the way that dangerous things in the Feywild tend to be simultaneously gorgeous and disturbing. Hjumpik asked if it was friendly. Toad Lee said he did not know.

Toad Lee noticed Waluigi and Aurelian walking away toward a theatrical performance. Waluigi would like to clarify for the historical record that he was conducting intelligence gathering through cultural observation, which happened to involve comfortable seating and distance from a people-eating plant. Toad Lee grabbed Waluigi hand with the grip of someone who had already decided the answer. Aurelian grabbed Waluigi other hand simultaneously. They walked as a group with Waluigi being physically led between them like a child between two parents at a shopping center. Saedia observed from the doorway that it reminded her of kindergarten. Toad Lee told her she could fight him about it. She asked how long he wanted the deaging to take and he did not answer.

On the first approach to the creature room, Waluigi opted to sneak forward and peer through the door. He tripped on the carpet. Hjumpik caught him. Waluigi maintains this was the carpet fault. The carpet was ancient, bunched, and hostile. No reasonable court would rule against him.

The creature eventually ate a butler and grew stronger. It ate a guard who screamed for help while Toad Lee mentioned the digestion process was slow. It slammed a door into Waluigi, who deflected it with his tennis racket while shouting the word cheater because door-slamming as a combat technique is low-class and Waluigi will not pretend otherwise. Lady Aurelian cast what she called fairy magic, then the door opened and a bartender and guard charged past shouting about fresh meat.

Hjumpik argued for diplomacy throughout. He wanted to knock the creature out rather than kill it. Toad Lee wanted to kill it and cleanse the house. Waluigi proposed turning the entire room into a freezer and rolling the ice cubes including the creature and Toad Lee outside, then defrosting them later. Hjumpik rejected this. Waluigi then suggested an explosive icicle thrown at Toad Lee. Hjumpik convinced him to wait a few minutes before doing anything drastic.

Lady Aurelian told Toad Lee she was too fragile to fight, used the word suggest with magical emphasis, cast a spell, and walked out. Waluigi caught the emphasis. Toad Lee did not. Waluigi would like to note once again that Lady Aurelian Corvinarus, a woman with draconic bloodline heritage, vertical pupils behind illusions, and confirmed elemental resistances, called herself too fragile. She is not fragile. She is performing fragility because fragility gives her maximum control with minimum accountability. Toad Lee yelled at her to get out. She left looking genuinely hurt, which is either performance or evidence that dragon-blooded aristocrats can be wounded by toad-directed bluntness.

The resolution came from Steely the mechanical dog producing a steam-powered screech at escalating volume that the shambling mound found intolerable. Everyone evacuated: Toad Lee first, then Waluigi, then Aurelian, then the guard, then Steely, then Hjumpik, who told the creature he had not wanted this to happen but it had put up a fight. Shambly entered the grove and became its problem. The quest was technically complete. The butler it had eaten was technically dead. Waluigi considers this outcome asymmetric but acceptable.

## The Wario Encounters (Multiple, Consistent in Character)

Wario appeared throughout the campaign with the reliability of bad weather, each appearance following the same internal logic: everything has a price, everyone is a customer, and empathy is a sales technique that can be learned in classes.

The first encounter happened when the party found Wario surrounded by looted goods. He asked Waluigi immediately whether he had paid his debts. The multiverse is fracturing, reality is in pieces, they are trapped in a temporal pocket of a fairy dimension, and Wario opening question was about accounts receivable. Waluigi loves Wario. Waluigi also wants to strangle Wario. These feelings have coexisted for decades without resolution.

Wario revealed a portal in the back of the estate that could serve as an exit. He offered to sell the information for eight hundred gold. Hjumpik did not have eight hundred gold. Wario said this was horrible and that no information would be forthcoming. He then mentioned empathy classes, described Hjumpik as a very valued customer, and left to make rounds shadeward, which could mean dimensional commerce or theft from sleeping fairies or both.

The second encounter found Wario in Saedia room, looted treasures scattered everywhere, a gemstone being inserted into his pocket with the words ooh shiny as sole justification. Hjumpik dried papers were among the stolen goods. Wario offered to sell them back for ten gold. Hjumpik threatened to inform Aurelian about the theft. Wario reconsidered because it would be bad for business, returned the papers greasy and stained, and kept almost everything else.

Wario handed over a sealed vial of 268-year-old vampire wine from the Raventree cellars, noting he and his pals had gone drinking a few days ago and he had paid for the drinks. The label identified it as a vintage from 687 BF produced in vineyards that no longer exist from grapes cultivated by vampire lords who appreciated fine wine almost as much as fine blood. The bottle was hand-blown glass with intricate etchings and wax bearing the House Raventree crest. Wario had approximately eight bottles stolen from the manor cellars and had already sold three for 500 to 750 gold each to merchants who did not ask questions about provenance. He was considering raising his prices because he believed he was undervaluing rare vintage vampire wine. He was correct. He was also describing a product line built on theft from an interdimensional vampire estate during a planar crisis, which is the kind of business model that Wario considers simply responsive to market conditions.

Wario also handed over a garlic grenade, a portable healing machine, and an aerodynamic cannonball from his bag of holding, which required plunging his arm in to the shoulder while something inside growled faintly and the smell of garlic and old cheese emerged. He did not close the bag properly afterward because he would need it again in thirty seconds anyway.

The debt ledger revealed that Waluigi allegedly owes 14,783 gold in partnership expenses dating to 1015 BF at 15% monthly compound interest. Waluigi disputes this entire debt. Waluigi has never authorized 15% monthly interest on anything, particularly not garlic expenditures classified as operational necessities. Bowser owes 50,000 gold for storage fees that were generated when Wario stole half the treasure and is now charging Bowser to return the remainder. Remi owes 75 gold plus a 25 gold recruitment processing fee. The non-monetary favors section includes a vampire from Raventree who said he owed Wario one after Wario did not stake him, with the note COLLECT THIS written in urgent capitals. Wario treats this ledger as sacred scripture and has multiple backup copies in different safehouses.

## The Solarium Detonation

Wario attempted to assassinate the Bramblefly with a beautifully gift-wrapped time-bomb because the creature nest contained treasure, and for Wario, treasure justifies methodology. He dusted off his overalls, slipped on brass knuckles with the W letters catching the light, cracked his knuckles with the sound amplified significantly by the reinforcement, and charged in declaring he was there for the gold kind of lore while kicking humanoid bones aside. When the Bramblefly dive-bombed him with an Air Strike, Wario performed a perfect greasy combat roll and stuffed a golden candlestick into his pocket mid-dodge because Wario multitasks greed and violence simultaneously.

Hjumpik revealed himself from concealment and said not everything needed the Wario touch and they could figure it out without explosions. Wario picked his nose and said he did not care. Toad Lee suggested setting the room on fire instead, which Waluigi notes was the first time Toad Lee voluntarily proposed the arson solution.

Hjumpik threw a hand axe at the time-bomb present. The gift tumbled to the floor between Wario and the Bramblefly and kept ticking. Wario froze, eyes wide, and had time to say no no no before the detonation. The explosion blasted him backward through the already weakened Solarium floor. He plummeted screaming his trademark wail, landed in a pile of treasure downstairs, and immediately began scooping gold while bruised and smoking. Still worth it, he declared. The Bramblefly remained unharmed, proving that Feywild insects are constructed to a higher durability standard than Wario expects.

## The Ghost of Usk and the Grafting Vision

Hjumpik touched a statue on the mezzanine and connected with Usk, a fog-elf appearing as a faint twisted shape composed of shifting drifting clouds in perpetual motion as though moved by an unseen wind. His features were angular and tight, his expressions composed with strange quiet dignity accented by deep shadows.

Usk said he had died and was now here. He was uncertain whether here was past, present, or future. He remembered touching a statue and seeing a memory: a Corvinarus in orange robes cutting their own palm over a dragon egg. The egg screamed. The date was 988. The Iron Legion was there. They called it the Grafting.

Hjumpik asked how Usk had died. Someone had cut off his fingers and stabbed him. Not vampires. His own teammate. He described the killer: a mage in robes, purple robes, with three eyes, the third positioned above the other two. His hands were burnt. He had not seen him use magic directly. He began to say the killer name before Toad Lee pulled Hjumpik away from the statue at the same moment the Rakshasa intervened.

Toad Lee touched the statue afterward. Nothing happened. The statue responded only to Hjumpik specifically, which raises questions about what criteria the manor magical infrastructure uses to determine who receives visions and who receives silence. Hjumpik began explaining the Grafting connection to the group. Toad Lee and Waluigi walked away mid-explanation to ask whether Azure was powerful. This is how information-sharing functions inside Disaster Inc.: the person with critical intelligence delivers it to people who are already leaving the room.

The description Usk gave matched Archie Miser closely enough that Toad Lee noted it could be him but could also be clones. This distinction matters and nobody pursued it adequately. Waluigi filed it under ongoing concerns.

## The Vine Room, Hidden Passages, and Aurelian Chalk Circle

The vine storage room was filled with huge green and purple vines covered in razor-sharp thorns, actively guarding various objects and responding to approach with whip-like strikes before the decision to move was even fully formed. Toad Lee entered because he said he saw someone of interest inside. The vines grabbed him and would not let go despite Hjumpik and the others pushing and pulling. Aurelian emerged from a nearby room, explained she had locked that door so nobody would get hurt, and seemed genuinely puzzled about how Toad Lee had gotten in. Toad Lee eventually cleared the full room of vines with his axe and stumbled out on all fours.

The room defensive system accepted three names when Waluigi used magical detection: Corvinarus, Oracle, and Cornelius. This means the room security recognized three specific authority categories. Understanding who qualifies under each designation and how those categories interact with the manor broader architecture is essential intelligence that nobody acted on immediately.

Hidden passages riddled the upper floors. Steely pawed at a wall revealing one. Waluigi discovered a crack behind the thorny vines at the western landing, summoned magical light to illuminate a hidden room beyond, and Hjumpik used his warhammer to clear a path inside. They found the Morning Glory weapon within, a flower bud of densely packed petals that bloomed into a blade of milky gray steel when exposed to daylight.

Aurelian chalk circle in the master bedroom was discovered to be incomplete despite earlier implications that it was finished or near-finished. When confronted, she admitted she was starting now and estimated four days for completion, which placed the ritual finish on the night before the fifth-night satyr deadline. This timing was either coincidental or deliberately engineered. Wario shoulder-bashed through the door mid-conversation, tripped, fell, and smudged the chalk as Aurelian looked on. She was not pleased. Wario offered to sell her better chalk from his counterfeit supplies, producing a chalk box and presenting it with the energy of someone who does not understand they are at fault for the problem they are now proposing to solve for money.

## The Diary, the Bloodline, and the Grafting Confirmed

Toad Lee read aloud from a diary found in the master bedroom. Three entries painted a picture that Waluigi found troubling in ways that multiplied the longer he sat with them.

The first entry described Aurelian walking the halls crowned in living ivy, smiling as if the Revel never ended, but with tired eyes. The satyrs had arrived like locusts and drank the wine cellars dry. The writer told her to send them away. She laughed and said the party must continue until the planes align. Three manors, three lords, three threads, she whispered. Cut one and the tapestry unravels. The flower bed bloomed brighter each night and whispered to her while she slept.

The second entry described Usk ghost drifting through mirrors like smoke, speaking of betrayal and severed fingers and a blade in the dark and a three-eyed mage in purple robes. His anger was cold fire. The vines listened when he named the betrayer and tightened around them. The writer feared he would become part of the manor, another shadow caught in the weave.

The third entry was dated Faystyl 15, Year 722 of the Eternal Bloom, and described the Grafting in first-person observation. The egg screamed as the blade bit deep. It was described as a pure piercing note like winter wind through crystal. Orange robes stained crimson but the bond held. The Legion observers nodded approval, their iron hearts warmed briefly by the promise of control. The writer watched from the branches. The child would be strong, heir to both vine and scale. But something in the scream lingered, a hunger not yet named. The balance tipped toward entropy already.

Toad Lee called the entries background lore. Waluigi would like it on the record that dismissing evidence of blood-magic, draconic binding, Iron Legion involvement in supernatural experiments, and proto-entropic instability as background lore is exactly the kind of historical negligence that gets kingdoms destroyed. Hjumpik recognized the connection to his own statue vision and confirmed the Grafting was real based on personal memory.

A framed image beneath the rug showed Orangus Cornelius and a dragon on the day the bloodline split. Hjumpik asked Aurelian if the Corvinarus bloodline had merged with a dragon. She said eww and gestured to her fairy wings as evidence against the idea. Toad Lee asked if by dragon she meant the giant dragonfly upstairs. She said no, that was a pest she wanted removed. Hjumpik asked if she was not powerful enough to handle it herself. She said she was just a delicate fairy. Waluigi filed this under lies told by women with draconic blood and elemental resistances who prefer the diplomatic leverage of appearing vulnerable.

Under the rug in the master bedroom, rolled beneath the framed image, they found instructions for breaching Darius Planar Sanctum by repairing the damaged magic circle in the Ruined Manor. The ritual required bone, ash, chalk, and iron formed into a paste from powdered components. The process would take eight hours and could be reduced with the right proficiencies. One circle fragment was in the Feyward master bedroom. Another was in the Shadeward master bedroom. Both needed to be studied before the primary circle in the Ruined Manor could be repaired. This was the endgame mechanism. Everything else was preparation.

## The Revelmaster and the Revel Entity

Hjumpik eventually found the Revelmaster in the staff room adjoining the banquet hall, which was filthy and stinking with broken furniture and garbage strewn everywhere and a makeshift throne assembled from damaged furniture jumbled together like a nest. The Revel itself occupied the space: an amalgamation of mouths and limbs, a horrific avatar of gluttony and debauchery, an ephemeral red haze roiling in the air. Looking at it for more than a moment stirred a horrible unnatural hunger in the stomach and revealed a chaos of motion, hands grasping flesh and claws slitting throats and fanged mouths gnawing through their own sinew and crying out in ecstasy.

The Revelmaster operated under multiple names simultaneously: Ralos, Relis, Rellis, Pal, Friend, Leader. He forgot Hjumpik presence mid-conversation, wandered off to chug beer and vomit, then returned having forgotten who Hjumpik was entirely. He knew things he should not have known, singing a song about Hjumpik getting pulled through the vine-room door that was accurate in its specifics. He claimed to have been working on the song since it happened, implying either constant surveillance or some form of temporal awareness.

When asked why people were dying, he said they were drinking too much. When asked if that was bad, he said the Revel never ends so the party does not either. When asked about the bodies, he said they just put them in. This was the true horror of the Overgrown Manor: not a haunting, not a single monster, not a curse in the traditional sense, but a perpetual celebration that consumed its participants and incorporated their remains into itself as fuel. The Revel was self-sustaining through attrition.

The satyrs sang their feelings about the arrangement throughout the campaign:

Oh, have you seen them in the street, a hundred sets of iron feet, they clank-clank-clank in perfect time to prosecute some pointless crime, their backs are straight their faces sour they have not cracked a smile in an hour they eat their rations hard and dry and watch us with a judging eye, the Iron Legion got two left feet.

They also sang about the party itself:

We rolled into Raventree on a Tuesday maybe Thursday, the wine was already flowing and the grapes were getting hazy, the lady said one night only with a smile so very thin, but we satyrs know a party when the party is letting in. The revel never ends, the revel never ends, the glasses never empty and the night has got no friends, we dance until we are breathless we sing until we are hoarse, this party has got no finish it is the satyr only course.

They sang about Hjumpik and Toad Lee specifically:

Hjumpik, oh the dwarf with the hero stride, swinging that hammer like it is three sizes wide, Toad Lee, ax too tall, trip once more and you will dig your own crawl.

Waluigi is choosing not to document what they sang about him. It was accurate and he does not need it preserved.

## Sergeant Coldbrook, the Legion Reach, and the Invitation

Sergeant Varn Coldbrook of the Iron Legion appeared in a room containing dead bodies, alive and unharmed despite his entire squad being dead around him. He claimed the purple one had destroyed his unit. He described himself as being on a mission and offered a deal: eliminate the Revelmaster and earn the Iron Legion favor. He left without confirming which faction he belonged to, though his phrasing and equipment suggested Legion origin.

Eager noticed he was unharmed and said nothing. Waluigi noticed Eager noticing and said nothing. Nobody said anything, which is sometimes how the most important observations are made in Disaster Inc.: silently, privately, filed away for later.

Waluigi explained afterward that the sergeant had sent guards after him, and Waluigi had used a fireball to destroy all of them, then looted the bodies. He gave Hjumpik a flask labeled Satyr Regret. He gave Toad Lee a sealed envelope. The envelope contained an invitation printed on human skin vellum inviting the holder to the Orange Heir Banquet. The ink smelled of rot. The text read: The Rot is Ripe. The Time is Nigh. Come feed.

Waluigi used the invitation to pick his teeth and then took it back.

The satyrs offered Hjumpik food that he identified on examination as a naturally occurring poison, an alcoholic substance so powerful it would kill on consumption. The satyrs knew about the party plans in detail, singing about them mid-conversation. Information traveled through the Revel network with no apparent delay, which meant privacy within the Overgrown Manor was maintained only by the other parties choosing not to act on what they knew.

## Dyanos, the Gallery of Three, and the Bathtub Monster

Toad Lee, separated from the group after mushroom spores temporarily removed his sense of having a face, encountered Dyanos, a guard who served Chirneros, Lord-champion of Fey, with fifteen years of service. Dyanos introduced Toad Lee to a personal gallery bathed in warm light with gauzy curtains, cases of strange and wonderful items along every wall, and a towering mirror along the southeast wall that reflected the room at night despite it being daytime, so convincingly that the mirror seemed to drink the surrounding light into itself.

Three miniature statues stood in one section: green, red, and blue. Dyanos explained their meanings. Green represented Survival, Adaptation, the Ones Who Endure. Red represented Violence, Consequence, Irreversibility. Blue represented Control, Cold, Memory. These were ancient, predating the Revel and possibly predating the manor itself.

Dyanos asked Toad Lee what he thought they represented. Toad Lee guessed seasons. Dyanos said no. He then handed Toad Lee a purple crystal frog, noting that it was interesting how a toad gravitated toward crystal frogs. Toad Lee said in a way yeah with the understated acceptance of someone receiving a compliment that is also a category observation.

They entered the bathhouse together for what was supposed to be a restorative rest, removed their armor, put on robes, and discussed the nature of the Doughnut World while the waterfall fountain filled the room with flowing water sounds and colorful plants overflowed from corner planters. Then a massive plant arm emerged from a pile of leaves, the rest of the body following until the abomination of plant matter stood fully upright with dangerous-looking talons, and tackled Toad Lee directly into its stomach.

Dyanos stabbed it with his weapon. Toad Lee tried to damage it from the inside and missed. The guard ran out to get help. Toad Lee burst out of the creature and flew across the room, then evacuated the gallery and found Dyanos outside asking what should they do. Toad Lee said he was beaten up and could not kill that thing. He cried. Then he heard an explosion south of the manor and decided to get a drink instead. They went to the bar, where someone had bought everything, all the beer paid for by an unidentified patron. Toad Lee rested. He did not ask who had bought the drinks and Waluigi thinks this was wise.

## Azure Warning, the Midnight Gate, and the Recurring Collapse

Azure the Rakshasa delivered the most significant intelligence of the campaign in fragments scattered across multiple appearances. She said she had seen many planes fall and collapse and had come to see it again. She almost mentioned the Regal Empire before stopping herself. She confirmed the BF calendar marked a previous collapse cycle, implying the current dimensional crisis was not unprecedented but cyclical. She gave three escape options: the Oracle portal plan requiring chalk and circle repair, the Midnight Gate that could be activated independently without the Oracle, or killing mostly everyone except the orange heir.

She immediately regretted mentioning the Midnight Gate and clarified she had not told them its location so it was probably fine that she had disclosed its existence. She said she would go make arrangements. A second Rakshasa appeared moments later, greeting Hjumpik cheerfully and offering him a flower. This was a different Rakshasa than Azure. Hjumpik had been tricked. The first had extracted information by appearing trustworthy while the second confirmed the deception by appearing friendly immediately after.

The Midnight Gate activated briefly when the second Rakshasa entered it and vanished. The portal deactivated. An escape route was discovered and lost inside a single conversation.

Perrius Annmatar spoke directly into Hjumpik mind with a warning: the timelines must not be severed or the plan would collapse. The heir must be killed unless an illegitimate heir could be found. There needed to be an odd number of Oracles because even was balanced and odd was irregular. If only one Oracle remained, probability would become 100% and the outcome would be fixed. Hjumpik gave the ghost a thumbs up, which is the most Hjumpik possible response to receiving existential cosmic intelligence through telepathy while standing in a fairy manor hallway.

## The Ritual Materials and the State of the Deadline

The current ritual materials checklist: chalk acquired from Wario counterfeit supplies, bone still needed and potentially available from satyr remains or fallen enemies, iron potentially available from Wario cannonball though that cannonball keeps getting lost, ash obtainable from burned furniture. The circle construction in the master bedroom is underway but will take four days, finishing precisely on the night before the five-night satyr eviction deadline.

This timing is either coincidental or deliberate. Waluigi does not believe in coincidence when dealing with Corvinarus family members who quote the three threads prophecy while building portals and managing party evictions simultaneously.

The five-night deadline itself may be a flexible construct. The Feywild measures time in obligations rather than sundowns, and the manor calendar has been demonstrably unreliable. Five nights may mean five sequential sundowns, five metaphorical thresholds, or five iterations of whatever event pattern Aurelian is using as her reference. What is clear is that consequences will follow its expiration, and those consequences involve at minimum the Iron Legion presence, the Revelmaster entity, the satyrs relationship with the Revel, and whatever Aurelian ritual is actually constructing in the master bedroom.

Waluigi does not fully trust Aurelian. Waluigi does not fully distrust Aurelian. She is doing something real with that chalk circle and she has agreed to send back more than just three members of the party if conditions are met, which suggests negotiating room exists. But the woman who snaps bodies into nonexistence and claims to be too fragile to fight while having draconic elemental resistances is not operating transparently, and transparent is the minimum Waluigi requires before extending genuine trust to anyone.

The Revelmaster must be dealt with. The ritual materials must be gathered. The satyrs must be evicted or relocated. The Legion presence must be monitored. Azure must be located again because her drunk flirting and dramatically convenient timing suggest she knows more than she is sharing and is choosing her moments carefully.

Waluigi has survived giant spiders, vampire dinner parties, dimensional fractures, a door slamming into him during a plant monster fight, and being led between two people by both hands simultaneously while a dryad compared the scene to kindergarten. Waluigi will survive five nights in a fairy manor with singing satyrs, a body-consuming Revel entity, a dragon-blooded aristocrat performing fragility, and a music box that never stops turning.

Probably.

WAH.

summary: After witnessing the horrors of the Planar Sanctum, Archie Miser demanded the Oracle immediately perform a ritual to send him to 'Shadeward' (The Shadowfell) to rescue his friends. The Oracle warned him that time moves differently there—a MONTH has passed in the Shadowfell since they last saw each other. Archie, refusing to listen to reason, demanded the ritual proceed. He left the comatose Bones in the Oracle's care (with strict instructions not to put him in a flesh vat). Archie stood in the center of the candles to act as the magical anchor. The Oracle noted that Archie was absorbing TOO MUCH power. The session ended right before the inevitable explosion. Waluigi is taking bets on how many limbs Archie retains upon arrival.
description:
Waluigi must document the sheer, unrelenting stubbornness of Archie Miser. 

Archie had just been informed that his magic bleeds entropy. He had just been shown that dimensional travel requires immense, agonizing power. He had just watched a man being ripped apart by crystal tethers. 

His response? 'Enough dilly-dallying. Let's do the ritual.'

## The Time Dilation Problem

The Oracle revealed a critical piece of intelligence: Time is not synchronized across the planar fragments. 

While only a few days have passed in the Material Plane (Raventree Manor), the Oracle explicitly stated that **A MONTH has passed in the Shadowfell**. 

This is disastrous. Waluigi has been trapped in the Feywild; he does not know what the time dilation is there, but if the Shadowfell is moving at a highly accelerated rate, the geopolitical situation has entirely changed. 

If a month has passed in the Shadowfell:
- Vivian Corvinarus has had 30 days to consolidate power or be hunted down.
- Green T has been surviving in a hostile, monochrome death-world for weeks.
- The Onyx Hand has had a month to recover from the Shattering of the Anchor and the shooting of Orangus Cornelius.
- Any rescue operation is arriving long after the trail has gone cold.

Archie didn't care. 'I still have to try. We haven't left a foot outside the mansion.'

## The Custody of Bones

Archie made one semi-responsible decision: he refused to take the comatose Bones through a volatile dimensional portal. He ordered the Oracle to watch over Bones, specifically demanding that the Oracle not subject Bones to his 'experiments.'

The Oracle agreed, stating it was 'quite a burden.' 

Waluigi finds this arrangement deeply concerning. Leaving an unconscious friend with a 46-year-old (in Toad years) interdimensional custodian who just showed you his secret room full of flesh vats is not a solid long-term healthcare plan. However, compared to taking Bones into a dimensional blender, it was the lesser of two evils.

## The Anchor's Overload

The Oracle instructed Archie to stand in the middle of the ritual circle. Archie was designated as the 'Anchor.' 

Waluigi has seen Archie act as an anchor before. It caused the Planar Fracture. 

As the candles were lit, Archie began to absorb magical power to fuel the transit. The Oracle, a being who routinely manipulates space and time, looked at Archie wide-eyed and said, *'It may be too powerful.'*

Archie's response: *'Well, you'll be in Shadeward. Where in Shadeward? I haven't got a clue.'*

And that is where the record ends.

## Waluigi's Assessment

Archie Miser is about to be fired out of a metaphysical cannon into a dimension that hates him, arriving a month late to a rescue mission, carrying enough volatile magical energy to potentially shatter whatever remains of the Shadow Estate.

Waluigi is not a praying man, but Waluigi is praying for the structural integrity of the Shadowfell. Because when Archie Miser absorbs 'too much power,' things don't just break. They cease to have ever existed.

WAH.

summary: Fawful—the mad tactician who somehow convinced five dragons to follow him—hosted a diplomatic gala that brought together representatives from nearly every significant faction in the region. The guest list read like a 'who's who' of people who want each other dead: Loyalist operatives, Regency diplomats, Rakasha chiefs, Iron Legion observers, independent power brokers, and apparently several individuals whose faction affiliations remain unclear. What happened at this gala has reshaped Waluigi's understanding of the assassination conspiracy, the current crisis, and the relationship between them. Chief Thornpaw confirmed his relationship with Princess Peach. Mistveil extracted intelligence that validated decades of Loyalist theories. Fawful demonstrated capabilities that terrify everyone who wasn't already terrified of him. And Waluigi was NOT INVITED. Waluigi finds this personally offensive.
