description:
Waluigi is going to document this event in full because it represents a new category of catastrophe — not dimensional collapse, not architectural malice, not ritual failure — but the specific horror of watching a party member get turned into ART and then SOLD.

## The Medusa (Who Nobody Thought to Mention Was There)

Raventree Manor has a Medusa. This information was not in any briefing Waluigi received. Nobody said 'by the way, there is a creature living in this building whose PRIMARY ABILITY is turning people to stone.' Nobody left a NOTE. The warnings Waluigi found previously said 'don't clean the mirrors.' They did NOT say 'don't make eye contact with the resident Gorgon.' Waluigi considers this a significant gap in the available documentation.

The Medusa — a person, technically, a being with a face and clothing and apparently a SCHEDULE — turned Remi to stone with a glare. One glare. That was all it took. Remi made eye contact, the Medusa said something approximately translatable as 'smile,' and Remi became a statue. Remi, who has survived things that would have broken seasoned adventurers, who has walked through chaos with a cheerfulness that Waluigi finds simultaneously admirable and EXHAUSTING, was reduced to decorative stonework in SECONDS.

Then the Medusa put on a paper bag. Over her face. As if this were a reasonable and normal thing to do. And she walked into another room. Waluigi watched this happen. Waluigi has no explanation for the paper bag. Waluigi has filed the paper bag under 'things about this building that will haunt him' alongside the mirror warnings and the servant uniforms with no servants inside them.

## The Library Discovery (Where the Imps Were)

Before the auction could be located, the party needed to navigate the library. The library contained imps — flying, scribing creatures who wrote down everything the party said and did, instantly and in real time. Every statement. Every expression of confusion. Every muttered complaint. Documented.

Waluigi finds the imps philosophically interesting and practically INFURIATING. On one hand, Waluigi APPRECIATES thorough documentation. Waluigi IS thorough documentation. Waluigi understands the value of a complete record. On the other hand, the imps were documenting for the ARCHIVIST — a vampire, presumably, who sat behind a one-way mirror and watched visitors with academic detachment — and their documentation was being used against the party in real time.

Markop also noticed a statue of Vivesna in the library. Vivesna, who Markop killed. Standing there as if to say: 'Hello. Did you think there would be no record?' The manor keeps records of EVERYTHING. Every death. Every deed. Every person turned to stone and auctioned.

## The Archivist (One-Way Mirror, Infinite Condescension)

The Archivist's room was locked. Eager attempted to pick the lock. The window swung open and the Archivist informed them — with what Waluigi can only describe as vampire SMUG — that one cannot see vampires in mirrors because mirrors don't show them. One-way glass. Eager fell to the floor.

The Archivist then handed the party a poster. An OFFICIAL POSTER. Printed and distributed. It read: 'Official Art Display feat. Archie Miser' — with an image of Remi, turned to stone, presented as an art piece titled after ARCHIE, who WAS NOT EVEN THERE.

Waluigi needs to pause and register his objections. Remi was turned to stone. Remi was classified as an art piece. The art piece was named after Archie, who had nothing to do with this situation, simply because Archie's name apparently means something in this building's social hierarchy. Remi, who was ACTUALLY THERE and is a REAL PERSON, was reduced to supporting cast in her own petrification. Waluigi finds this offensive on multiple levels and intends to remember it.

## The Auction (Twelve Thousand Gold)

The auction room was accessed through a window that Markop used as an observation point before the situation required direct intervention. Through the window, the party watched a bidding war in progress. Remi — Remi, who Waluigi has watched dodge danger with the cheerfulness of someone who doesn't fully process that danger is dangerous — stood at the front of the room as stone. Inert. Sold.

Purple T won. Twelve thousand gold. The winning bidder — who would later identify himself as Mystic Morsole — stood up and with an authority that suggested he did this regularly, freed Remi from her stone state. Then announced that she 'belonged to him.'

Waluigi has strong feelings about the phrase 'she belongs to me' and those feelings can be summarized as: NO. Waluigi does not care what was bid. Waluigi does not care what auction rules say. People are not PROPERTY and the Raventree auction house — which is apparently a THING that EXISTS — can take its entire operating structure and throw it into the ocean.

## The Room Erupts (Bowser's Finest Moment)

Markop broke the window. This was the correct response. Waluigi endorses window-breaking as a valid tactical option when the alternative is watching a party member get claimed as a purchased item.

The chaos that followed was, in Waluigi's assessment, textbook Disaster Inc. Wario appeared — from WHERE, Waluigi does not know, Wario simply APPEARS in chaotic situations like a bad omen in mustache form — and shoulder-barged Markop to the floor. A mages guild operative materialized and claimed Remi for THEMSELVES. Bowser pulled out a device to call his son for backup, which is either terrifying or comforting depending on how you feel about Koopa reinforcements. Markop summoned a moonbeam. Mystic Morsole jumped out a window.

Salam started picking flowers. Waluigi does not have context for this. Waluigi has CHOSEN not to pursue context for this.

Remi ran out and jumped into Dan's arms. The auction was over.

## The Aftermath (Mystic Morsole, Persistent Problem)

Remi was free. Remi was also standing next to Mystic Morsole, who had jumped out the window and apparently landed directly into the aftermath of the situation he caused, which Waluigi considers AUDACIOUS.

Mystic Morsole — Purple T, winning bidder, self-described owner of a person — explained himself with what the toads assessed as a LIE. He then offered tea. He offered incense. He insisted on following Remi 'to keep his end of the deal,' a deal that Remi had no memory of making, which is the most concerning detail of an extremely concerning afternoon.

A deal. With someone Remi doesn't remember. For a price she can't recall. Mystic Morsole insists it exists. Remi cannot confirm or deny it. Waluigi has placed Mystic Morsole in the category of 'problems that are currently walking around behind the party and have not been resolved.' That category is unfortunately crowded.

Wario also reappeared with a debt list the length of the mansion. Bowser owes him money. The list was long enough to cross a single item off and still remain longer than most legal documents Waluigi has encountered. Wario claimed the bomb he once gave Remi in a box was 'incidental.' Waluigi does not believe anything involving Wario is incidental. Wario is the OPPOSITE of incidental. Wario is purpose made.
